cells.remarks: The date is wrong. But Kuli 4031 curiously enough corresponds to the cyclic year Sarvadharin. This is evidently another forgery of the type of No. 1 of Appendix A to the Annual Report for 1909 and No. 6 of Appendix A to the Annual Report for 1910. See above part 1, paragraph 15.

prathanna, Mounday.

di. trayōdaśi, Monday.
cells.remarks: Similar to No. 12 of Appendix A to the Annual Report for 1906. The inscription is evidently a forgery. The name of the village granted is not clear, three to four lines at this place being written on erasure. See below Part II, paragraph 7.

cells.king: Śaribha-Choḍadēva of the Koḍa family, residing at Nellūrapuṭi.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Registers the gift of the village Kuṇeduru on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadra by the king on the occasion of the installation of his two sons, Yuvarāja Vikramāditya-Kumāravinaya and Tānu-Choḍa and Shanmukha-Choḍa as yuvarājas. The village was divided into four shares two of which were given to the gods Agastyēśvara and Mahādēva and Kumārasvāmin at Tānu-maṇḍala. The third share was given to his own purōhit and the fourth to the worshippers, servants, &c., of the two temples.

cells.date:
Śaka 1478, Nala, Srāvana, ba. di.
ashṭami, jayunti.
Thursday.
cells.remarks: These are the missing third and fourth plates of No. 24 of Appendix A, to the Annual Report for 1917 with which the grant is complete. Registers the grant, with all the incomes, of the village Marripūndi surnamed Raghunāthapurum situated in the Valanādu division of the Kondavidu-sīma to the great schoolar and astronomer Sarva-Bhatṭa, who belonged to the Yaska-gōtra and Apastambasūtra and was a Yajurvēdin. He was the son of Kondu-Bhatṭa and grandson of Sarva-Bhatṭa and was a resident of the village Penumpnali as also a devotee of the god Gōkaraṇadēva. The gift was made on the reprosentation of the king's minister Ramaraja.

Registers the tax-free gift of the village Ardiha in the Vaudēvakhōja-vishaya by the king to Brāhmaṇas, some of whom were of the Vājasanēya-charaṇa and Kāṇva-śākhā while the others were of the Vatsa-gōtra. The king was the son of Śatrubhañjadēva, the grandson of Śatrubhañjadēva and the great-grandson of Śilābhañjadēva.

States that the king granted, tax-free, the village Mula-Machhida in the Machhida-khaṇḍa-vishaya to a Brāhmaṇ named Bhaṭṭa-Parāśara, a son of Dēvaśarman, the grandson of Hariśarman of the Vājasanēya-charaṇa and the Kachhita-gōtra. The king was the son of Śilābhañjadēva, grandson of Dīghabhañjadēva and the great-grandson of Raghabhañjadēva.

Records the tax-free gift of the village Machhida in the Machhida-khaṇḍa-vishaya by the king to Bhaṭṭa-Dēvaśarman, the son of Kēśava and the grandson of Chharu, both of the Vājasanēya-charaṇa and of the Vatsa-gōtra. The king's ancestry is the same as in No. 6 above.

Registers the grant of some land in the village Amārāṅga of the Jalamōra-vishaya by the king to Śvāmśarman, son of Bhaṭṭaputra, of the Vājasanēya (i.e., Vājasanēya) charaṇa, Kāṇva-śākhā, Kauśika-gōtra and Jāmadagnya-gōtra. The king is said to be the son of the lord of Kaliṅga, and Śvētakadīśadhāna is mentioned.

Records the grant of the village Kōmyana in the Vōda-vishaya with all its income to the Dīkshita Jagadharaśarman, of the village Padhuvādapāku in the Kōntavēṅga-vishaya. The donee belonged to the Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Mādhyandina-śākhā and was a student of the Yajur-vēda. He was well-versed in the Śrauta and Smārta rites and was strong in astronomy (jyōtiḥ-śāstra). The grant was made on the uchchāyana-ēkādaśī day in the bright half of the Kārtika month when Vishnu is believed to wake up from his four-months' sleep.

States that the king granted to the village Komboru lying one gavunda to the south of the village Vlonturu in the Kamboru-j-vithi-vishaya, to a scholar of the Vedas and the Sastras named Somasarma, who was the son of Svāmisarman and grandson of Damodara of the lost clan (gotra) of Gārgya-gōtra and a master of the four Sastras.

Registers the gift of the village Madhipatharakhanda [in] the Mahēndra-bhōga to a certain Ujanaka by Rānaka Sri-I-Bhamakhēdi, son of Mahamaṇdalēsvara Rānaka Sri-Bhamaktēdi of the Kadamva (i.e., Kudamba) family, the lord of five vishayas (pañchavishayadhipati). The order of gift is addressed to the officials and people of the Pañchapatra-vishaya.

The plates are so very faintly engraved in characters of about the 9th century that it is almost impossible to read them. Register the grant of the village 'lamvaddi in [Sala ..]-vishaya. The donee's name is not clear. The grant was issued from Kaliṅganagara.

cells.date: Śaka 814 manuvasu, Moshu, Chaitra, badi dvitiya, Monday, Maitra, Mithuna.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a land growing 1,000 neca-nut trees, another land sowable with 50 khandikas of paddy-seed and a house-site in the village Attili in the Attili-vishaya, to the songstress Challava who was the daughter of Mallapa, the son of Thundaka who was no less than an upsaras in beauty.

Much mutilated and incomplete. One or two plates missing. The order of the gift made to a Brahman (name lost) of the Bhāradvaja-gōtra is addressed to the officials of the Vapanāndu (i.e., Velanāndu)-vishaya.

cells.king: Umārāja of the Sōda ritu and the Bhārata gotra.
cells.date: Śaka 1304, Dunmuki, Māgha, su. di. dasami, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land at Undikapuram, to a number of Brahmans as agrahāra. It also records the names of a dozen other villages similarly granted by him to Brah-mans; the king's capital is mentioned to be Saravasiddhi.

The same as the last, except by three indivi-duals of the village Palupalarti to two other individuals waiving permanently the right of collecting certain taxes payable to them, for the consideration of 50 gadyāṇakalu received as the commutation amount.

Durmati, Vaisakha, su. di tritiya.
cells.remarks: States that, while Lingōji-Pandita was governing the Karnaṭaka kingdom from Penugonda-paṭṭana as a subordinate of Akhanna-Pandita, the younger brother of Madanna-Pandita who was the best of Brahmans and the chief officer of the king of Bhagnager, Nañjappa of the Kāmakāyana-Viśvāmitra-gōtra, Āśvalayana-sūtra and Rik-sakha who was the sthala-karṇam of Lepakshi in the Roddhanaṭi-sthala in Penugonda-rājya gave some land in that village to Kumārayya of the Bharadvaja-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajuś-śakha, who was the aradhya at Lepakshi. It registers also the gift of rates on pack-bullocks, shops, looms and marriages to the same Kumārayya by the samayins of Ayyavaji, etc., the Vaiśyae of the 102 gōtras, the representatives of maṭhas the Yajamanas of the Lepakshi-sthala, etc., assembled in the temple mandapa of that place for daily offerings and lamps to the god Nañjundēśvara.

cells.date:
Śaka 1415, Bahudhanya (wrong), Karttika, su. di.
Paurnima, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: States that a certain Pedda Aholalēndri who was a divan under Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kṛishṇadēvarāya who was ruling at Peṇugonda, gave some land to Aholalam at Peṇu-Lakshmi Nrisimhasvāmin at -omaghaṭṭa in accordance with the direction given to him by the deity at Ahōbalam in a dream. Registers the gift of the village Kūṇṭalla-palle in the Gōraṇṭla-samutu by the king for offerings and some gold for lamps to the god and for certain contributions by the temple of Śrī-Nṛisiṁha.

The record is incomplete, only the first 3 plates of the set remaining. It stops with the partial description of the qualities of king Sriraṅga, the son of Pedda Venkaṭapati who was the second son of Sriraṅga, the son of the great Rāmaraja who was the minister of Sadaśiva. Sec the genealogical table, Epigraphia Indica Vol. III, page 238. The king is stated to have been crowned by Tatayarya.

The Saka date falls into the reign of Virupaksha I predecessor of Bukka II. Registers in detail the incomes that the guarding officers (kaval-doregalu) of Madakaira were to get from the several classes of people, residing in the village. Also specifies the incomes that the ayagaras (i.e., the village servants) of certain villages were to get after the king's share was deducted.

cells.date: Saka 1687, Kali 4866, Parthiva, Tai, 4, Friday, śu. di. pañchami, Uttarm (Uttaru-Phalguni), Auṭitayōga, Balava-ka-ruṇa.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of land at Kavulpatti, hamlet of Palanivadam made by the king for certain services and charities to be conducted at the time of the festivals of the god Bala-Subrahmanya on the Palani-hill on the bank of the Shanmukhanadi in the Vaigavur-nāḍu. The grant was executed in favour of Subrahmanya-Udaiyar, son of Palniyola Mudaliyar, of the Karkatta-gōtra and Pālani-kēhetra. A certain Palni Venkatarayyar was given land and entrusted with the charity. The coin Rājagōpāli is mentioned.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for lamps to the temple of Ādittēśvaramuḍaiyār-Paramēśvaran at Tirumaraiyūr nāḍu by Namban-Diran a resident of Iyangudi in Ingaṇa-nāḍu. Mentions the measure called Mapalavan, the village Viḍēlviḍugu-Tuṟkachchōḻi-chaturvēdimangalam a brāhmaḍēya in the said nāḍu and refers to the 7th year of the reign of Parakēsarivarman.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Built at the beginning. Records a sale of land to the temple at Karur by a native of Sāttānguḍi in Tirumaraiyūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Kshatriyaśikhāmaṇi-vaḷanāḍu. Refers to the shrine of the goddess, Tiruppaḍiyār-Nambirāṭṭiyār.

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 18th „ [date-calculation appendix, No. 283: 7th year, Mēsha, śu. di. 13, Wednesday, Uttiram. According to note to No. 871, Kielhorn's South-Indian Inscriptions (App. to Vol. VII, Ep. Ind.), the 17th year of his reign coincided with Ś. 1261 = A.D. 1339-40; and May 1323 must have fallen in its 1st year. Reckoning by these indications, Wednesday, April 12, A.D. 1329 when the equivalent of the present date Wednesday, April 12, A.D. 1329 when śu. 13 ended at ·54; but it was a day of "Hasta", Nak. "Uttiram" having ended at ·61 on the previous day.]
cells.remarks: -Built in at the beginning. Registers a gift of land by a private individual for worship in the shrine of the goddess, Tiruppa||iyarai-Nambirattiyar.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.date: 49th „ [date-calculation appendix, No. 284: Chālukya Vikrama year 53, Plavaṅga, Āshāḍha, Amāvāsyā, Sunday, Dakshiṇāyana-Saṅkramaṇa, Vyatipāta. In A.D. 1127, on Sunday, 10th July, Āshāḍha Amāvāsyā began at ·27 of day and ended at ·29 on the following day.]
cells.remarks: Fragments. Much damaged.

cells.place: On the west wall of Amṛtavanēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Ādittēśvaramuḍaiyār at Karur in Tirumaraiyūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Kshatriyaśikhāmaṇi-vaḷanāḍu. Refers to a revenue survey of land.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Relates to the gift of land for 3 lamps by the same individual mentioned in No. 281 above and refers to gifts of land made in the 7th, 8th and 9th years of king Parakesarivarman.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: 2nd „ [date-calculation appendix, No. 287: Chālukya Vikrama year 48, Subhakrit, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti. In A.D. 1128 (= Subhakrit), Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti fell on December 25, Tuesday.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase for offerings and worship to the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Damaged [date-calculation appendix, No. 288: Śaka 1193, Dhanus, śu. di. 1, Friday, Mūlam. =A.D. 1271, December 4, Friday ; 93 ; 44.]
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to register a gift of land to Kulōttuṅgaśōḷapperumpaḷḷi at Kūrūr alias Kulōttuṅgaśōḷanallūr in Tirunaraiyūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Kulōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, and the dēvadāna of Tiruveḷḷerukkīśvaramuḍaiyār, and Tirumambaḷamuḍaiyār.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Provides for offerings to the temple of Āditta-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Paramasvāmin at Kūrūr in Tirunaraiyūr-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple. The donor was Rājarāja-Pallavaraiyan of Kuvaḷālam one of the Perundaram of the king.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 26 kasu for a lamp to the temple of Adittavlśvaramudaiya-Bhatṭarakar at Kūrūr in Tirunaraiyūr-nādu, by a certain Astraśiva.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a flower-garden. Mentions Muḍigoṇḍaśōḷapperāṟu and Karikālaśōḷa-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Mahādēva.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of money for lamps to the temple of Tirumambaḷamuḍaiyār at Kūrūr by three ladies one of whom was the wife of Vayiri Kuṭṭeran alias Śōḷavijjādira [Pallavaraiyan] one of the officers of the Perundaram of king Rājarājadēva.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: [9]th ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 295: Vikrama, Vṛśchika, śu. di. 14, Friday, Aśvati. (About 14th century.) In A.D. 1340 (= Vikrama) on November 3, Friday, the tithi śu. 14 was current the whole of that day and nak. Aśvati ended at 13.]
cells.remarks: Refers to a gift of land in exchange for lands already given for festivals to the temple of Āditta-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Bhaṭṭāraka. Mentions the channel called Kalidiran-vāykkāl.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Registers a sale of land by the assembly of Tirupperundurai which was a brahmadēya in Tirunaraiyūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Kshatriyaśikhāmaṇi-vaḷanāḍu to the temple of [Ādityēśvaram]-uḍaiya-Mahādēva at Kūrūr. Refers to a revenue survey.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of a land by purchase to the temple of Tirumambaḷamuḍaiya-Mahādēva for feeding a certain number of persons during Sunday festivals.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: States that this stone temple was built by Maḍamuḍaiyār-Varaguṇa-to[ṇḍar] whose figure is sculptured above the inscription.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: [10]th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 299: 4th year, Makara, śu. di, 5, [Monday, Rēvati]. = A.D. 1257, January 22, Monday; '42; '53.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Gift of land and a house-site to the temple of Āditta-Īśvaramuḍaiya-Bhaṭṭāraka for conducting the festival called Śittirai-tiruviḻā in the shrine of Nambi-Ārūran.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: 23rd ,, [date-calculation appendix, No. 300: 32nd year, Mēsha, śu. di. 1, Sunday, Mūla. Irregular.]
cells.remarks: Incomplete. States that certain land granted to the temple was made tax-free.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end and damaged.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: 15th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 302: Śaka 1461, Vikāri, Bhādrapada, śu. di. 12. Details not enough for verification for want of week-day.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Gift of land, by purchase, for a lamp to the temple of Aditta-jīśvaramuḍaiyār by the wife of Vīraśikhāmaṇi-Pallavarayar. Mentions the brahmadeya village Vīḍalviḍungu Inkkachchōḷurvēdiman-galam.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Built in the end. Registers a gift of land by purchase by Madurāntakadēvar, for feeding the persons who atten-ded the nine-days' festival in the temple of Aditya-Iśvara-muḍaiyār at the place.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: Lost [date-calculation appendix, No. 304: Śaka 1461, Vikāri, Bhādrapada, śu. di. 13. Details not enough for verification for want of week-day.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers a gift of land, by Vāvirukūttan alias Sūḷavaḍi-Iḷaṅkōvēḷār, for offerings to be constructed by him in this village which is stated to be situated in Tirumaiyūr-nāḍu a sub-division of Muḍikoṇḍachōḷa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end unit damaged. Gift of money for a lamp.

cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1436, [Bha]va, Tula, śu. di. Utthanadva-[daśi]. [date-calculation appendix, No. 306: Śaka 1461, Vikāri, Bhādrapada, śu. di. 12. Details not enough for verification for want of week-day.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Mentions Maṇḍalamaiya-Nāyiṇār.

cells.place: On the north wall of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.language: 27th year, Makara, ba. di. Monday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Stones missing and out of order. Seems to register a gift of a house for a monastery (guḍai).

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.language: 27th year, Makara, ba. di. Monday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of land for a lamp to the temple of Tirumaiyūruḍaiyār at Kūrur by certain residents of Pēraiyūr alias Sūḷakēraḷanallūr in Tirumaiyūr-nāḍu a sub-division of Kuḷōttuṅga-chōḷa-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.language: 27th year, Makara, ba. di. Monday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Records that Madurāntaka-Śōṇan alias Virudarāja-bhayaṅkara-Vayantāṇḍavan of Pañjūrnūr in Tirumaiyūr-nāḍu a sub-division of Kuḷōttuṅga-chōḷa-vaḷanāḍu sold lands in Arumolidevanallūr to meet the expenses of the festival on the new-moon days and for feeding the devotees who attended the temple on the day of Śittirai-tiruvila respectively to a maṭha in the temple of Tirumaiyūruḍaiyār at Kūrur. Mentions Māṇābharaṇa-Mūvēndavēḷār, a mudali of the Kūḷattūr-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: Kulottunga-Choladēva. [date-calculation appendix, No. 310: Śaka 1398, Vikrita, Aippasi 13, Trayōdaśi, Monday, Aśvati. The given details are not found in Ś. 1398 current = Vikrita = A.D. 1470-71.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the temple by certain residents of Poṇṇattūr in Tirumaiyūr-nāḍu a sub-division of Kuḷōttuṅga-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to provide for offerings to the same temple by the assembly of Vijayarājēndra-chatur-vēdimangalam a brahmadeya in Tirumaiyūr-nāḍu who met together in the temple of Tirumaiyūru-Muḍikoṇḍa v

cells.place: On the west wall of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for lamps to the same temple by a native of Sirṟalattur in Tirunāvaḻi-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kshatriyasikhāmaṇi-vaḷanādu.

cells.place: On the south wall of Amṛtavanēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and stones out of order. Seems to record a gift of land for a flower garden. Refers to Periyadēvar Tribhuvanaviradēva and mentions Sirrarkadu in Arkattū-kūṇam, a subdivision of Pāṇdikulaśani-valanādu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by purchase by a lady for burning a lamp in the same temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.date: 4th year, Sirnha, Wednesday, Pushya, sū. di. trayōdaśi. [date-calculation appendix, No. 315: 4th year, Simha, Wednesday, Pushya, śu. di. trayōdaśī. In A.D. 1220, on Wednesday, July 29 which fell in or immediately after close of 4th year (regnal year began according to Kielhorn between 27th June and 10th July 1216) ba. 13 (not śu. 13) in Simha, ended at 23 and Nak. 'Pushya' ended at 94.]
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by purchase to provide for a processional image of the god set up in the temple.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 9th year, Mithuna, śu. di. prathamā, Thursday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of land by purchase for offerings to the temple of Tirunāmāḍuḍaiyār at Kurur in Tirunāvaḻi-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kshatriyasikhāmaṇi-vaḷanādu. The land was sold by the assembly of Takkakōṇḍi alias Vijayarājēndra-chaturvēdimangalam in the same nādu and is stated to be in a subdivision of Uyyakkhoṇḍar-vaḷanādu.

cells.place: On the wall of Amṛtavanēśvara †
cells.remarks: Stones in disorder. Seems to record a gift of land and money for worship and offerings in the temple. The conquests of the king extend up to Kōṇādu.

cells.place: On the south wall of Netrodharkasvamin temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at both ends and incomplete. Begins with the introduction Śīṇgaśrēṇgālu, etc. Gift of paddy for a lamp to the temple of Paravai-Iśvaramudaiya-Mahadēva by a native of Tangdalam in Jayaṅgondaśola-mandalam.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Gift of paddy for a lamp to the temple of Paravai-Iśvaramudaiya-[Maha]dēva in the city of Paravaipuram in Purai[yūr]-nādu a subdivision of Panaiyūr-nādu which was a district of Rajendraśola-valanādu. Characters similar to that of No. 318 above.

cells.place: On the wall of Netrodharkasvamin †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Provides for offerings and lamps to (the images of f) Rajendraśoladēvar and Paravai-Nangaiyār set up in the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of Netrodharkasvamin temple. †
cells.date: Kollam (?) 902, Plavaṅga, Vaigāsi, 29. Details not enough for verification. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 321]
cells.remarks: Fragment. Provides for offerings and the reading of the Sivadharmam, recitation of the Tiruppadiyam hymns, musical performances on the vīṇai, etc., in the temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Netrodharkasvamin †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase to the same temple by a native of Pu [n] gajāyūr in Malai[n]-kūṛram, a district of Rājarāja-Pāṇḍināḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Netrodharkasvamin †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Mentions the temples of Paravai-Īśvara-muḍaiyār and Rājēndraśōḷa-Viṇṇagar-Āḷvār. Makes provision, for maintaining a teacher in a free school, for watersheds in front of the above-mentioned two temples and the mandapa called the Rājēndraśōḷan and for one who supervises the elevations, śālābhōga and the temples.

cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of Netrodharkasvamin temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions the temple of Kangamanda-Nāyaṇar in Puravār-Paṇangāttūr in Panaiyūr.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 6th , [date-calculation appendix, No. 325: Alagan-Perumāl Ativirarāma Śrivallabha. Śaka 150[8], [2]3rd year, Vyaya, Uttarāyana, Vasantaritu, Mēsha 7, ba. di. 10, Sunday, Avittam. = A.D. 1586; April 3, Sunday; '55; '62.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. The inscription commences with the words samasta-bhuvanaikavira, etc. Gift of lands for offerings and other requirements of the same temple.

cells.place: On the east wall of the same prākāra.
cells.remarks: Seems to record a gift of a garden for the merit of Maddu-Kṛishṇappa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the wall of Netrodharkasvamin .. †
cells.date: Śaka 1480, Kalayukti, Kārttigai. Details not enough for verification. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 327]
cells.remarks: The right side of this inscription is obstructed by the images of the deities. It is a gift of land in the village of Vēḷāṅguḍi for the merit of Mēḷaiyūr Pāvir Panniṅgaṭṭar and Senbai in Vaṇagap-pāḍi-naḍu on the northern bank of Peṇṇai (Peṇṇār). Above it is a fragment of an inscription in an early character which provides for various requirements of the temple of Madurāntaka-Īśvaramuḍaiyār Paravai-Īśvaram in Paraiyūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Paṇaiyūr-nāḍu which was a district of Jayangoṇḍa-Chōḷamaṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Satyan-bika shrine in Netrodharkasvamin temple. †
cells.date: Šaka 1312, Šukla. Kaṭakn, šu. di. Sunday, Mula. [date-calculation appendix, No. 328: Śaka 1[4]9 [2], 8th year, Pramōdūta, Tai 10. Day intended was probably Sunday, 7th January A.D. 1571; but there is no week-day in the inscription.]
cells.remarks: Records a rent-free gift of the village of Kuṇṛattūr in Kolliya-pāṇaiyūr-nāḍu for worship, festivals and repairs to the temple of Uḍaiyār-Kumaṇḍa-Nāyanār at Tiruppa-ravūr Paṇiṅgaṭṭar a line Paravaiyūr in Poṇaiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Paṇaiyūr-nāḍu which was a district of Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: At the entrance into the second prākāra of the same temple, left side.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Muḍḍukṛishṇappa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: At the entrance into the second prākāra of Satyan-bika shrine, left side. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Begins with the introduction [S]aka[s], etc. Reports that the assembly of the free village (taniyūr) Rājēndra-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmādāya in Paṇaiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Rājēndra-vaḷa-nāḍu met in the mandapa called Muṇḍadīśoḷan with Aruḷāḷanḍa-Vigraha and the village assembly of Muṇḍa-vōḷār who gave gift of lands. The gift of the village lands belonging to the temple of Triṇayapāḍidēvar to be taxed according to the lowest scale as in the case of the lands of the temples of Rājēraja-Viṇṇagar-ēvar and Kuṇḍavat-Viṇṇagar-ēvar.

cells.place: On the north wall of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: Šaka 1461, Vikari, Mi[thu]na, šu. di. pañchami, punarvasu, Wednesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 331: Śaka 1461, Vikāri, Mithuna, śu. di. pañchamī, Punarvasu, Wednesday. In Vikāri, Punarvasu in Mithuna fell on Tuesday (not Wednesday) śu. prathamā ending at ·05 and dvitīyā ending at ·97 (= A.D. 1539, June 17, Tuesday). Pañchamī an error for prathamā.]
cells.remarks: Records the gift of Nallalam as a vađa-ottukanipparru by Śraṅgarajar, son of a certain Venprumalai-itṭar, to a private individual. The free village of Ennayiram Rajaraja-ohaturvēdimaṅgalam is said to be situated in Panaiyūr-nađu, a subdivision of Palakunga-kōtṭam which was a district of Jayaṅgonda-Chōlamandalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: Śaka 1467, Viśvāvasu, Kumbha, śu. di. daśamī, Friday, Hasta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 382: Saka 1517, Manmatha, Simha, śu. di., paurṇimā, Aviṭṭam, Saturday = A.D. 1595, August 9; -85; -72.]
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Under the orders of Śiruppa-Nāyakkar-Ayyan, provision seems to have been made for presenting betel-leaf offering in the temple of Alagiyasinga-Perumāḷ at Emayiram, a subdivision of Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu, a subdivision of Pāṇḍyakulāśani-vaḷanāḍu of Jaṭāvarman Sundara-Chōḷadēva.

cells.place: On the wall of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words Śrīkachāvar, etc. Records that at the order of the king, a gift of 45 vēli of land in Ānaṅgūr alias Rajarājanallūr was made to the temple of Rajarāja-Vinnagar by the assembly of the free village (tapiyūr) Rajarāja-chaturvēdimangalam for offerings, festivals, recitation of Tiruvaymoli and the maintenance of an educational institution in which the Vedas, Vyakaraṇa, Mimamsa, and Vedanta were taught.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1465, Sōbhakrit, Magha 7. [date-calculation appendix, No. 384: Śaka 1469, Pramādi, Bhādrapada, śu. 15, Tuesday = A.D. 1547, August 30, Tuesday; ·81; “Satabhishaj” was current till ·17 on Tuesday.]
cells.remarks: Records that Śiruppa-Nāyakkar, the younger brother of Aḍapa-Baiyappa-Nāyanagāru reconsacrated the temple of Alagiyasinga-Perumāḷ at Emayiram which was built by Rājēndra-Chōḷa and had become dilapidated.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.date: 25th year and 112th day, Kaṇṇi, ba. di. Thursday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Records that by order of the king, the assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam, a free village (taniyūr) governed the village, and made a settlement (vyavasthai) regarding the incomes derived from lands belonging to a number of shrines and set apart for various services. Among the temple's deities mentioned are Rājarāja-Viṇṇagar-Āḷvār, Kuṇḍavai-Viṇṇagar-Āḷvār, Śrī-Kailāsa-Viṇṇagar-Āḷvār, Dēvēndra-Sarasvatī, Śrī-Bhaṭṭāraka, Mahāmōḍiyār, Sūryadēva, Saptamātṛis, Mahāśāstā, Durgaiyār, Subrahmaṇya, Jyēshṭhaiyār and the village gods.

cells.place: On the north wall of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: 11th ye4r [date-calculation appendix, No. 386: 6th year, Siṁha, śu. di., Ashṭami, Wednesday, Anusha = A.D. 1255, August 11. Śu. 8 commenced at ·27 on Wednesday and the nak. Viśākha ended at ·00 or A.D. 1228, August 9, Wednesday; f.d.t. ·18; f.d.n. ·09.]
cells.remarks: Records that at the order of the king, the assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam in Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu, gave Naṇṇāḍarpakkam alias Vikkiramaśōḷanallūr which was a dēvadāna, of Tiruvirāmēśvaramuḍaiyār at Eydar, a hamlet of this village, to Uyyakkonḍān Pañchanaḍi-Āṇḍān, an adhikārin in Poḷiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Ārmōḷidēva-vaḷanāḍu, for his descendants, as a kani-kavi. The village granted was renamed Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu-yūr and entered in the Revenue accounts. Mentions the Chief Secretary (tirumandirōlai) Chōḷēndrasiṅga-Mūvēndavēḷār.

cells.place: On the wall of Alagiya-Naraśinga-Perumāḷ †

cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a gift of land for offerings by a private individual. Refers to the 2 + 22nd year of the reign of Aļagaṇ Peruma] Parākrama-Pāndyadēva.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyalanallūr

cells.remarks: Gift of land 'tax-free' by the king for offerings to the temple of Kāriyamaṇikka-Aḷvār at Marudūrkōṭṭai.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyalanallūr
cells.place: On the same wall

cells.remarks: Gift of land in Aḷagulam alias Śīvakappāri at Marudūr-kōṭṭai to a certain Śīvayār-ēḍinān, a native of Tiru-vejumūr and one of the Śrī-Vaishnavas of the temple of Nāchchiyār at Śrīvilliputtūr in Tirunallī-nāḍu, for reciting daily in the presence of the god the hymns of Śaḍagōpaṇ (i.e., Nammāḷvār).

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †

cells.date: 2 + 37th year, Mina 26, śu. di. dasami, Pūsam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 645: 2 + 37th year, Mīna 26, śu. di. daśami, Puśam = A.D. 1469, March 22, f.d.t. ·00; ·33. The week-day was Wednesday.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship to the temple of Mayinār Kulashēkhara-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On the wall of Kāriya-māṇikka-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 2 + 40th year, Mosha 2* śu. di. pañchami, Wednesday, Uttirādam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 646: 2 + 40th year, Mēsha ·2, śu. di. pañchami, Wednesday, Uttirāḍam = A.D. 1473, April ·17, ·46; f.d.n. ·82. Nakshatra commenced at ·87 of day. But the week-day was Saturday not Wednesday.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Kuriyāṇaikkā-Āḷvār for being assigned as a kaṇiyāṭchi for writing the tirumugam.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of Kāriya-māṇikka-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land in Viraśikhāmaṇi, a village of Kallaga-nādu to the same temple.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On the wall of Kāriya-māṇikka-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship and feeding Brahmans.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyalanallūr
cells.place: On the wall of Kāriya-māṇikka-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 2 + 36th year, Vṛishchika 30, su. dvitīyā, Satur-day, Kēṭṭai. [date-calculation appendix, No. 649: 2 + 36th year, Vṛiśchika, 30, śu. di. dvitīyā, Saturday, Mūla = A.D. 1467, November 28, Saturday, f.d.t. ·06; ·20. śu. 2 commenced at ·03 of day.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land under the tank called Nōchchikkuḷam for daily worship and offerings to the temple of Kariyāṇaik-kā-Āḷvār.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On the east wall of the Vishṇu-kōṇi shrine in Kāriya-māṇikka-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.king: Jaṭilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnērinmaikoṇḍān Perumāḷ Kulashēkharadēva
cells.date: Saka 1456, Jaya, Vaikāshi 2, ba. di. prathama, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. The introduction commences with the words Bhuvamukhavīra, etc.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On the stone built into the outer-wall of Vishṇu-kōṇi shrine. †
cells.remarks: Records that the matha was the charity of Sāmman-malaiyan Ayudayan of Tirunelvēli.

cells.location: Kaḍaiyāḷanūr †
cells.place: On a slab known as Saṅgilippaṭṭar at Sivaramappaṭṭai, hamlet of Koḍikurichchi.
cells.date: Śuka 1589, Kollam 843, Plavaṅga, Karttigai 29. [date-calculation appendix, No. 652: Saka 1491, ba. di., dvitīyā, Tuesday, Uttara-Phalguṇi. Perhaps A.D. 1570, February 21 is the probable date for the details given above. The tithi commenced at -68 and the nak. Uttara-Phalguṇi ended at -83 on Tuesday. The month then must be Kumbha.]
cells.remarks: Records that Vadamalaiypapar Tirumalaikkolunda Pillai, the agent of the Nayaka, issued a sañkotapaṭtyayam for the occupation of Sivarāmapēṭtai by the people of the 56 countries.

cells.location: Iḍaikal
cells.place: On a stone set up on the roadside
cells.date: Saka 1522, 38th year, Iḍa (Chitta), Tai 10. [date-calculation appendix, No. 653: Saka 1477, Rākshasa, Simha, śu. di., dvitīyā, Sunday, Uttara-Phalguṇi = A.D. 1555, August 18; f.d.t., -20. The nak. was current throughout the day.]
cells.remarks: Records that a portion of Kijaṅgaṭtār was formed into a new village called Sivalanallur by Sivalamāṇa who revived the old times.

cells.location: Nayinaragaram
cells.place: On the north wall of the Kulaśōkharusvamin temple
cells.remarks: Records that the king granted Kulaśōkhara-agrahāra to 66 Brāhmanas of various gōtras and sūtras residing in Mungrumudikkumuriya-chaturvodimaṅgalam whose names are given in the inscription.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of Vishṇu-kōṇi shrine. †
cells.date: 3rd year, Tula 13, śu. di. tritiya, Monday, Anusham (Anuradha). [date-calculation appendix, No. 655: 33rd year, Tulā 13, śu. di. tritiyā, Monday, Anisham = A.D. 1645, October 13, Monday. But śu. 3 had ended at ·77 and the nakshatra Anisham at ·72 the previous day.]
cells.remarks: Anina was the third-day asterism of the King. Records that the lands granted in Nos. 653 and 654 were divided into 76 shares: 64 shares to Brahmans, four to the temple of Rājarājēśvara-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān, six to the temple of Kulashēkharēśvaram-Uḷaiyār and two to fragments.

cells.place: On stone built into the walls of the Vēdhavēśvaran temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Tyāgēśachihniya-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān at Iḍaikal.

cells.location: Panpuli
cells.place: On stone built into the walls of the Vēdhavēśvaran temple in the same village (as Vishṇu-kōṇi shrine). †
cells.king: Jaṭilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnermaikondāṇ Perumāl Parakrama Pandyadēva
cells.date: [Śuka 14] 67, 3rd year, Viśvavasu, Kanṇi 30, ba. di. dasami, Tuesday, Siddha-yōga, Rishabha-karaṇa, Puehya. [date-calculation appendix, No. 657: Jatilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnērmaikonḍān Perumāl Parākrama. Śaka ..67, 3rd year, Viśvāvasu, Kaṇṇi, ba. di. daśami, Tuesday, Puśhya. = A.D. 1545, September 29, Tuesday, f.d.t. ·57; ·46; ba. 10 commenced at ·49 of day.]
cells.remarks: Records that this prince [Tirunelvēliperumāḷ] born in the asterism a-vati was the son of Abhirāma-Pāṇḍyarājan assigned certain lands to a private individual for adhyayanam.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the north wall of the mandapa in front of Vēdhavēśvaran temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1466, 10th year, Krodhi, Kumbha 6, ba. di. pañchami, Sunday, Subha-yōga, Kōlava-karaṇa, Hasta.
cells.remarks: Records transfer of an assignment of land by the order of the king to the temple of Tiruvīraṭṭāṇam-uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, for worship in the temple of Nāgarīśvara and Pāṇḍya-paṭṭaṇam in Vaḍavāri-nāḍu. The original holder is said to have died without leaving any claimant.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.date: Śaka 14[72], 7th year, Śādharaṇa, Sīttirai 2[2], ba. di. saptamī, Wednesday, Gajakaraṇa, Śubhayōga, Pusam.
cells.remarks: Records gift of land to a private individual for writing the accounts of the temple. Mention of the temples of Nikuṭhēśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, Mūlasthānam-uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, Tiruvīraṭṭāṇam-uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, Ediriliśōlapuram, the village Parākrama-Pāṇḍyanallūr and prince Tirunelvēlipparuṇal born in the asterism Aēvati.

cells.location: Panpuli
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.date: Śaka 1469, 5th year, Plavaṅga, Kārttigai 7, ba. di. okadasī, Monday, Priti-yōga, Sīnha-karaṇa, Hasta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 660: Śaka 1192, Chaitra, śu. 13, Thursday = A.D. 1271, March 26, Thursday; ·05.]
cells.remarks: Records transfer of an assignment of temple land to a native of Tenkāśi for writing the accounts of the temples mentioned in 659 and for others at the instance of the prince Tirunelvēlipparuṇal born in the asterism Aēvati.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the west wall of Vēdhavēśvaran temple. †
cells.king: Jaṭāvarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnērinmaikoṇḍān Alagapperumāḷ Ālivirāma alias Śrīvallabhadēva.
cells.date: Śaka 1496, 17th year, Pramādi, Āṇi 3, ba. di. pañchamī, Śubhayōga, Śubhakaraṇa, Uttiram. [date-calculation appendix, No. 661: Śaka 1496 (= Bhava), 17th year, Pramādi (Ś. 1501), Āṇi 3, ba. di. pañchamī, Uttiram. Pramādi corresponded to (not Śaka 1496 but) Ś. 1501. Āṇi 3 in Pramadi fell on śu. 7 (not ba. pañchamī) on which day Uttiram began at 77 (= A.D. 1579, June 1, Monday). In Śaka 1496 (Bhava), Āṇi 3 fell on śu. 12 and the nakshatra was Visākhā. The day intended was probably the former.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to a certain Toṇḍaimān of Tirunelvēli in Kīlveṇbā-nāḍu made at the instance of prince Perumāḷ Alagapperumāḷa Vīrarāghavarāma for writing accounts (tavaṇai kaṇakku).

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the south wall of Vēdhavēśvaran temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1466, 10th year, Krodhi, Kumbha 6, ba. di. pañchami, Sunday, Subha-yōga, Kōlava-karaṇa, Hasta.
cells.remarks: Records transfer of assignment of a temple land on the death of the previous holder made in the instance of Tirunelvēlipparuṇal born in the asterism Aēvati for conducting worship in the temple of Nāgarīśvara.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.remarks: Refers to the transaction recorded in No. 662 above.

cells.location: Panpuli
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.date: Śaka 1425, 2 + 28th year, Kumbha 2, śu. di. dvadaśi, Sunday, Tiravadirai.
cells.remarks: The inscription reads from bottom upwards and records gift of land to Alaṅgari and others as kapiyaṭchi for doing service in the temples of Nakulīchchuramudaiyar and Nagarichchuramudaiya-Nāyaṇār at Gāṅgēyakulakalapuram alias Panpolil in Vadavari-nādu.

cells.location: Panpuli
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.remarks: Built in the middle, gift of land as a dēvadāna for offerings by Taṇḍaikkuḷḷāy Tirumalaināthē[ch]chan and Taṇḍaikkuḷḷāy Kāliṅgarāyaṇ of Pappuḷi alias Gaṅgayaṅkoṇḍapuram to the shrine of Tribhuvanasundara in the temple of Nāgarīśvara.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the wall of Vēdhavēśvaran †
cells.king: Jatilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Konerimaikondan Perumal Srivallabhadevan
cells.date: Śaka 1467, 10th your, Viśyāvasu, Tula 13, śn. di. pañchami, 'Monday, Siddha-yōga, Hasta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 666: Tirunelvēlipperumāḷ Kulaśēkhara.]
cells.remarks: Mentions Tirunelvelipperumal born in the asterism Asvati and records gift of land for ārbati offerings to the same temple.

cells.location: Iḍaikal †
cells.place: On the north wall of of Sundararaja-Perumal temple in the same village (as Vēdhavēśvaran temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 157 [4], Nandana, Āvani 20, Friday, ba. di. [dvādnāi], Pashya [date-calculation appendix, No. 667: Śaka 157[4], Nandana, Avaṇi 20, Friday, ba. [dvādaśi], Pushya. = A.D. 1652, August, 20, Friday; 69; 98.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple by two private individuals.

cells.location: Kankkuppillaiyavalasal
cells.place: On a slab known as Sarkara-Vinayakar
cells.date: Śaka 15 [9]4, Kollam 847, Paridhavi, Ādi 6, Sunday, Paurnamavasi, Vaidhriti-yōga, Śubhakaraṇa, Uttira-dam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 668: Śaka 15[9]4, Kollam 847, Paridhavi, Adi 6, Sunday, Paurnamāvasī, Uttiradam, = A.D. 1672, July 28, Sunday. Tēdi 6, is mistake for 29. Paurnamāvasī, began at 61 on this day.]
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to record a gift of land for the sacred bath and offerings to Sankaranaayanar for the merit of Achyutappa-Nayakkar. Mentions Sakkalingapuram.

cells.location: Tachhankudiyiruppu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the public well
cells.remarks: Gift of land for maintaining a matha by the agents of Tirumugappandiyariyan.

cells.location: Tachhankudiyiruppu †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field called Attamakkalvelji at Alagappapuram, hamlet of Kuttukalvalasai.
cells.king: Jatilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Konerimaikondan Perumal A- ganpuram] Adhivaram alias Sivadadyan.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village of Sambandhanallar for the festival called Chittirai-tirunal of the god and for the sacred bath of the goddess Ulagamman, by the king.

cells.location: Kolimigundla
cells.place: On a slab near the eastern wall of the Āṇjumayasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records that the Mahamandalesvara China-Timmayadava- Maharaju, son of Ramaraja, grandson of Ramaraja and great-grandson of Araviti Bukkaraja of the Atrēya-gotra and born in the lunar dynasty (soma-vamsa) granted, under orders of the king to the mahajanas of the agrahara of Kollimigundla in the Avuku-sima, the taxes, sōtriyam, Kanika, vetti and vānut in that village.

cells.location: Kollimigundla †
cells.place: On a stone built into the floor of Anjaneyasvami temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the construction of the garbhagriha of the temple by Bāla-Subbayya, son of Paṭham Chinna Veṅkaṭayya and Veṅkaṭamma.

cells.location: Kollimigundla †
cells.place: On a slab lying in the court-yard of ‘the four temples’ (nālku-guḍi-galu) in the same village (as Anjaneyasvami temple). †
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records the grant of 2 matta of land on the road to Kaikuṇṭ[e], a flower-garden and an oil-mill, for worship and offerings to the god Kēśava set up at Koḷmigūḍi by the village headman (prabhu) Muppi-Rāji.

cells.location: Koṭapaḍu
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the chāvaḍi
cells.remarks: Registers that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara China-Timmayya-dēva-Mahārāja, son of Timmārāja, grandson of Rāmarāja and great-grandson of Āravīṭi Bukkarāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra and the Sōma-vaṁśa remitted the taxes, śōtriyam, kaṭnam, kāṭika, veṭṭi and vēmi, payable to the palace by the mahājanas of Kōpaṭu and Kośinīpu in the Avuku-sīma and granted those villages as sarvamānya.

cells.location: Koṭapaḍu †
cells.place: On a stone set up in the place of Anjaneyasvami. †
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Much damaged; the last two or three lines alone are preserved. Mentions the name Prōlama-Raṭṭi of which the second part corresponds to raṭṭōḍi (Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XI, page 342 f).

cells.location: Koṭapaḍu †
cells.place: On a broken slab lying in the court-yard of the Śiva temple in the same village (as Anjaneyasvami temple). †
cells.dynasty: Bāṇa †
cells.remarks: Highly damaged. Begins with the usual eulogy of the Bāṇa kings : Śakalā-jagattraya, etc.

cells.location: Perūsumula
cells.place: On a slab built into the platform of the mukha-maṇḍapa in the Chennakesavasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: In modern characters. Damaged. Mentions Penumasni Tīrtha[n]nāyaka and seems to register an agreement with Voṅkaṭādri-Nāyaṅgāru.

cells.location: Perūsumula †
cells.place: On the east face of a stone set up at the entrance into Chennakesavasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions a certain [Ra]janarāja.

cells.location: Perūsumula †
cells.place: On the south face of the stone of Chennakesavasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara . . . Rāma-rāyya and Paruśumala.

cells.location: Perūsumula †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of Chennakesavasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Hanumyadēva-Mahārāja, son of Chiṇṭakunta Sōmanāthadēva-Mahārāja, of the Ātrēya-gōtra, granted to the god, Virayya, Chenna-kēśava-perumāḷ, of the Kōṭa-gōtra, the village of Perusamuḍa which Saluvarāja Raghupatirāya-Mahārāja had granted to him as umbali, the taxes paid in grain and in coin for the worship in the above-said temples. It is stated that these taxes had been unjustly imposed by previous rulers on tax-free lands.

cells.location: Perūsumula †
cells.place: On a stone lying in front of the karṇam's house in the same village (as Chennakesavasvāmin temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1299, Piṅgala, Margaśira, sū. di. 5, Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village [Peru]śalu to the teacher, Śivāchārya-Śivakēdēguru, by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara-Chōḍa-Mahārāja, son of Śāvana-Vōḍayar, on receiving from him the initiation (upadēśa) of Bayanēvari.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi
cells.place: On a pillar of the mukha-maṇḍapa in the Vaṅgōpalasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: States that Pannavataya, Anantayya and Mallayya, sons of Vallabhayya and grandsons of vipravinōdi Mallayya of the Kāśyapa-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Śukla Yajus-śākha and born in the Gōburikōḍu kula, granted the toll (śulka) of the village of Yarraguḍi (customary toll) paid by the mahājanas of Yarraguḍi to that community, for conducting the Vaiśākha festival of the god Gōpinātha.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi †
cells.place: On another pillar in Vaṅgōpalasvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the grant of lands to two masons (viz.) Basavōju, son of Vallabōju and the son of Tiṇṇabattu by Viṭṭhalarāja, son of Nāgarāja-Bēṇuarāja under the orders of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Yarraguḍi Tirumalayadēva-Mahārāja.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi †
cells.place: On a pillar of the mukha-maṇḍapa in the Śiva temple in the same village (as Vaṅgōpalasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the southern stone wall of the mukha-maṇḍapa in the temple of Bhōgadēva, by Bakkann, son of Kēśana-heḍḍi and grandson of Hēmantin-Reḍḍi.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi †
cells.place: On the base of a water-trough in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of one dry and one wet field to the men who filled this trough with water, by Anumantayya, son of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara-Gōparāja Abhayarāja, for the merit of Tirumalairāja-Gōparāja-Mahārāja.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi †
cells.place: On the outer surface of the same water-trough.
cells.remarks: States that Anumantayya, son of Abhayarāja constructed the water-trough for the merit of Tirumalairāja, son of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Yarraguḍi Kāchirāja.

cells.location: Yarraguḍi †
cells.place: On a stone which serves as a foot-step leading into the Ādijēya-svāmin temple in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to mention [Varagu]ḍi Timmala and a mahāsāsana put up by him at Yarraguḍi. Refers to internal dispute and their settlement by the elders of the village.

cells.location: Hanumantagundam
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Chennakēśavasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records the grant of lands for providing breakfast for Brahmans on the Dvādaśī day for god Raghunāyaka in the temple of Hanumantarāya at Hanumantagundam by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Jīleļa Raṅgapatirājayya, for the merit of the king.

cells.location: Hanumantagundam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Chennakēśavasvāmin temple at B. Uppalūru.
cells.date: Śaka 1469, Parābhava, Māgha, ba. di. 3, [Monday]. [date-calculation appendix, No. 689: Śaka 1469 (Plavaṅga), Parābhava (Ś. 1468), Māgha, ba. di. 3 [Monday] = A.D. 1547, February 7, Monday; ·93]
cells.remarks: States that Anantayya and Paravataayya, sons of vipravinōdi Vallabhayya of the Kāśyapa-gōtra, the Kātyāyana-sūtra and the Śukla-Yajur-śākhā and some others granted for the merit of the vipravinōdi community, the village of Uppalūru to them for the construction of a maṇḍapa in front of the temple of the god Chennakēśava of the god Chennakēśvara at Malimāḍu-Puṇḍi, the village of Sōmalasamudra in the Ghaṇḍikōṭa-sīma, the amara śīme of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Nāndela Timmayadēva-Mahārāja. The names of a few other members of the community are also mentioned.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Āñjanēyam temple
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the income derived from svāmyata etc. on numerous festive occasions (?) in the Kovilakuṇṭla-sīma by Dēvarāya-Mahārāja, son of Siṅgarayyādēva-Mahārāja and grandson of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Nāndela Narasiṅgayadēva-Mahārāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra and born in the lunar race. The country of Kovilakuṇṭla-sīma was enjoyed under feudal tenure by these chiefs as a gift from the king.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Guḍḍēśa temple in the same village (as Chennakēśavasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Siddharámappa-Náyanigáru, son of Immeđi-Démappa-Náyanigáru and grandson of Haṇdé-Démappa-Náyanigáru, declaring that the mortgagees of the many-lands of Gods and Brahmanas should, in the 13th year after possession, restore them back to the owners with documents without receiving back any money.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a broken slab lying in the courtyard of the Śiva temple in the same village (as Guḍḍēśa temple). †
cells.remarks: Broken and damaged. Registers a gift of land for a temple after building it, on a day of solar eclipse.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Vīrabhadrasvāmin temple in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1744, Chitrabhānu, Mārgaśira, śu. di. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 693: Saka 1474, Paridhāvi, Pushya, ba. di., 30, Solar eclipse = A.D. 1553, January 14, Saturday. There was a solar eclipse on Saturday.]
cells.remarks: Relates that Basuvaliṅgayyu, son of Maraiyya and Báramma, the shareholder of a moiety in the many-lands of the maṭhas, Pedgómaṭha and Dornipaṭi and other villages, repaired by raising alms the temple of Virabhadrésvara at Kövelakuntlá which was in ruins. The merchant classes, on being approached, gave for worship and offering ½ chittedu of rice and one ruvva-weight of lamp-oil. And on Friday fairs, those who sold by scale, set apart ½ guvagulu (?) and those who sold by measure, one chittedu, evidently for the same purpose.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Aśvatthasvāmin temple in the same village (as Vīrabhadrasvāmin temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1476, Ānanda, Chaitra, śu. di. 10. [date-calculation appendix, No. 694: Śaka 1470, Kīlaka, Mārgasira, śu. 11, Thursday. The date intended is apparently A.D. 1548, November 11, Sunday; ·98. The week-day quoted in the inscription seems to be a mistake.]
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the vartana paid to them year after year by the mahājanas of Kōvilakuṇṭla for the Śrīrāma-jātrā festival in the temple of Kōvilakuṇṭla Vithalēśvara at Kōvilakuṇṭla, by Chāṭṭalamāri Pānḍuranga, son of Vallabhayya and grandson of vipravinōdi Mallayya of the Kaśyapa-gōtra, the Kātyāyana-sūtra and the Prathama-śākha, Mādhavayya, son of Vāraṇāsi Vallabhayya and grandson of vipravinōdi Piriyana of the Vāraṇāsi-gōtra, the Āśvalāyana-sūtra and the Ṛg-śākha and other vipravinōdis for the maintenance of the vipravinōdi community in Vidyanagaram, Boḍḍakoṭla, Kaṭaka and the Draviḍa-dēśa.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a pillar in the mukha-maṇḍapa of the Raṅgasvāmin temple in the same village (as Aśvatthasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of a house, land, and garden at Kōvilakuṇṭla and money for the maintenance of the Ranganāthasvāmin matha there by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Timmayadēva-Mahārāja, son of Nandyāla Nāraṇarāja and grandson of Nandyāla Nāraṇarāja, of the Ātrēya-gōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra and born in the lunar race.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a broken slab set up in the court-yard of Raṅgasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: The top portion is broken. Registers the grant, on the banks of the Kṛishṇa, of lands and flower-gardens for the vasantōtsava and other festivals of the god Panḍurangī Vithalēśvara, by Timmayadēva, son of Murāri-rāja and grandson of Rāmarāja of the Ātrēya gōtra and born in the lunar race.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Raṅgasvāmin. †
cells.date: Śaka 1506, Tarana, Kārtika, śu. di. 15, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: States that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Veṅkaṭādrirāja, son of Kṛishṇarāja and grandson of Nandyāla Nāraṇarāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra, the Āpastamba-sūtra and the Yajuś-śākha granted as sarvamānya, lands in the villages of Kōvilakuṇṭla, Chintakunta, Chinakōperla and ..., the vartana (customary tax) on kabbus (sugarcane) and ... the mānakōṭa and kōlayata collected at Kōvilakuṇṭla for offerings, the bodily and festive enjoyments, the Rāma-nija-kūṭa, the palanquin service and other festivals of the god Vithalēśvara at Kōvilakuṇṭla.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the third slab set up in the place of Raṅgasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: The bottom portion of the grant is seriously damaged. States that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Nāraṇarājadēva-Mahārāja, son of Timmayadēva-Mahārāja and grandson of Nandyāla Nāraṇarājadēva-Mahārāja made grandson to the god Panḍurangī Vithalēśvara-Mahārāja made grant to the god Panḍurangī Vithalēśvara at Kōvilakuṇṭla in Kōgilakuṇṭla-sīma which was granted to him as a nāyaṅkara by Śrīraṅgadēva-Mahārāya.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the fourth slab set up in the place of Raṅgasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Chinakōperla attached to Kōgilakuṇṭla-sīma, granted to him as nāyaṅkara by Timmayadēva-Mahārāja, of lands, wet lands, toṭla, money-income and fruit trees to the god Panḍurangī Vithalēśvara-Perumāḷ at Kōvilakuṇṭla by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Nāraṇarājadēva-Mahārāja, son of Timmayadēva-Mahārāja and grandson of Nandyāla Nāraṇarājadēva-Mahārāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha and born in the lunar race.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up on a platform at the entrance into the village of Akumalla.
cells.remarks: Records that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara China-Timmayyadēva-Mahārāja, son of Timmarāja, grandson of Rāmarāja and great-grandson of Āravīṭi Bukkarāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra and born in the lunar race remitted the taxes, śrōtriyam, kaṭnam, kānika, veṭṭi and vēmi payable to the palace by the mahājanas of Ākumāla in Āvuku-sīma held by him as a nāyaṅkara from the king.

cells.place: On a slab lying in the Chennakēśavasvāmin temple at Ardavīḍu (Cumbum taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Highly damaged. Registers a gift of land made for the bodily and festive enjoyments of the god Ahōbala-Nara[siṁha] at Araduṭuvīḍu, after repairing the breaches in the tank.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On another slab lying in the place of Chemakōṭa-vasavam. †
cells.date: Śaka 1112, Tāraṇa (mistake for Sādhāraṇa), Kārtika, śu. di. Paurṇamī.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of one puṭṭeḍu of wet land, one puṭṭeḍu of dry land and one kuncheḍu of garden land for the daily offerings and worship of Siddha-Mallikārjuna of Adidamvīḍu by Visanoḍayalu.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a pillar of the mukha-maṇḍapa in the Śiva temple at Remata (Gudur sub-taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Mentions Chanda-Gāvu[ṇḍa], Gogga-Gāvuṇḍa and [Bīra]-Gāvuṇḍa who were evidently the builders of the maṇḍapa.

cells.place: On four pieces of a broken slab lying near the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1471, Piṅgala (wrong), Bhādrapada, śu. di. 10. [date-calculation appendix, No. 704: Saka 1479, Piṅgala, Chaitra, ba. di., dvādaśi. Details not enough for verification.]
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of a dry field by Sō[ra*]rāja and Kō[nērā*]ja, sons of Pinnamarāja, for feeding Śrī-Vaishṇavas during the tirunāḷ-festivities of the god Gōpīnātha at Kandanavōlidurgam. The cultivators, Kādi-Reḍi of Gōranṭla, Yēli-Reḍi, Timmi-Reḍi and others who cultivated the land thus granted, agreed to pay the several items of income on the land for the said purpose and to maintain the charity.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On another fragment of a slab in the place of Ādijanēśvara-svāmi. †
cells.remarks: Mentions Pinnamarāja and the gift of two fields made in the presence of Viṭhalēśa. Evidently the reference is to the grant of land recorded in No. 704 above.

cells.location: Anantapur District, Madakasira Taluk. — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the west of Muddanallayyanapalya, a hamlet of Agali.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land for lamps in the temple of Kāḷikādēvi and Kamaṭēśvara at Agaḷi, by Raṅgapparāja [son of] Mahārāja Harati Sarajarāyapparāja.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab lying on the west side of the same hamlet.
cells.remarks: "May this pillar which is of the form of a boundary (mark) on the south side of the village of īṅgalāru remain permanent." The slab was evidently put up on the occasion of fixing the boundaries of īṅgalāru, a village 2 miles north of Agali.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab built into the wall left of entrance into the main shrine of the Rāmasvāmi temple at Ramapuram, another hamlet of the same village (as Ādijanēśvara-svāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Records that Rayaparāja, the grandson of Chōḷarāya to whom the god Rāmachandra had become manifest built maṇḍapas and [gō*]puras and also performed sacrificial rites.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a beam of the mukha-mandapa in Rāmasvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Refers to the manifestation of the god Rāmachandradēva before the "Eleven Rudras" and to his having received worship at the hands of Chōḷarāya. Registers the construction of the gōpuras and the front-maṇḍapas, the several repairs and the performance of sacrifices by Rāyaparāja, the grandson of that Chōḷa. He also granted to the god Rāmachandra the villages, Rāmachandrapura, Īśvarapura, Rāyasāgara, Komadēnahaḷi, Nirukalu in Miḍigēśi-sīme and Maddagiri in Bijāvarada-sīme and lands under the tanks of Agaḷi, Maduviḍu, Raviḍu, Kaṇṭavaḷalu and Kāki.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the south base of Rāmasvāmi temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1407, Viśvāvasu, [Āśvija], ba. di. .. solar eclipse. [date-calculation appendix, No. 710: Śaka 1407, Viśvāvasu [Āśvija] ba, solar eclipse. There was a solar eclipse on ba. amāvāsyā in Śrāvaṇa. The date given will correspond to A.D. 1485, September 9, Friday. ba. 30 ended at ·00.]
cells.remarks: Registers that Rāyapparāja, son of Ba[yi]rajadēva-Chōḷa-Mahā-arasu gave a valley after purchasing it, a field of 15 honnu (tax) and the channel Śaṅkaradēvara-kāluve to the god Rāmachandra and to the individuals Narasiṁha-Sōmayāji, Prasanna-Sōmayāji and Lakshmaṇa-Sōmayāji, sons of Daśagranthi Narasiṁha-Sōmayāji of Madhusūdanapura, of the Āśvalāyana-sūtra, Kāśyapa-gōtra and Ṛik-śākhā. The valley was converted into the tank called Narasāmbudhi in the name of the king and the four khaṇḍugas of land below it was equally divided between the three brothers and the god Rāmachandra.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the south wall of Rāmasvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. States that Rāyapparāja, grandson of Chōḷa-Mahārāya to whom the god Śrī-Rāmachandra had made himself manifest, constructed the maṇṭapa, the prākāra and the gōpura, celebrated the car-festivals of that god and granted the villages of Rāmachandrapura, Īśvarapura and Rāyasāgara and also a tank built in his name.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up by the side of the road on the west side of Agali.
cells.remarks: Registers the kānachi grant of a mānya land of five kolagas below the Agaḷi tank for an areca-nut garden to Agaḷigoṇḍa-Gauḍa, son of Molegoṇḍa-Gauḍa of Agaḷi, by the Mahānāyakāchārya Harati Raṅgapa-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a slab set up on a vacant site in the middle of the same village (as Rāmasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers that Alappa, the brother of Addiri Dēvaṇṇa and the brother-in-law of the Mahāpradhāna Jatiya-Daṇṇāyaka [commenced] the repairs to a breach in the bund of the Agaḷi tank, 60 māru long, 12 māru broad and 12 men deep and completed it on Monday the 10th of the dark half of Phālguna.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a stone lying in the court-yard of a Jaina basti in the same village (as Rāmasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: [This is] the nisidhi of Krish[ṇi]-Seṭṭi, son of Beṭṭi-Seṭṭi, a lay disciple of Dēvachandradēva of the Mūla-saṅgha and the Dēśiya-gaṇa.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a pillar set up in a field north-east of the same village (as Rāmasvāmi temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1621, Vikāri, Pushya, ba. di. 7, Friday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 715: Śaka 1521, Vikāri, Pashya ba. di. 7, Friday. = A.D. 1599, December 28, Friday; 89.]
cells.remarks: Registers the sarvamānya grant of a garden-land to the nīrgaṇṭi Kammaṭi Basavirayya by the gauḍa (headman) and the sēnabōva (karaṇam) of Agaḷi.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On a beam supporting the roof of the choultry in the same village (as Rāmasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of wet, dry and areca-nut garden lands by Kōṭaya, the daṇḍanāyaka of Ballaha to a temple of Vishṇu (Vishṇu-gṛiha) built by himself.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Saṅkarēśvarasvāmi temple in the same village (as Rāmasvāmi temple) †
cells.date: Śaka 1432, Pramōda, Āśvija, śu. di. 12. [date-calculation appendix, No. 717: Śaka 1198, 5th year, Dhātu, Chitra, śu. di., prathamā, Tuesday = A.D. 1276 March 17. Śu. 1 commenced at ·12 on Tuesday and the nak. was Rēvati.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the remission of taxes on marriages in the several provinces of the Vijayanagara kingdom.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the wall of Saṅkarēśvarasvāmi †
cells.date: Śaka 1209, 17th year, Saravajit, Śravaṇa, śu. di., paurṇimā, Thursday = A.D. 1287, July 25; f.d.t. ·81. The week-day was Friday and not Thursday. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 718]
cells.remarks: Registers that Kachapa-Voḍeya granted the taḷavārike of Agaḷi to taḷavāra Doḍḍa, son of Chanda-Nāyaka of Hulikunṭe.

cells.location: Anantapur District, Madakasira Taluk. — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On the wall of Saṅkarēśvarasvāmi †
cells.date: Śaka 1420, Piṅgala, Chaitra, śu. di. 15, Saturday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 719: Śaka 1420, Piṅgala, Chaitra, śu. di. 15, Saturday = A.D. 1497, March 18, Saturday.]
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village of Paḷḷiganahaḷḷi alias Immaḍikāchapura in Agaḷi-sthaḷa in Rāyadurga-chāvaḍi by Immaḍi Kāchapa-Nāyaka, son of Kāchapa-Nāyaka of Ādavāni, for offerings to the god Śaṅkaradēva and the sahadēvatās (attendant deities) at Agaḷi in the presence of the god Rāmēśvara at Sētubandha-Rāmēśvara whither he had gone with Narasaṇa-Nāyaka. It is stated that Kāchapa-Nāyaka held the district Rāyadurga-chāvaḍi as a fief from Narasiṅgarāya-Mahārāya and Narasaṇa-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Kovela-kuṇṭla †
cells.place: On the east wall of Saṅkarēśvarasvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the grant of wet lands under the tanks of Togaṭigere, Paṭigere and Agaḷikere as sarvamānya to taḷavāra Mādapa of Agaḷi, by the Mahānāyakāchārya Harati Raṅgapa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of a maṇḍapa on the south-western side of the village of Ratnagiri.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the gift of Bhuṭṭenaha[ḷ]ḷi surnamed Raṅgāpura, a village in Ratnagiri-sthaḷa in Agaḷi-sīme belonging to Rāyadurga-rājya, to Bhadrappadēvaru, son of Kachchuṭadadēvaru and grandson of Nambiyaṇṇadēvaru of Nāgarabāvi of the Ātrēya-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra by the Mahānāyakāchārya Raṅgappa-Nāyaka, son of Lakshmīpati-Nāyaka, a pupil of Bhadrappadēva and grandson of Harati Guṇḍappa-Nāyaka of the Yanumala race and the Vamlika (Vālmīki?)-gōtra.

cells.place: On a boulder in front of the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple, south of the same village.
cells.remarks: This (temple ?) was the work of the son of Kāśi Periyaṇṇa and grandson of Chavaṇḍi-Āchāri.

cells.place: On a stone set up in a field to the west of Tigalerahatti, hamlet of Ratnagiri.
cells.remarks: Timma-Gauṇḍa is the holder of the kaṇachi-gauḍike in the agrahāra of Sā[ḷva]-Bhaṭa.

cells.place: On a hero-stone lying in a field south of Lakkappanahalli, hamlet of Kaki.
cells.remarks: Mentions Saṇṇariyar, a servant of Kāvali-Arasa and the assault of Karaṭikallu. Some gifts were made to this Saṇṇariyar in the newly acquired country.

cells.place: On a pillar supporting the roof of the village entrance at Byadigera, a hamlet of the same village.
cells.remarks: States that this stone entrance was constructed by [Ma]laiya of Bēdageri.

cells.place: On a hero-stone lying in a date-grove to the west of the same hamlet.
cells.remarks: Damaged. In characters of about the tenth century. Refers to a cattle raid and to the death of some heroes.

cells.location: Dodderi
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Kariyamman temple
cells.remarks: Records the construction of this temple by Maḷamma, wife of Pūjāri Vaḍusaiya.

cells.location: Flodderi †
cells.place: On a boulder at the entrance into the same village (as Kāriyaman temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 15[0]8, Vyaya, Kartiku, sū. di. 12, Utthāna-dvādaśi. [date-calculation appendix, No. 728: Śaka 10 [47], Makara, ba. 11, Friday = A.D. 1125, January 2, Friday; ·28.]
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Registers the gift of the village of Do[d]deri surnamed Veñkaṭeśvarasamudra in Agalī-sīme by the Muhanāyakachārya 'aṅgapa-Nāyaka, son of Harati Lakshmipati-Nāyaka of the Kasyapa-gōtra. Mentions Siṅgām-Bhata of the Kasyapa-gōtra, Vaikhāmasu-sutra and Yajuś-śākhā and his descendents who were establishers of the Vedumarga (Vedamargapratishṭhacharya).

cells.location: Flodderi †
cells.place: On a slab lying near the Arjanyasvamin temple at Sarajamannahalli, a hamlet of Kotagaralahalli.
cells.date: Kīlaka, Phalguna, sū. di. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 729: Saka 1466, Krōdhi, Māgha, ba. di., ēkādaśi. Details not enough for verification.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the gift of the village of Kariyakētanahalli as a kodge to Kalī-Nāyka of Kaidala by the big merchants (maha-vaddavevahāri, ubhayananādeśi) and the gaudas of Agalī, ṭaṭhūvadi and Nidugallanādu. Mentions incidentally Vira Ballaĵadeva.

cells.location: Flodderi †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the north of Badigegondanahalli, another hamlet of the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers the sale of the lands and attached to the gudike of the village of Kereyodatanahalli for 7 varahas by Bolaya, son of Basavagaunda of Karukattahalli to a merchant Bafso-vaya.

cells.location: Madhudi
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the court-yard of the Mallesvarasvamin temple
cells.date: Saka 881 Siddharthi. [date-calculation appendix, No. 731: Saka 1482, Raudri, Mārgaśira, ba. di., shashṭhi. Details not enough for verification.]
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land to the temple of Vishnu (Vishnu-griha).

cells.location: Madhudi †
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near the Arjanyasvamin temple in the same village (as Mallesvarasvamin temple). †
cells.king: Mayipommdeva †
cells.remarks: Registers that Buchaya, son of Yaraka-Gaudu of Madhuvadi, fell fighting in a Hoyisana (Hoysala) raid which happened during the reign of Mayipommdeva and that a garden and a wet field measuring 100 kulas were given.

cells.location: Madhudi †
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the bazar in the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1091. Virodhi, Śravuna, sū. di. Trayōdaśi, 1 hurs-day, Uttarayanna-vēñkramapa. [date-calculation appendix, No. 733: Śaka 1177, Rākshasa, Āshāḍha, śu. di., ēkādaśī, Monday = A.D. 1255, June 16, Wednesday. Here also the week-day given in the inscription appears to be a mistake.]
cells.remarks: While Jagadekamalla-Mallideva-Chola-Mahāraja, son of Iruṅgōja was ruling at Heñijeṛu, the Mahapradhāna Hiniya-Tantrapala Nāmana, son of Echimayya and Muddab[b]e and younger brother of Bammana, granted a wet land, a garden land and an oil-mill for a perpetual lamp, rice offerings, bodily enjoyments, servants, repairs, the Chaitra-pavitra festival, and the feeding of Brahmanas and asectics, in the temple of Nāgēśvara at Madhuvadi.

cells.location: Madhudi †
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the north of the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the gift and the village Madhuvadi; also to the death of a hero.

cells.location: Ravadi
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up on the tank bund
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Damaged. Mentions Siragutti.

cells.location: Ravadi †
cells.place: On a pillar lying near the Arjanyasvamin temple in the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1526, Krodhi, Pushya, ba. di. [3], Makara-Sañkrānti.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the gift of the village Ravadi, sur-named Kumara-Ramapura to Madhuvadi-nadu in Agali-sime, belonging to the Bayaduga-vente to Umapati-Arasu, son of Somaya, the grandson of Kotaya Ramaraya, of the Bharadvaja-gotra, Asvalayana-sutra and Rik-sakha by the Mahamandalacharya Immadi Kempa-pa-Nayaka, son of Lakshmipati-Nayaka Rangapa-Nayaka of Harati.

cells.location: Ravadi †
cells.place: On a slab set up near the village entrance at Aludi, a hamlet of the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers an umbaḷi grant of the village Āluvaḍi belonging to Maduviḍi, with all its forests, wet lands, income in money and grain, for perpetual enjoyment to Sahēkhāna Khalila, by Harati Raṅgapparāja [son] of Sara[ja*]rāyaparāja, for his valuable service to the state.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple in the same hamlet.
cells.date: Śaka 1238, Naḷa, Phālguna, śu. di. 5, Thursday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 738: Śaka 1238, Naḷa, Phālguna, śu. di. 5, Thursday = A.D. 1317, February 17, Thursday.]
cells.remarks: Mentions a son of the king named Tipparasa Bhairavadēvarasa. Records the gift of the village of Haḷuviḍi to a merchant by the above-named prince as a koḍagi grant.

cells.location: Ravadi †
cells.place: On a stone set up on the frontier line between Muddalur of the Mysore state and Aludi.
cells.date: Saka 1485, Durmati, Śrāvaṇa, śu. di., 15. Details not enough for verification. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 739]
cells.remarks: Mentions a son of the king named Tipparasa Bhairavadēvarasa. Records the gift of the village of Haḷuviḍi to a merchant by the above-named prince as a koḍagi grant.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the backyard of a house at Komarenahalli, a hamlet of the same village.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of a wet and a dry field to Chiga-Boppaya, son of Gaudra Boppaya of Komarehal[1]i for his construction of the foundation of the fort thereof, by Harati Sarajaráyaparaja.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple at Paduvala Byadigera.
cells.remarks: Registers the sale of the village of Paḍuvaṇa Byāḍagere in Maduviḍi-sthaḷa with its forests, wet lands, money-income, grain-income, etc., for 500 Pādaśāhi varahas to Saida Yakūba-Bokāri, son of Saida Mīrāna and grandson of Saida Yakūba-Bokāri by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Raṅgapparāja, son of Vīra-Rāyapparāja and grandson of Harati Sarajā Sammeṭa-Rāyapparāja of the Ātrēya-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā for the darga also called the maṭha of the teacher at Sirya.

cells.place: On a hero-stone lying in a field to the east of Upparatonasanahalli, hamlet of the same village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that this stone was put up in memory of the self-immolation of a gamuṇḍa (gāvuṇḍa) in fire.

cells.place: On a slab built into the fort wall at Vadaguntanahalli, another hamlet of the same village.
cells.remarks: Records the sale of Vaḍaguṇṭahaḷḷi in Maduviḍi-sthaḷa, for 450 Kaṇṭirāyi varahas, the parties to the transaction and the purpose thereof being the same as in No. 741 above.

cells.place: On a stone set up on the road from Cherulopalli to Chintakunta.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of a tank (kuṇṭe) to the god Tiruveṅgaḷanātha of Śire by the Gajapati prince Vīrabhadrarāya for the merit of king Krishṇarāya.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the north of the village of Narasambudhi.
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Registers the death of Mādaṇṇa, son of Keradara Beḷḷi-Gāvuṇḍa of Piri-Yiṅgaḷūru, in . . . . . after causing a thousand (of his enemies ?) to be cut off.

cells.location: Ravadi †
cells.place: On another hero-stone lying in the place of Arjanyasvamin. †
cells.remarks: Do. Registers the death of Keradara-Bijayi, son of Māyiṇḍa-Gāvuṇḍa who was the younger brother of Beḷḷi-Gāvuṇḍa of Piri-Yiṅgaḷūru, in a cattle-raid.

cells.location: Ravadi †
cells.place: On another broken hero-stone lying in the place of Arjanyasvamin. †
cells.remarks: Do. Records the death of Sikka (Chikka) Chendu-Gāvuṇḍa, son of Akkā-Gāvuṇḍa and grandson of Bērikalla Pir[i]-Cha[m]dra-Gāvuṇḍa, in a cattle-raid.

cells.location: Inugaluru
cells.place: On a stone lying beneath the tank-bund
cells.remarks: Do. Records the death of a hero, the son of [U]mapati-Arasa in the cattle-lift at Māḷajāvara-Mārimañchi.

cells.location: Huilīkēredevanahalli
cells.place: On a stone lying in a field in front of the Aujaneyasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village of Huilīkēre belonging to Āgaļi-grāma as a sarvamānja to Brāhmanas by-mana-Nāyaka for the merit of Krishnaraya-Maharaya on the banks of the Gautamī, in presence of the god Markandēśvara.

cells.location: Madakasira
cells.place: On the four slabs of the parapet wall of a well in a house
cells.date: Śaka 1505, Svabhānu, Āśrya [Āśvina ?], śu. 10, Saturday. Perhaps A.D. 1588, September 15, Sunday; f.d.t. ·57. The week-day in the inscription may be an error. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 750]
cells.remarks: Three of the slabs bear the name Lakahamagatīrtha engrav-ed in Kannada, Nāgarī and Kamanesa characters. The fourth slab, which is Nagari is much damaged. It men-tions Madakāra and some other name (not legible on the impression) and a religious teacher.

cells.location: Madakasira †
cells.place: On a pillar of a dilapidated mandapa in the court-yard of the Vēṇugōpālasvāmin temple in the same village (as Arjanyasvamin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers that the king of Vēňgi ran away on hearing that the Chōla (king) had ordered (his general) Sōļiyavaraiyan to conquer that country; see nos. 23 of 1917.

cells.location: Madakasira †
cells.place: On another pillar in the place of Vēṇugōpālasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Registers that the mandapa (in which these pillars originally were) was commenced on the 160th day of this year and finished in 40 days by the general Arniyan Rajarājan alias Vikramaśōla-Sōliyavaraiyan of Sattamaṅgalam in Tiraimūr-nādu. Below the inscription are engraved the titles Edirttavarkalan and Samantakesari; see ibid and No. 24.

cells.location: Sante-Bīdanūru
cells.place:
Anantapur district, Hindupur taluk.
On a hero-stone set up in a vacant site
cells.remarks: Refers to a fight between the king and Ayyakuṭți in which some heroes appear to have died. The end of the record is not quite intelligible.

cells.location: Sante-Bīḍanūru †
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the south of the village of Tur-gepalli, a hamlet of the same village.
cells.remarks: Seriously damaged. Mentions a chief who was entitled Pallavabhumalla.

cells.location: Sante-Bīḍanūru †
cells.place: On a stone lying in a field to the west of the village of Karudipalli, a hamlet of Chaulluru.
cells.remarks: Records the kuṭukuḍigi grant of a land to a private individual of Darvadaṇali by Aiduļa Hammu Baһāba ruling the Ponugonda-rājya for his having constructed the new village called Hosaduļi.

cells.location: Modā
cells.place: On a stone lying near the Añja-nēyasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of a māyuva land by Vīrappa to Virapans Parvatārādhya of Gūṇuṇḍu for conducting the worship of Śiva.

cells.location: Śrīkaṇthapuram
cells.place: On a slab set up near the chāvaḍi
cells.date: Šaka 1426, Krōdhana, Chaitra, śu. di. 1, Wednesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 757: Śaka 1426, Krōdhana (= Ś. 1427) Chaitra, śn. di. 1, Wednesday. Śaka 1426 (= A.D. 1504-05) corresponded to Rakshasa (not to Krōdhana) in which Chaitra śu. 1 was Sunday. In Krōdhana (= Śaka 1427) Chaitra śu. 1, was Thursday the tithi ending at 91 but Quaitra śu 1, in Śaka 1428 (i.e.,) Kshaya Samvat was Wednesday (= A.D. 1506, March 27, Wednesday). The inscription refers to Chaitra at the beginning or Chaitra at the end of a year. Śaka 1426 (= Krōdhana = A.D. 1505-06), which would be the same as Chaitra at the beginning of A.D. 1506-07 (= Ś. 1428 = Kshaya Samvat).]
cells.remarks: (Erhanganged). Seems to record the grant of the village (Śrīrangasamudra, to a certain Narasimha-Dīkshita of the Ārvalayans-sūtra and the Kāsypana-gōtra.

cells.location: Paldūti
cells.place: On a broken stone lying near a private house
cells.remarks: Mentions a certain Nolam[ba]-Gāmuṇḍa.

cells.location: Paḍḍēri †
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the south of the same village (as Vēṇugōpālasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: The stone is broken and the characters visible are highly damaged. Seems to refer to a cattle-raid and the gift of a kaināḍu.

cells.location: Yerragunta
cells.place: On a Nandi-pillar set up near the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple
cells.date: Ānanda, Māgha, ba. di. 5. (at the end of the record is given ba. di. 3).
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of Yaragunṭe, a village between Ūṭakūru and Herahe to the god Vīrabhadra as a pura by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Iguṇadēva-Chōḷa-Mahārāja. Several items of income are mentioned, such as, cash, grain, sheep, cows, potter’s fee, forced labour, etc.

cells.location: Parigi
cells.place: On a hero-stone lying in a field under the tank bund
cells.remarks: Registers the death of Madesakada-Khapaṇapa, son of Chōḷabōva.

cells.location: Parigi †
cells.place: On a stone lying in the place of Vēṇugōpālasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Broken. States that Veṅkaṭapatirāyadēva-Mahārāya granted a wet field as a sarvamānya to the spearman Vobaḷēsa.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the north of the village of Utkuru.
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Registers that a certain Palage Nāgiyaṇa, son of Nāgi, died in the battle of Ramadi (a village in Agaḷi-nāḍu) in which were engaged Nītimārga-Vemmaḍi and Bīra-Noḷamba. This stone (kulisagallu) was set up by Bāsaka, the wife of the hero and the daughter of Āyta of the Kaḍambas. The engraving (?) was done by Koṅga.

cells.location: Kotnuru
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Relates that this temple of Sañjīvarāya of Koṭnūru was constructed by Narapa-Reḍḍi for the merit of his mother.

cells.location: Kotipi
cells.place: On a Nandi-pillar set up near the Āñjanēyasvāmin temple
cells.date: Śaka 1354, Paridhāvi, Kārtika, śu. di. 1, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records the remission of the marriage tax on all castes, at Koṭapi. The curious benediction at the end states that the married people who go round this Nandi (bull), will be blessed with many children.

cells.place: On a boulder in a field below the tank bund in the same village.
cells.remarks: Bears the sentence ‘Svasti śrī Mandachariya bhasam sandudu’: “Hail ! the speech of the blessed Mandachari has proved true.” On another part of the stone are three lines of writing not quite legible. The first line seems to contain the name Charurasibhandirar for Charurāsi-Paṇḍita, the title of a particular order of Jaina monks (see Ep. Carn., Vol. II, p. 61).

cells.location: Gollapuram
cells.place: On a broken pillar lying in front of the Īśvara temple
