cells.remarks: Records sarvamanya grants of Vagaikulam, Sengulam, Avišagapperi, Arppanāngulam, belonging to the north-east hamlet of Rajaraja-obaturvēdimatgalam, Iluppaikkurichi, and others, made by a Pāndya king in Śaka 1408, corresponding to Kollam 661, Puratṭadi 20, ba. di. saptami, Tuesday, Mrigaśīrsha and during the reigns of Mallikarjuna, Virūpaksha, Krishnaraya and Viramārtāṇa, for daily worship, monthly and annual festivale, offerings and other requirements, to the temple of Nayinar-Nārumpūnkondaruliya-Tambirānar at Dakshipakaśi alias Putārjunastītala, in Mulli-nādu. Relates to the grants made in No. 1 above.

cells.date: Śaka 1617, Kollam 871, Ađi 11, 6u. di. dašami, Thursday, Anu-ham.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Sattivađa in Erada-vishaya, to Ganapati-Nayaka, the grandson of Ganapati, a resident of the village Valutavuru in Kaṅchideśa.

Records the gift of the village Vīruḷ-Koḍiḷi in Vārahāvarttani, to Nārāyaṇan, son of Kēśava-bhaṭṭa and Nārāyaṇanman of the Kāśyapa-gōtra, who were residents of the village Kalipūre. The king was crowned in Śaka 992, on Jēshṭha, Śubha, Ashṭamī, Siṁha-lagna, Thursday with Uttara-Phal.
States that the three villages Paṭugrāma, Hopōḍa-grāma and Mōrkhinī were together formed into Vānya-agrahāra and granted to a certain Erapa-Nāyaka, the son of Māñchi-Nāyaka of the Vaiśya caste.

Registers the gift of the village of Sellada in the Rājāvaṭṭana-viṣhaya, to Koṇḍaman-dēva, son of Nārāyaṇa-bhaṭṭa, a resident of Taḷagrāma, for worship, offerings and lamps of the goddess Bhagavatī of that (i.e., Sellada) village and for the repair of the temple.
Records the gift of the village Virintjika in the Pushkaripi-vishaya to four brothers.
Appears to record a gift of land in Kantaka-vartani-vishaya.

States that the five hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvula granted as sarvamānya, the exemption of the tolls, suñka, magame and birana, on 50 packages on bullooks, buffaloes or assess to a certain Malli-Seṭti, for having constructed the temple of Gannapēsvara at Nelloripaṭṭana surnamed Abhinava-Dvārāvati and Chikk-Ayyāvoje.

Grant of the privilege to trade in certain articles without paying duty, to a certain Puliy-ma-Setti for having killed Karapaka-la Kati-Nayaka who had become a traitor to the samayave, by the merchants of the eight-een-thousand of all countries (residing) in Nandyala-sthala.

Records a grant similar to the above by the same body of merchants to a certain Attena, son of Loki-Setti for having killed Annamaraja and Sitigaraja the sunka-karanas (toll-accountants) of Cheruvuru in Pedakanti-didu.

Only the second and last plates of the set are given. It records the grant of the village Kondavalli or Bhargavapuri to a person named Krishnadava-Maharayammavaru in Hapuru-sima which belonged to the Nellore-valita in the Udayachala-rajya to a number of Brahmans whose names are not given in the record.

cells.location: Tagarapuram — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: COIMBATORE DISTRICT, KOLLEGAL TALUK. On a slab set up near the Maramman temple
cells.date: Śaka 1437, Bhava, Chaitra, ba. di. 5, Friday.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Tagarūru to Sōmayya-Gōpaya, son of Bālagōpa of Bālagōpa of Nōgūru by Sāluva-Gōvindarāja, with the consent of his younger brother the Mahāpradhāna (prime minister) Sāluva Timmarasa, under the orders of the king. The king is stated to be the son of Kathāri-Sāluva Narasimhadēva-Mahārāja, the lord of the Southern Ocean. The donee's grandfather Sōmēśvarabhaṭṭa, also called Mallikārjuna, was the guru of Vīra-Rudru, the lord of the town of Ōrun.

cells.place: On a stone oil-mill set up in a field near the same village (as Maramman temple). †
cells.date: Bhāva, Srashṭhi, (Jyēshṭha), ba. di. 9, Jivavāra [i.e., Friday].
cells.remarks: Gives the names of several persons that set up a nandi-pillar and an oil-mill. On the reverse is given the name of Sōmappa the son of Bēlaladēva [i.e., the king?].

cells.place: On a slab lying by the side of the road from Kollegal to Mudigundam.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Refers to a tax-free dēvadāna, to the temple of Śrī-Vīra-Ballāḷadēvar Pēriyadēva-Nāyaka (by the resident?) of the village.

cells.location: Lokkanahalli
cells.place: On a broken hero-stone lying near the Uttamamman temple
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Kōḍuga knocked down his own head and died. Mention is made of a certain Rachamanna and his wife Bā[jūle].

cells.place: On a stone lying near Uttamamman temple. †
cells.remarks: In arohaṇa characters. This is the nisidhi set up by Doramma in memory of his father Jaigēva Basavayya who took the sanyāsa and fulfilled the vows.

cells.location: Nandi-Bēvuru — Karnataka
cells.place: BELLARY DISTRICT, HARAPANAHALLI TALUK. On a slab set up near the Aḍḍanēyasvāmin temple
cells.date: Śaka 976, Jaya, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, Sunday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 201: Trailōkyamalladēva.]
cells.remarks: Registers that while Trailōkyamala-No[lamba-Pall]ava-Permanadi was ruling the No[lambavadi] 32,000, Ballakunde [300] and Kodambaļi 1,000, the 120 mashajanas of Rechohūru, granted for the worship of Jina, a garden, a wet field, 5 houses and one oil-mill, to a certain Ashṭopavāsi-Bhaļa of Dēsiga-Gaṇa. The record mentions Jagadēkamalla-No[lamba-Brahmadhiraja] as a subordinate of the chief mentioned above. On the back of the slab is a partly damaged record of the same period, referring to a grant made to Ashṭopavāsi-muni at Baihūru. A certain Viranandi-siddhanti is mentioned.

cells.place: On a beam of the Kaḷḷēśvarasvāmin temple in the same village (as Aḍḍanēyasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Nandiyā-Bēvuru for the lamps to the temple of Lakaḷmmēśvara of the same village. The gift was made for the merit of Bhikshā-vṛitti-Ayya by the son of Vīrappa, the lord of Ōrēya.

cells.place: On a slab lying in a field to the north of the same village (as Kaḷḷēśvarasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land to a private individual by the Mahā-janas and others for the construction of a car to the temple of Basavanna.

cells.location: Bennehalli
cells.place: On a pillar in the madhya-mandapa of the Pampapatisvami temple
cells.remarks: Registers gift of lands in the villages Holagundhe, Morigere, and Rajana-Bennevini, by the Mahamandaleshvara (the king's subordinate) Vira-Ramachandradeva. The donor is said to have propagated the new Pasupata-samaya and to have been the President of the 77 (?) (saptahattari) sthanas and the chakravarti of the 7 crore samayas of Kogali 500.

cells.place: On another pillar in Pampapatisvami temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 18 guttaras of money and 1 mattar of land by the rajaguru Vithava Vitavahi (i.e., Hitavahi ?) to the temple of the 12 Brahmanas of the agrahara of Byanamahal for a water-shed in the agrahara (i.e., market place).

cells.place: On a pillar in the front mandapa of Pampapatisvami temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the gift of the village of Bennevaru to the temple of Virupaksha.

cells.place: On another pillar in the same Hoyala mandapa, Pampapatisvami temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the tax millage, the taxes on looms, oil mills, the five artisan classes and the taxes on the minor communities, by Uttavaka-Heggade and Janayya-Heggade for feeding the feeding Brahmanas in the temple of Virupakshadeva.

cells.place: On the slab of Pampapatisvami †
cells.date: Chitrabhanu, Bhadrapada, ba. 1, Thursday. Chitrabhanu, 11th year, Shukla Chaitra, su. amavasya, Monday, Uttarayanu-sankranti.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of a cow and a buffalo, for offerings and lamps and for feeding 12 mahajanas in the temple of Virupakshadeva at Banavaru, by Giripayya, the keeper (upagra) of the good buffaloes.

cells.location: Bennehalli
cells.place: On the slab of Pampapatisvami †
cells.date: Chitrabhanu, Bhadrapada, ba. 1, Thursday. Chitrabhanu, 11th year, Shukla Chaitra, su. amavasya, Monday, Uttarayanu-sankranti.
cells.remarks: Seems to record a gift to the temple of Virupaksha at Banavaru by the members of the district assembly (mahanadu) and the whole village of Banavaru.

cells.place: On a slab set up in Pampapatisvami temple. †
cells.date: Chitrabhanu, Bhadrapada, ba. 1, Thursday. Chitrabhanu, 11th year, Shukla Chaitra, su. amavasya, Monday, Uttarayanu-sankranti.
cells.remarks: Records that the Mahamandaleshvara Jagadkamalla Vira-Pandyadeva, ruling the Nonambavadi 52,000 from his capital Uchchangi, granted a vritti to the 12 Brahmanas of the brahmapuri (Brahman village) of Benneganuru, to the ascetics, etc., of the temple of Svayambhudeva at the village, while over the Koturu 12 and Kogali 500, the Mahamandaleshvara Vira-Ballaladeva, lord of Banavasi was ruling from Kotturu. Mention is made of the Abhinava-Pasupata teacher Lakulisa, Vidyarati-Pandita, Dharmaradi-Pandita and Chandrarasi the contemporary of the donor.

cells.place: On a pillar lying near the Kalleshvarasvami temple at Bada, a hamlet of Bennehalli.
cells.date: 7th year, Raktakshi, Prathama Sravana, Purnime, Sravana, Purnime, Saka 10[9]6, Jaya, Prathamashada, Sravana, Purnime, Lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the gift of a matha by a chief of Bada to the temple of Nonambesvara (i.e., Nonambesvara or Nojambavara) at Harihara-kattara, a certain Nopambakravarti.

cells.place: On another pillar in the place of Kalleshvarasvami †
cells.date: 7th year, Raktakshi, Prathama Sravana, Purnime, Sravana, Purnime, Saka 10[9]6, Jaya, Prathamashada, Sravana, Purnime, Lunar eclipse. [date-calculation appendix, No. 212: Śaka 10[0]95, Jaya, Prathamāshāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, Puṇṇama, lunar eclipse. = A.D. 1173, June 27, Wednesday; ·13; f.d.n. ·72. There was a lunar eclipse on that day.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to the same temple by a certain Nopambakravarti.

cells.location: Kuruvatti
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kallēśvarasvāmin temple
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 24 Pramādhi, Jēshṭha, śu. Paurṇamāsi, Sunday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers grant of land and taxes on grass, firewood, vegetables, fruits and cotton exported to and imported from Kuruvatti together with money for offerings, and for feeding ascetics in the temple of Abhinava-Sōmēśvara at Kuruvatti. The donor of the village and Kalidāsa, its chief. The village belonged to the Beṇṇevūru 12 which was ruled by Surēśvara-Paṇḍita-dēva, Laṅkēśvara-Paṇḍita whose santāna, i.o., spiritual descent is given in the record was present at the ceremony of grant

cells.place: On a slab set up in the Mallikārjunasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 29, Tāraṇa, Vaiśākha, śu. tadige, Sunday.
cells.remarks: States that the mahājanas of the agrahāra Gaṇḍarādityana-Hoḷaḷ, having complained to the emperor (chakravartti) that Māyidēva, son of the late Hēgāḍe Būchimayya was plundering all properties of the said Hēgāḍe and his family, had the emperor sent for Boppayya, chastised him and took from him an undertaking that he and his successors should secede from the government of Hoḷaḷu. The chief did accordingly in the presence of the thirty-two thousand (representatives) of Beṇṇevūru 12, Niruṅguṇḍa 2, Baḍah-guḷi, Māṅgoḷa, Bidirahaḷḷi, Hābanūru, Honnavatti, Kuru-vaṭṭi and Mūguḷi and drank water at the temple of Tripurāntakadēva.

cells.place: On a beam in the same temple
cells.date: Śaka 1104, Plava, Pushya, ba. di. 3, Friday, Saṅkramaṇa.
cells.remarks: Record that, while the chief was governing the Beṇṇevūru 70 and Beṇṇevūru 12, his minister (pradhāna) Sōgaya-Daṇṇāyaka, on the sanction of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vijaya-Pāṇḍyarasu, renewed, in the presence of the mahā-janas of Kuruvatti and Bācharasa of Beṇṇevūru, the grant of 70 mattar of lands originally made to the temple of Ahavamallēśvara by the elder (hiriya) Vikramāditya.

cells.location: Kuruvatti
cells.place: Do. on the same beam
cells.remarks: States that the five hundred svāmis of Ayyāvaḷe, the nānādēśi, the settis, etc., having assembled mahā-nāḍu at Kuruvatti granted the Bejjunha tax to Lōkābharaṇa-Muni for the worship of the god Ahavamallēśvara.

cells.location: Kuruvatti
cells.place: Do. on the same beam
cells.king: Pratāpachakravartin Vīra-Baḷḷāḷadēva, ‘residing at his palace at Baguḷi.’
cells.date: Śaka 1117, Ānanda, Chaitra, śu. Paḍi-va (prathama), Friday.
cells.remarks: Gift, by the king, of the village Baḍahad Mukhunabbe in Beṇṇevūru 12, to Lōkābharaṇa-Munindra, for repairs, offerings and festivals to the temple of Ahavamallēśvara.

cells.location: Kuruvatti
cells.place: Do. on the same beam
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Baḍa and lands in Beṇṇevūru 12 for repairs to the temple of Ahavamallēśvara, by the Mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Vīra-Gāmādēva, the subordinate of the king. The donor is described as the lord of Dvārāvatī and the noon of the Yādava family.

cells.place: On another beam
cells.remarks: Registers gift, by purchase, of land to the temple of Ahavamallēśvara, by two settis.

cells.place: On the wall to the right of the southern entrance into Mallikārjunasvāmin temple. †
cells.date: 15th year, Krōdhana, Jeshṭa Paurṇami, Sunday, Lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land to the rajaguru Lōkabharavadeva for offerings to the temple of Ānjanāyanadēva at Hirya-Kuruvatti, surnamed Dakshina-Varanasi by Bhandari Sōva-rama, the Mahapradhana of the chief queen, Padumaladēvi. The Mahapradhana was in charge of the Guttolala-nādu. Below this, in slightly smaller characters of the same period, is a completely worn-out record.

cells.place: On the wall of Mallikārjunasvāmin †
cells.date: 7th year, Piṅgala, Jeshṭa, su. Punṇami, Monday, Lunar olipse, Vyatipaat saṅkramaṇa.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of income from taxes, tolls and oil-mills, for the lamp to the rajaguru's temple, by the Maha-pradhana Uttarakha-Heggade and Mahadeva-Danna-yaka of Arasiyakere and the Heggade Jannayya. The donor is the rajaguru Lōkabharava-gurudeva.

cells.location: Haluvagalu
cells.place: On a slab set up in the courtyard of the Ānjanāyanasvāmi temple
cells.date: Āsaka ..... Sōbhakrit, Āāvija, su di. 15, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Damāged. Seems to register the terms of a lease (cowl) in respect of a shop built at Haluvagilu. Mentions Mahanayakachārya Hasavappa-Nāyaka of ĵaguli and his mother Niochhava (Niochavava).

cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Ānjanāyanasvāmi. †
cells.date: Śaka 13[11], Vibha-va, Jēshṭha, su. di. 1, Friday.
cells.remarks: Registers the setting up of a Nann-pillar in the sante-pēṭe (market place) at Haluvagalu by the Aivole [seṭṭis] and the mummuri-dandas of the several places like Hastināvati, Holekere, Harahara, Bāda, Hemavati, Karapura, Bēharu, Kavina-Hadagali, Holabali in the Pange-nādu.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the Kallēśvara-svāmi temple in the same village (as Ānjanāyanasvāmi temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 120[4], Chitrabhānu, Vaiśākha, su. di. 14, Monday, Svāti, Vyatīpāta-yōga.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land to the temple of Jigarasi, for repairs and offering to the temple of Svayambhu-Kali-nātha, at Haluvagalu, by Vasudēva, the chief of the village, under orders of Haridēva who was the adhikari of Pandi-nādu and a subordinate of the commander-in-chief and Mahapradhana Rāmachandra.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in Kallēśvara-svāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Refers to the death of a hero in a fight.

cells.place: On a broken slab set up in a field to the north of the same village (as Kallēśvara-svāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: A much mutilated and damaged fragment in archaic characters of about the 8th century A.D.

cells.location: Teligi
cells.place: On a slab in a private house
cells.remarks: Gift of land by two individuals of Teligi-Duggati-nādu to a charanti (Jaṅgama disciple). Mentions the towns Kalburigi, Nsgara and Ānegondi. The characters are too modern for the date given.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Hari-harēśvarasvāmi temple in the same village (as Kallēśvara-svāmi temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 959, Pramādi, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṁ-krānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 228: Śaka 959, Pramādhi, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti. The reckoning of Pramāthin is by northern cycle. A.D. 1037 = Pramāthi (N. cycle).]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a gift of land to a ganda at Teligi situated in Bikkiga 70, by Jagadēkamalla-Nojamba-Pallava-Permānadi ruling the Nolambavādi 32,000, Kōgali 500, Ballakunde 300, Karuvidi 30 and Paravi 70.

cells.location: Duggavati
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Īśvara temple
cells.date: Āsaka 1049, Parabbava, Pushya, su. Padiva, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkramaṇa.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land and an oil-mill for a lamp and of tax (perjjunka) on the oil-mill, for the temple of Īśvaradēva at Bammadeva-Navaha, by the chief of Duggati in Bakkiga 70 near Kōgali 500, Maha-Vaddavyavahāri Nambigunni-seṭṭi and others. Also registers gift of money for a lamp officer in charge of the land-tax and the Mahapradhana, Dandanāyaka Chodadhara, the officer in charge of the hojjunka tax, in Kadambige 1,000 and Kēgali 500.

cells.location: Tumbigere
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Iśvara temple
cells.king: Jagadēkamalla-Nirnamadi-Nojamba-Pallava-Permānadi †
cells.date: 6th year of the Chālukya Vikrama era, Durmati, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti †
cells.remarks: Registers that while Jagadēkamalla-Nirnamadi-Nojamba-Pallava-Permānadi was ruling the Kōgali 500, Balla-gālli 300 and Kārviḍi 30 from his residence at Gan-gāvi, his subordinate Gangarāja-Nāyaka granted lands for offerings to the temple of Mahādēva at Tumbigere in Bikkiga 70 and to the ascetics of a matha in the same place. At the end is another inscription dated in the 6th year of the Chālukya Vikrama era, Durmati, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, recording a monthly grant of 1 peru (bundle) of betel leaf for a lamp to the same deity by Chāvarayya-Nāyaka, son of (Hugguriya Māchiheṭṭi in charge of the pannāya tax, Daṇḍanāyaka Mājamayya and Sambiyappa.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near Iśvara temple. †
cells.date: Kaḷayukti, Śrāvaṇa, ba. di. 1, Wednes-day. [date-calculation appendix, No. 231: 1918-1919]
cells.remarks: Records that this hero-hand (vīragal) was granted in memory of the death of a certain Kuruḷa by Sākarasa, an officer of the Mahāpradhāna and Sarvādhikāri Kāli-dāsa-Jīya, the headman and all the inhabitants of the village.

cells.location: Rāgina-salavāḍa
cells.place: On a stone set up near the Añjana-yāsvamin temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the Mahājanasvakyabhāgali Bāsa-vappa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the ruined Sasa-vēśvara temple in the same village (as Iśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged and mutilated. Mentions the Muḷāmaṇḍaladēva Tribhuvanamalla-Paṇḍyadēva, 'Lord of Kaḷāvipura' who was ruling Noḷambavāḍi 32,000 and Gaṅgāvāḍi 96,000.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Iśvara temple in the same village (as Sasa-vēśvara temple). †
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 52, Pla-vaṅga, Āshāḍha, amāvāsya, Sun-day, Dakshiṇā-yaṇa-Saṅkrā-maṇa, Vyatīpāta.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant, of two panas per month out of the vaddarāvula tax and out of the pannaya tax in Mosalevida to the god Ratnabhūshapa-Vinayaka by Herggade Vujibhaṭṭayya under the orders of the Mahāpradhāna Indarāṇa-Bhaṭṭayyain charge of the vaddarāvula tax and land-tax of the Nolambavađi 32,000 as the subordinate of the Mahāpradhāna and Kannada-sandhivigrahi Bhōga-Bhaṭṭayya who was enjoying the vaddarāvula (tax) of the 7½ lac (country) and Banavase 12,000. Registers also grant of money by the Mahadaṇdaṇayaka Cholāṇdadēva, the lord of the Nolambavađi 32,000 and by the members of the Vira-Baṇañja sect to the same temple.

cells.location: Satturu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kāḷlēśva-rasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records that, while Jagadekamalla-Nanni-Nolamba-Pallava-Permamāidēva was ruling the Kogali 500, Kadambalike 1,000, Ballakunde 800 and Kaneyakallu 300, Sōvimayya, the chief of Sattiyūru and Kupparasa of the Yadaya family, belonging to Masavađi 140 granted land for a lamp to the temple of Mahadēva at Sattiyūru.

cells.location: Kanchikera
cells.place: On a slab set up near the ruined Mandapa-matha
cells.king: Jagadekamalla-Nolamba-Nolamba-Pallava-Permanadi †
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of a linga and the grant of land to it by a sandhivigrahi while Bāchimayya was ruling Gañchikere under Jagadekamalla-Nanniya-Nolamba-Pallava-Permmāna[di], the overlord of Kōguļi 500 and Kadanubali 1,000.

cells.location: Alagillavada
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kālidēvara temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the king's feudatory Permaḍi-Dayadānatka, the later's subordinate Pègguḍe Dasimayya and Barmadēva.

cells.place: On a broken slab set up near Kaḷḷēśvara temple. †
cells.king: Vira-Pāṇḍyadēva †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Register gift of a garden to the villagers of Aragilvāda by the Mahāmandaleśvara Vira-Pandydāva, ruling the Nonambavadi 32,000 and his queen Vijayadēvi.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near the place of Kaḷḷēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Records the death of Haripi-Seṭti, brother of Banajiga Singayya of Hojalakere in a fight during the capture of Aragiluvāda.

cells.location: Kunchuru
cells.place: On a broken slab set up near the Mallikārjunēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Mutilated and incomplete. Registers gift of garden land to [the temple] at Maṭṭamāra by Vira-Pāṇḍyadēva and Vijayādēvi.

cells.place: On another slab in the place of Mallikārjunadēva †
cells.remarks: Mutilated and incomplete. Mentions the Mahāmandaleśvara Tribhuvanamalla-[Vira-Pandya].

cells.place: On a pillar in Mallikārjunadēva temple †
cells.date: 15th year, Sarvajit, Śrāvaṇa, śu. di. 15, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 242: 15th year, Sarvajit, Śrāvaṇa, śu. di. 15, Monday. 15th year of Ramachandra's reign was A.D. 1285, while Sarvajit was A.D. 1287-88. In A.D. 1286, on Monday August 5, Śrāvaṇa śu. 15 ended at ·84.]
cells.remarks: Registers grant of a śrōtra to Kalleya-jiya Haripa-jiya for offerings to the temple of Mallikarjuna at Mattavūru by the sarvyadhikari Jakkarasa under the orders of Lingadēva-Raneya, son of Jajjigidēva.

cells.place: On a pillar in the Āñjanēyasvāmi temple in the same village (as Mallikārjunadēva temple). †
cells.date:
10th year, Pramādi,
Āshāḍha, ba. di.
10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 243: 10th year, Pramāthī, Āshāḍha, ba. di. 10, Monday. In A.D. 1279 = Pramāthī, Āshāḍha ba. 10 fell on Wednesday. In A.D. 1280, the same tithi fell on Sunday; and in A.D. 1281 on Saturday.]
cells.remarks: Registers a nirmālyagrant to the temple of Srayambhu Kal-ināladēva, by the Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Manneya Nāchidēvarāyiu, of Hulasugalu and Malkiya, the chief of Kuruvala.

cells.place: On a broken slab set up near the Kaḷḷēśvarasvāmi temple in the same village (as Mallikārjunadēva temple). †
cells.remarks: Mutilated and incomplete. Mentions the Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Tribhuvanamalla-Pāṇḍyadēva and his subordinate Iruṅgarasa of Koḷchapura.

cells.location: Yarabalu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kniḷaēvarasvāmi temple
cells.date: Gh. Vik. 47, Subhakrit, [Pa] u ālaya, śu. di. 7, Saturday, Uttarāyane-Saṁkrānti, Vyatīpata. [date-calculation appendix, No. 245: 6th year, Simha, śn. di. 1, Sunday, Makhā. Proceeding as above, we have, as the equivalent of the present date, Sunday, August 7, A.D. 1328, on which day śu. 1 ended at ·18; but here again the Nakshatra "Makha" had ended at ·68 on the previous day. We might suppose a different system of reckoning Nakshatras : but neither Garga nor Brahma-siddhānta yields a different result.]
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Registers gift of land for offerings to the temple of Mahādēva at Kramahāluva by Machabhōva and Siṅgabōva, while the Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Tribhuvanamalla Pāṇḍyadēva was ruling the Noṇambavāḍi 32,000.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near the Kallēśvarasvāmi temple at Nitturu.
cells.remarks: Records that the hero-stone was set up by Kalloju in memory of his father, Masaṇōja, the carpenter of Nachararasa of Holavālu who died in the battle of Kadiirimidi.

cells.location: Kaḍatī
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in the Iśvara temple
cells.date: 1[2]th year, Chitrabhānu, Vaiśakha, ba. di. 2, Sunday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 247: 12th year, Chitrabhānu, Vaiśākha, ba. di. 2, Sunday. In A.D. 1282 (= Chitrabhānu), on Sunday, April 26, Vaiśākha ba. 2 ended at 55.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the death of a hero.

cells.place: On another hero-stone in the place of Īśvara. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to the death of Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Goḍati Chaṭṭaranı.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the place of Īśvara. †
cells.remarks: Damaged and mutilated. Registers grant of land to a matha, temple and ascetics by a certain Chikarasa [in the presence] of Kriyāśakti-paṇḍita.

cells.place: On a nandī-pillar et up by the side of the road from Guṇḍagaṭṭi to Eḍehalli.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers grant of land to Śivāmāya-Nāyaka, chief of Guṇḍagaṭṭi in Bikkiga 70 for the requirements of the temple of Aditya.

cells.location: Guṇḍagaṭṭi
cells.place: On a nandī-pillar lying near the Muktēśvara temple
cells.date: Śaka 985, Sot hakrit, Paushya, śu. di. 2, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a gift of land by Cheṭṭaya-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a broken slab lying near the Īśvara temple in the same village (as Muktēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Mutilated. Mentions the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vīra-Pāṇḍyadēva who was ruling the Noḷambavāḍi 32,000.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Bhāgyēśvara temple at Taḷavagaḷu, hamlet of Guṇḍagaṭṭi.
cells.date: Śuka 955, Bhava, Paushya, śu. di. 1, Wednesday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land for offerings and other requirements to the temple of Bhogéśvara at Talavage in Bikkiga 70 which was a district of Koṇaļi 500, by Jagadēkamalla [Uda] yadityadēva-Nojamba-Pallava-Permānadi, who was ruling the Nojambavādi 32,000, Kadambalige 1,000, Koṇaļi 600, Ballakunde 300, Harage 70 and Karividi 30.

cells.place: On the slab of Bhāgyēśvara †
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land to the temple of Bhōgēśvara having died, Chikka-Gauḍa, the sixty tenants and others appointed an other in his place.

cells.location: Kaḷḷahaḷḷi
cells.place: On a slab set up in the backyard of a house
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Bassava-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Manneramassalavāḍa
cells.place: On a slab set up on the site of a ruined matha
cells.date: Śaka 1219. Hēmaṇambi (Hēvilambi), Margaśira, śu. di. 5, 1 hurs-day. [date-calculation appendix, No. 256: Śaka 1219, Hēmanambi, Mārgaśira, śu. di. 5, Thursday. In A.D. 1297, Mārgaśira śu. 5 fell on Wednesday, November 5, and it ended at ·83; but in A.D. 1296 (= Durmukha) Adhika Mārgaśirsha, śu. 5 fell on Thursday, November 1 and it ended at ·73.]
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land to Vinayachandradēva, disciple of Bhaṭṭāraka-Ravich of the Mūlasaṅgha, Dēśiga-gaṇa and Mūlabhadra-gachchha, by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Bhairavadevarasa, the gauḍas and o'hers, for offerings, etc., to the Jina temple at Mova levāḍa which was repaired by Kesava-Paṇḍita, son of Sāvanta-Paṇḍita, the prime-minister of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Salaveya Tilamādova Rāpeya.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the Kallēśvarasvāmin temple in the same village (as Bhāgyēśvara temple). †
cells.date: 4th year corresponding to Śōbhakṛt, Jēshṭha, Paurṇami and the lunar eclipse †
cells.remarks: Records the revival of old grants and gift of fresh lands for offerings to the temple of Mulasthanadēva by the Mahāmaṇdalésvara Vikramādityarasa in charge of Mosaļevaṇa 12, Heggaṇe Aichana and others while the Mahāmaṇdalésvara Vijaya-Pāṇdyadēva was ruling Koṇaļi 500 and Noṇambavādi 32,000. The record is dated in the 4th year corresponding to Solbhakrit, Jeshṭa, Punnime and the lunar eclipse of Rāyanārāyaṇa Āhayamalladēva of the Kaṇaḥuri family.

cells.place: On a slab set up near Kallēśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 958, 1bhatu, Kārttika, śu. pāñiva, Sunday, Solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Records that Ayyana-Bhivajigarasa, Mara-Gāvūṇa and others granted lands in the presence of Gurudēva who was ruling that village, to the same temple of Kalidēva at Mosaļevaṇi in Koṇaļi 500, while Nojamba-Pallava-Permānadi was ruling the [Koṇaļi] 500, Kadambalige 1,000 and Ballakunde 300.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near the Kallāvarasvāmin temple at Basarakoduchchanahalli of Sivagangahalli.
cells.remarks: Mutilated and damaged. Mentions Kocharideva.

cells.location: Hagarānuru
cells.place: On a slab upin a field near the tank bund
cells.date: Šuka [14] 69, Pluvaṅga, Kartika, sū. di. 2, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of the village Ānura [gate] in Kolūrāl-sīma to a matha at Mayūra by Channapa-Nayaka, son of Tammanna-Nayaka, with the merit of Krishnapa-Nayaka, son of Bayapa-Nayaka.

cells.location: Chīgateri
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in the courtyard of the Ramalingasvāmin temple
cells.date: Šuka 1132, Šukla, Jeshṭa, sū di. 5, Sunday
cells.remarks: Highly damaged.

cells.location: Musuvanahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kāḷi[ka]varṇasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Registers gift of a part of the village of Kalahalī by Rājōji-Nayaka for the merit of the king.

cells.location: Alaburu
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Honnattiyamman temple
cells.remarks: Records gift of land to the shrine of the 'goddess Honnakalī' at Ahāburu by Krishnappa, son of Basavapa-Nayaka, the olaganāyaka of the king.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Rāma-liṅgasvāmi temple in the same village (as Honnati-yamma temple). †
cells.date: 10th year, Prabhava, Paushya, sū. di. 4, 1 hursday, Uttarayana-Saṅkrānti, Vyatipata.
cells.remarks: Records the event in the presence of Vamadeva-Paṇḍita, the disciple of Kalēśvara-Paṇḍideva, of Muda for worship and offerings to the temple of Sṛiyaṅkamuḷḷa-mahā-jana by the 84 mahājanas of Alambura while the mahamaṇḍalēśvara Nachchōdarasa, the subordinatio of the Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Pratāpa-Jagadēkamalla-Pāṇḍyadēva who was ruling the Nolambavādi 32,000, was in charge of Kōgali 500.

cells.place: On a stone lying in a field to the north of the village of Maiduru.
cells.remarks: Highly damaged. Mentions Basappa-Nayaka. Much damaged.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in the court-yard of the Iśvara temple in the same village (as Rāma-liṅgasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On a slab set up on a vacant site in the [ta]lavara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Records the remission of taxes on the barbers of Maiduru in Kōttūru-sīme.

cells.location: Muttigi
cells.place: On a pedestal of the god in the Kīmarāmasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Records that the imago of Kinnakranavani was consecrated by Yarapa-gauda, the gauda of Muttage, for the prosperity of his family.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the manor temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1136, Dhātu, Vaiśākha, śu. di. 1, Monday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: The slab is highly worn out. Seems to register a gift of land for the maintenance of a water-shed at Muttage in the Pūṇya 30, a subdivision of Kōgali 500 by the chief ṇippayya of the village.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Ajanaya-svāmi temple in the same village (as Kumaṇaravāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions a certain Krishnapa-Nayaka.

cells.place: On a hero-stone set up in a field to the west of the village of Kadabageri.
cells.remarks: Refer to the victorious death of Maleya, son of Mudadah Doṇayya, the garuḍa of Kalkeravādi, in a fight with Nanniṅga, son of Yajjayya-Pallava of Nolambavādi, while the Mahāsāmanta, Biijja[ṇa] was ruling the Kōgali 500 and Maṇiyavādi 140.

cells.place: On another hero-stone in the place of Ajanaya-svāmi. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the south of Kasavanahalli, hamlet of Kaḍūru.
cells.date: Śaka 1581, Vikāri, Phālguṇa, śu. di. 3, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records gift of land by Bāguli Basavappa-Nāyaka to Sībappa son of Basavappa and grandson of Gōmallappa for the merit of the village.

cells.location: Arasikere
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field near the tank bund
cells.date: Śaka 1583, Plava, Mārgasira, śu. di. 5, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Records gift of land by Bāguli Basavappa-Nāyaka to Basavappa, son of Sīva-Mallappa and grandson of [Sa]-mita-Rāvuta of Arasikere-Mutige.

cells.location: Nichchavahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Āñjanēyasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Registers gift of the village Nichchapura by the Mahanāyakachārya Bagali Basavapa-Nayaka to Subedar Līṅgappa for his valuable service to the state in getting the tribute paid to the Hindu king reduced from 10,000 varahas to 8,000 varahas by obtaining the consent of Abdul Nabikhan for building Hosapēte and causing the reduction of the rent to 6,000 varahas.

cells.location: Hosakote
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Āñjanēyasvāmi temple
cells.date: Śaka 1434, Ura-jōtpaṭṭa, Pauṣya, ba. di. 30, Amāvāsya.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the agrahāra of Bakkasagara to Channabasayya, son of Vithamayya, the sthānīka of the temple of Hariharadēva, by Haridāsa-Raṇuta, son of Rāmappa-Raṇuta, the chief of the Toraṭaga[lu] fort.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the Īśvara temple at Guḍihalli, hamlet of Hosakote.
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 36, Kārttika, śu. di. 11, Sunday, Uttara-rāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti
cells.remarks: Registers grant of lands by the Mahāsāmanta, Singarasa, the son of Kūmararasa and Chaṭṭabbe, ruling Koṅgal-nāḍ 800 and Nolambavāḍi 32,000 for the offerings, etc., to the temple of the grandfather was Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara-Dēvarasa and the grant was made in the presence of Vārasvara-Paṇḍita a disciple of Vārasakti-Paṇḍita whose preceptor was Dīryasakti-Paṇḍita.

cells.place: On another slab in the place of Īśvara. †
cells.date: Śaka 987, Viśvāvasu, Pauṣya, śu. saptamī, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti
cells.remarks: Registers the village of Kaḍalora in the district of Murttage 30 in Kōgali 500 by Bijjaladēva, for worship, offerings, etc., to the temple of Nolambēśvara at Arasiyabīḍu, for feeding ascetics and for education, while he was ruling as Yuvarāja-Vijayāditya, ruling Kadambali 1,000, Kōgali 500 and the land of 300 was encamped at this place on his way for the conquest of the south, under the orders of the king.

cells.place: On a third slab in the place of Īśvara. †
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 37 Nandana, Pauṣya, śu. di. 11, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the tax called vaddarāvula and two gardens, made in the presence of Varēsvara-Pandita, for festivals and offerings to the temple of Nolambēsvara at Arsiyakere in Murttage 30 a subdivision of Kōgali 500. States that the mahasamantadhipati Anantapālayya was in charge of the same tax over the 7½ lakhs (country), that his subordinate the mahapradhāna Mādirajarasa was in charge of Banavase 12,000, Halsaiga 12,000 and Nolambavadi 82,000 and the latter's subordinate the Dandanāyaka Pāyamarasa was mangsing Nolambavadi 32,000 and that Chamundamayya-Nayaka was, under the orders of the last, in charge of Kadambaļike 1,000 and Kōgali 500.

cells.place: On a pillar in the front mantapa of Īśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Timmanna, son of Rangadasa, ruling over Arasikere, repaired the sluice of the tank in the village, under the orders of Nagara who was governing the Koṭṭūru-sime and was the agent of Rayasa Nagappa, son of Timmanna of the king's gold treasury. The last mentioned is in charge of Nonaban-Amakere in Koṭṭūru-sime.

cells.place: On a slab lying in a field to the south of Anjigere.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings and lamps to the temple of Kalidēva at Kāchegola in Uchohanĝi 30, by Pallava-sāvanta of Asagōdu, a subordinate of the mahapradhana Ammappa-Danpāyaka.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Ittara temple at Srinivasapura hamlet of the same village (as Īśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records gift of land, for offerings and worship, to the temple of Jōgēśvara at Koṭṭūru by Jagadēkamalla-Vira-Pāṇyadēva.

cells.location: Rajabāvanahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Añjanēyasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Records that, under the orders of the king, Hariyaṇṇa, son of Lakkappa gave rent-free lands to Singaṇṇa, son of Vitharru and others for having constructed a tank and founded a village called Hariyaṇṇana-dū [the] to the east of Kambana-Arasikere by reclaiming the forest.

cells.place: On a hero-stone lying in a field to the north of Uohohangidurga.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records the death of a hero in the fort of Uohohangi and the death of Madava who was said to be of the Yadava family and the mahāsāmanta of Ballaha. Kāñchīpuri is mentioned.

cells.place: On the pedestal of a dhvajastambha to the north of the same village (as Ittara temple). †
cells.remarks: States that Saretaya Hiryanna of Tambarahalli set up this lamp-pillar to the goddess Uohohanga.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Taraka-dēvarasvami temple in the same village (as Ittara temple). †
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land and tank in Uohohangi fort made by Bijjaladēva in the presence of Kageyara-Pēḍḍi, to the temple of Galagēśvara while Vishṇuvardhana-Maha-rāja-Vijayādityadēva was ruling Nolambavādi-32,000. Accounts of the four names Meghamatha, Kanakagiri, Uttuṅgaparvata and Uohohangi by which the last mentioned place was called in the Krita, Treta, Dvāpara and Kaliyugas respectively.

cells.location: Bāmaghatta
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kallēśvarasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records a grant of land to the temple at Bāmaghatta by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Tribhuvanamalla-Rāya-Pāṇyadēva made at the request of the commander of the elephant forces in the presence of Harimara who had consecrated with his funds the temple of Rāmeśvara at Trikūṭa. Also registers grant of money for a lamp by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chāṭṭarasa and others.

cells.location: Channahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up near the Añjanēyasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Registers the construction of a tank by the king's Chāṭṭarasa for the merit of the king, of the village of Channahalli situated in the Uohangi-vōye was adyaksara of Visana-rāvatta, son of Murār-ravatta to Nārāyaṇa-Bhaṭṭa, son of Dēvaru-Bhaṭṭa.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kalleśvarasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.date: 6th year, Kabaya, Jeehtha, éu. di. 13, Monday, Lunar eclipse, Vishu-Sankramaya.
cells.remarks: Refers to the construction of an old agrahāra, tank, and the temple of Nöyēśvara and registers a gift of land made to it by some of the Śaiva Brāhmaṇas. Uyyappa, the chief of Puppalura for the celebration of the Śivaratri festivals in the month of Chaitra, lamp, worship and repairs to the temple, by the Daṇḍanāyaka Guṇaya-nāyaka Pāṇḍyadēva, who was ruling over the Uchchhaṁgi-nāḍu for his own merit, and that of Jagadēkamalla-Vīra-Pāṇḍyadēva ruling Nolambavāḍi 32,000. Records also a grant of land for feeding Brāhmaṇas and for the merit of Rāya-Pāṇḍya's deva and Sōvaladevi.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kalleśvarasvāmin temple at Punṇagatta.
cells.date: Saka 974, Nandanam, Pushya, éu. di. 1, Thursday, Uttarayana-Sankranti.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land for offerings to the temple of Mahadēva at Hösagere by Nolamba-Mahādēvi, wife of Trailōkyamalla-deva-Nolamba-Pallava-Permanaḍi-Naranimghudēva.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Kalleśvarasvāmin temple at Nandikamba, hamlet of the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 974, Nandana, Magha, Amāvasyā, Sunday, Uttarāyana-Saṁkrānti.
cells.remarks: Records grant of the village of Pethibeyagatta made in the presence of Sūmēśvara-Pāṇḍya to the temple of Kadamba-Cēśvara, by Kateya Nāśayyarasu, ruling the Kadambalige 1,000 and born in the family of Mayarmanavar.

cells.location: Hire-Mogalagari
cells.place: On a slab set up in the tank-bed
cells.date: Śaka 981, Vikari, Śrāvaṇa, Punṇime, Lunar eclipse, Vishü-Saṁkrānti.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land to the temple of Svayambhū-Kaļlidēva, at Mōgampere by the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siṁgaṇadēva, who was ruling over Uchchhaṁgi 30.

cells.place: On the slab of Kalleśvarasvāmin †
cells.date: Saka 9[8]3, Plava, Jeehtha, Amāvasya, Sunday, Solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Svayambhu-Kalidévasvämi at Meganangere situated in Kadambajike 1,000, by Pergede-Dāṇdanāynaka and Kesimayya-Dāṇdanāyaka.

cells.place: On another slab in the place of Kalleśvarasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentiones the Mahāsamantadhipati Dāṇdanayaka Polamayya. Below this is a damaged record which mentions the king and the Saka year 955, Sīmukha, and which registers a grant of land for offerings and lamps.

cells.place: On the slab of Kalleśvarasvāmin †
cells.king: Jagadēkamalla-Nolamba-Brahmādhỉrāya †
cells.date:
Śaka 975, Vijaya,
Āshāḍha, śu. di.
3, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land to the temple of Svayambhūdeva at Mogampere by Jagadēkamalla-Nolamba-Brahmādhỉrāya.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Rūpeśvarasvāmin temple in the same village (as Kalleśvarasvāmin temple). †
cells.king: Vijaya-Pāṇḍyadēva †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that while the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vijaya-Pāṇḍyadēva the younger brother of Vīra-Pāṇḍya and the son of Rāya-Pāṇḍya by his queen Sōmadēvi was ruling over the Nolambavāḍi 32,000 from his residence at Uchchhaṁgi, his subordinate Gōvindadēva-Daṇḍanāyaka made a grant of land to the temple at Mēgapa [gāri], Vijaya-Pāṇḍya's chief minister was Vanavamumūvenda of Velayambākham.

cells.location: Sirastahalli
cells.place: On a hero-stone set up near the Śaṅkaraliṅgēśvaran temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to state that Ayapayya was ruling Māsavāḍi and Kogali.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the place of Śaṅkaraliṅgēśvaran †
cells.date: Śaka 970, Sarvadhari, Māgha, 6u. di. 6. Sunday, Uttarāyapa-Saṅkrānti.
cells.remarks: Records that while Naraśiṅgbadēva was ruling the Kogali 500, Kadamtalige 1,000, Balakunde 300 and Sindavađi 1,000, Nanniya Butabbarasi, Kekarasa and the 120 maha-janas of Sirivelli granted in the presence of Vidyanidhi-Pandita, disoiple of Tejōnidhi-Pandita, land to the temple of Saṅkharadēva in that village.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Śaṅkaraliṅgēśvaran. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records that Aimmađi-Nolamba was ruling Kogali and Kadambali countries.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Liṅgalayya well in the same village (as Śaṅkaraliṅgēśvaran temple) †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records that the Liṅgalayya well by Bāyakara Rāmappayya for the merit of his son Liṅgalayya.

cells.place: On the slab of Śaṅkaraliṅgēśvaran †
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of Ramayamantri who obtained the government of the Kopdēvidu country from Achyutadēvaraya. His several acts of charity are enumerated such as the building of temples, construction of tanks, etc.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Gōpālakriṣṇasvāmi temple at Timmalapuram (Hospet taluk, Bellary district).
cells.remarks: Registers the construction of the temple of Gōpinātha by Bāyakara Rāmappayya for the merit of his parents Hiriya Timmaraśayya and Hiriya Lakṣmīśamma.

cells.place: On the slab of Gōpālakrishṇasvāmi †
cells.remarks: and Copy of No. 301 above.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Mallikārjuna temple in the same village (as Gōpālakrishṇasvāmi temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers the construction of the temple of Mallikārjuna by Namasivāya, the officer of Bāyakara Rāmappayya, for his own merit.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Śiva temple in the same village (as Mallikārjuna temple). †
cells.remarks: and Copy of No. 301 above.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Śiva temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers the construction of the temple of Rāchēśvara, Ammēśvara and Kṛiṣṇēśvara by Bāyakara Rāmappayya for the merit of his uncle Bācharasayya, his aunt Ammajamme and his brother Kṛiṣṇappa.

cells.place: On the same slab
cells.remarks: and Copy of No. 301 above.

cells.location: Marandai
cells.place: On west wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple
cells.remarks: Damaged and stones missing. Registers a gift of land for offerings, to the temple of Kailasamudaiya Nayaṇar at Marantaya[nalīr] alias Vikrama-Pandyapuram in Mulli-nādu.

cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Records that the temple of Śrikayilāsamudaiyar at Marantayanalīr alias Vikrama-Pandyapuram in Mulli-nādu, was built of stone by a certain Malai-Amuduñ-cheyda-Māni-Paguvayan of Kiliyūr.

cells.place: On the north wall of Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of money (Apu-śechu) for a lamp, by a merchant, and by few other residents of the same temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Gift of money for lamps and offerings to the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Provides for lamps to the shrine of Kuṇamāṛaṇḍa-Piḷḷaiyār in the same temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for offerings to the temple of Tiruvāṇaikkā-Viṉṇagar-Paramāṇiḻaigal at Kaḷakkudi-nallūr a brāhmaṇaya in Kaḷakkudi-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the west wall of Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Stone missing. Seems to register a gift of land for the temple.

cells.place: On the north wall of Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Introduction mentions a gift of land for offerings to the shrine of Viṉayaka-Piḷḷaiyār at Kuṛuchchi alias Vīrakēraḷanallūr situated to the west of Māṛudaṉallūr.

cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Seems to register the assignment of the incomes of arecanute and betel-leaves by the mudalis and nagarattārs of Vikrama-Pandyapuram to the temple of Kailasamudaiya-Nāyunār at that village.

cells.location: Marandai
cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the same temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Registers a gift of land for morning-offerings to the image of Kuṇamāṛaṇḍa-Piḷḷaiyār which was set up in the temple of Kailāsamuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Māṛudaṉallūr alias Vikrama-Pāṇḍyapuram, by Aṛuṇāgirināthavaṉ.

cells.location: Marandai
cells.place: On the wall of Kailāsanātha †
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Seems to register a gift of money.

cells.place: On a stone set up in the Kaṭṭamāḷar in the same village.
cells.remarks: Records gift of land in Māṛudaṉallūr as dēyadāna to the temple of Tirukkulamudaiyaṉār and Sōyhagadēvi-Nāchchiyār, for worship and offerings.

cells.location: Nettūr
cells.place: On a slab set up near the dam
cells.remarks: States that the dam was constructed by a certain Nāranapapyaya a resident of Sokkanadapuram which was a hamlet of Netṭtur.

cells.place: On a stone set up in the Kaṭṭamāḷar in the same village (as Kailāsanātha temple). †
cells.remarks: Records certain restrictions imposed on industrial classes inhabiting the street Aṭivīra Rāman-perunderuvu at Nottūr, in Kuṛugumai-nāḍu by those who had lent money to them.

cells.place: On a boulder in the tank near Keḍuvēṭṭi.
cells.remarks: Gift of land under Parāntakapēri to the temples of Aṛikēśvari-Īśvara and Iyaṛkēśvara at Kaḷakkudi in Kaḷakkudi-nāḍu.

cells.location: Kaḷakkalaṅgal
cells.place: Fragments in the ruined Śiva temple
cells.remarks: Mentions Kaḷḷaga-nāḍu. Another fragment in the same temple mentions Kaḍuvēṭṭivāḷar and a third the measur-ing rod called Sundara-Pāṇḍyaṉ-kōl.

cells.location: Kaḷuṅkuḷam
cells.place: On a slab now worshipped as Māḍaṉam
cells.king: Jaṭilavarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Kone[rmai]koṇdān Perumāl Ajagan-Perumā. Ativirarāmaṇ alias Srivallabhadēva.
cells.date: Śaka 150[8], [2]3rd year, Vyaya, Uttarāyana, Vasantaritu, Mēsha, 7 ba. di. daṣami, Sunday, Vanijakaraṇa, Aviṭjam.
cells.remarks: Commences with the words Viṉṇagar-śiva, and registers a gift of land in Kaḷakkalaṅgal alias Kuṛum-baḷanallūr situated in Kuṛum-baḷa-nāḍu for a service called Śrīvallabha-sandhi in the temple of Tirukkulamudaiyaṉār, in the king who is said to have been born in the asterism Puṉarvasu.

cells.location: Suruṇḍai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vīra-Pāṇḍīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to make provision for repair to the temple of Tiruvirāmīśvaramuḍaiya-Nayiṇār at Suruṇḍai.

cells.place: On the wall of Vīra-Pāṇḍīśvara †
cells.remarks: Records that a merchant constructed the ardha-maṇḍapa and the Kapōḍamāḍam.

cells.place: On a stone set up in front of Vīra-Pāṇḍīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to provide for repairs to the temple.

cells.place: On the south wall (inside) of the first prākāra of the Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ temple at Tirumōhūr, (Madura taluk, Madura district).
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Registers the gift of the village of Śīrukuḷ-gūḍal in the Pāṇḍi-maṇḍalam to the temple of the god (Paramasvāmin) at Tirumōhūr by a certain Gaṅgēya. Part of the inscription is peeled off at the right side.

cells.place: On the wall of Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of land to the shrine of Tiruvāḷi-Āḷvār set up in the same temple, by a certain Gaṅgēya. Part of the inscription is peeled off at the right side.

cells.location: Suruṇḍai
cells.place: On the wall of Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 8th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 331: Śaka 147*, Ānanda, Adhika-Āshādhā, śu. 15, Lunar-eclipse = A.D. 1554, June 15, Friday. There was a lunar-eclipse on this day.]
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village of Kuṇarakapavittra-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in the Vēṇbā-nāḍu in Veṇbā-nāḍu in Veṇbā-nāḍu, separated from the temple of the god (Paramasvāmin) at Tirumōhūr.

cells.location: Suruṇḍai
cells.place: On the wall of Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 8th year and 287th day. [date-calculation appendix, No. 332: Śaka 1477, Rākshasa, Vaiśākha, śu 1, Sunday = A.D. 1555, April 21, Sunday; f.d.t. ·10.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift, for the same purpose, of the village of Vīranārāyaṇa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam separated from Tēṇūr-Tiruvēṅgaḍam in Pāgaṇūr-kūṛṛam.

cells.location: Suruṇḍai
cells.place: On the wall of Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Paṇaiyūr to the offerings of the god māṅgalam should provide for the offerings of the god when taken in procession for marriage in the month of Mārgali and during the hunting festival, according to the scale fixed for daily offerings in the temple.

cells.place: On the north wall of the Paḷḷi-koṇḍa-Perumāḷ shrine in Kaḷamēgha-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the Brahmans of Kaṇḍavai-chaturvēdi-maṅgalam should provide for the offerings of the god when taken in procession for marriage in the month of Mārgali and during the hunting festival, according to the scale fixed for daily offerings in the temple.

cells.place: On a pillar in a maṇḍapa in front of an empty shrine in Paḷḷi-koṇḍa-Perumāḷ shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of money for service in connection with the temple.

cells.location: Tirumōhūr, Madura taluk, Madura district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: At the entrance into the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Tirumōhūr-māṇḍapa temple
cells.remarks: Consists of four fragmentary inscriptions which appear to register a gift of land. Mentions the king's officer Maḷavarāyar.

cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāra (inside) of the [I]var-dhani-Amman shrine, in Tirumōhūr-māṇḍapa temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land as a dēvadāna to the shrine of Tirukāmakōṭṭam, constructed in the temple of Tirupparaṅguṇ-muḍaiya-Nayiṇār, by Sēndappaḷḷai.

cells.place: On the wall of Amman †
cells.remarks: Records a similar grant of one vēli of land to the same shrine by the king (Tirumōhūr-Nayiṇār).

cells.location: Tirumōhūr, Madura taluk, Madura district — Tamil Nadu

cells.date: 5th year, Simha, ba. di. Navami, Friday, Rohini.
cells.remarks: The inscription stays with the details of date.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.remarks: Gift of land and house sites to certain Brahmans for reciting the Vēdas, for making a flower-garden and for providing offerings to the temple of Vīrapāṇḍyīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāya-nār built in the name of the king by a certain Vaidya-chakravarti. The goddess is called Vēyaṉatojji-Nachchi-yār.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings etc., in connection with the ser-vice of Kaliyugārāman-sandhi instituted in the temple, in the name of the king and for the bathing of the temple and the Nāyaṉārs at the mouth of the river (Kāvērī).

cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.king: Parakēsarivarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin who having taken Madura, Īḷam (Ceylon), Karuvūr and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya, was pleased to take the appointment of heroes and victors.
cells.date: 37th year, Mēsha, ba. di. Tritīya, Sunday, Māla.
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words prākara. Registers a gift of land by purchase, by a native of Kulōttungasōla-chaturvēdimangalam in Puraṅgarambai-uādu, a sub-division of Rajēndrasōla-valanādu, for lamps to the temple of Tiruvenkādudaiyār.

cells.place: On the south wall of the prākāra of Gaṇēśa. †
cells.date: 2nd year [date-calculation appendix, No. 513: Śaka 1476, 5th year, Ānanda, Uttarāyaṇa, Grīshma-ritu, Mithuna 30, ba. di. trayōdaśī, Mṛigaśirsha. = A.D. 1554, on June 27, (Wednesday) the tithi and nak. ended at ·63 and ·88 respectively.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the gift of the village of Abhiumuktiśuramaṅgalam, made at the instance of the king's officer Pallavarāyar, to the same temple. Mentions the Royal Secretary Neriyudaichohola-Mōvēndavelān.

cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records that up to the 32nd year of the king (i.e., Śrivallabha) commencing from the time when Kōpperuñjiṅgadēva was fighting against the Kannadiyas who were building furtresses on the north bank of the river Kāvēri, the festivals of the temple were not conducted and that they were now ordered to be resumed. A certain Tondaimanār is stated to be an officer of this king and of Sundara-Pāndyadēva

cells.place: On the east wall of the prākāra of Gaṇēśa. †
cells.date: 26th year, Risha-bha, Monday, Mūla. [date-calculation appendix, No. 515: 47th year, Makara, śu.-chaturthi, Monday, Pūrattādi = A.D. 1117, January 8, Monday.]
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the village of Kuḷattūr-nāḍu-Pāḍi, in Tiruvali-nāḍu, for lamps to the same temple by a native of Pāśali-nāḍu, a sub-division of Māpavil-kōṭṭam which was a district of Jayangoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.remarks: Damaged. The introduction commences with the words pū-maruviya. Seems to register a gift of land for the same temple.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the wall of Gaṇēśa †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the same temple by a Brahmana lady of Vijayarājēndra-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 2nd year, Makara, śu. di. Trayōdaśī, Friday, Mṛiga-śīrsha.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase, for a lamp to the temple of Tiru-vēṅkaḍaiyār in Rājādhirāja-vaḷanāḍu, by a native of Poruvanūr in Paṭṭina-kuṟṟam a sub-division of Gēya-māṇikka-vaḷanāḍu. Refers to a branch of the Kāvēri and the consequent silting up of the surrounding fields.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 27th year, Simha ba. di. Trayōdaśī, Tuesday, Āyil.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase to the same temple for lamps, by a native of Kānnanūr in Kuṅgūrnāḍu, a sub-division of Poḷiyūr kōṭṭam alias Kuḷattūr-nāḍu-vaḷanāḍu which was a district of Jayangoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam. As the land was lying fallow for many years, the donor paid money for the cost of clearing it.

cells.location: Tiruvengadu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.date: 26th year, Mēsha, śu. di. Pañchami, Wednesday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words pū-maruviya. Gift of land by purchase in Nelvayi, by a native of Aḷampakkam in Puḷiyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kuḷattūr-nāḍu-vaḷanāḍu which was a district of Jayangoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam for lamps to the temple of Tiruvēṅkaḍaiyār. The donor also gave money for reclaiming the land.

cells.place: On the west wall of the first prakara of the shrine of the goddess Brahmavidya.
cells.remarks: Records that the walls of the shrine of the goddess Periya-nāyaki-Amman were constructed by Dandayuda-

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the central shrine of the Śivāloktyā-gar temple
cells.remarks: Records the assignment of a fixed quantity of salt from the salt-pan of Mahāpālakanallūr for the requirements of salt, sandal-paste, incense, etc., for the temple of Tiruppurambiyamudaiya-Mahādēva at Nallūr in Vennai-yurnādu, a sub-division of Rājādhirāja-valanādu. Mention the Royal Secretary Mahāyappaiyar.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of Śivāloktyā-gar temple. †
cells.remarks: Dādēvar. Introduction commences with the words "Ganga-dēvar". Records a gift of land for the expenses of the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of Śivāloktyā-gar temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a gift of land formed into the new village called Edirilichōlanallūr, to the same temple for the maintenance of a matha.

cells.place: On the north wall of the mandapa in front of Śivāloktyā-gar temple. †
cells.date: 8th year su. di. panchami, Wednesday, Pushya. [date-calculation appendix, No. 525: 8th year, śu. di. 5, Wednesday, [Pushya]. In A.D. 1343, Wednesday, 30th April was a day of " Pushya " but the tithi was 6th, not 5th in the bright fortnight.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Refers to the 10th year of Kulōttunga-Chōladēva and to a land gift.

cells.place: On the north wall of the first prakara of Śivāloktyā-gar temple. †
cells.date: 16-1st year, Rishabha, śu. di. Chaturthi, Saturday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the Vaikuntha exempting the temple lands from the payment of sabhaviniyōgam.

cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by the assembly of Pañchvanmadēvi alias Kulōttuṅgasōla-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Vennayūrnādu a sub-division of Rajadhiraja-valanadu, for offerings to Āludaiyapillai and Sokkiyar and for feeding Apūrvins during the service of Āyirattennūruvaṇ-sandi instituted in the temple of Sri-Kayilasamudaiyar of the same place. Refers to the 12th year of Karikala-Chōla and the 30th year of the reign of Tribhuvanaviradēva.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: Do. *
cells.date: 10th year, Makara, śu. di. Navami, Monday, Viśākha. [date-calculation appendix, No. 528: 10th year, Makara, śu. di. 9, Monday, Visakha. = Monday, 11th January A.D. 1143; .62; .42. NOTE.—It is note worthy that these epigraphs, as proved by their dates, should belong to the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōla II whose dated inscription, have so far occurred only in Telugu districts (vide the article on this reign by the present writer in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XI, page 287). There are no dates satisfying the given details in the reign of either Kulōttunga-Chōla I or Kulōttunga-Chōla III. The blank in No. 380 of 1918, which has been read conjecturally as "bahula" should be "sukla," while "pūrvapaksha" or "śu. di." in No. 528 of 1918, which is quite clear in the impression, is clearly an error for "apurapaksha" or "ba. di.," the combination of śu. 9 and nak. "Visakha" in Makara mouth not being possible except in aparapaksha. See the present writer's Eye-table.]
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the king making the lands belonging to the temple of Tirunallār-Perumanamudaiyār, tax-free as previously held. The sabha met in the treasury-hall of Sri-Kayilasamudaiyar at Pañchavanmahādēvi alias Kulōttuṅgasōla-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Veqnaiyūr-nādu a sub-division of Vadagarai Rajadhiraja-valanadu.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Gives a detailed list of lands comprising the villages of Tiruppurambiyamnallūr and Tribhuvanavīranangainallūr, the former being the temple of Tiruppurambiyamudaiya-Nāyanār. The former village was constituted out of lands separated from Satianamabhimanallūr, a hamlet of Kīzh-kharanallūr, a hamlet of Panchavanmādēvi and the latter was formed from the lands attached to the same village, in the 30th year of the reign of the king's father (Pēriyadēvar) Tribhuvanavīradēva.

cells.place: On the west wall of the prākāra of Śivāloktyā-gar. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to the shrine of Tirukkalakkōṭṭa-Muḍaiya-Nāchchiyār constructed in the temple of Uṛaiyūr-perumāḷuḍaiyār, by Chandraśēkharan Pāṇḍiṇadēviyār, the headman of Nerkuṇṛam in Puḷiyūr-kōṭṭam alias Kulōttuṅgaśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, a member of Jayangoṇḍa-Chōḷa-Mūvēndavēḷār, the Royal Secretary (Ōlai-Garbu) Nerayūruḍaiyān-Mūvēndavēḷār.

cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.date: 13th year, Vṛiśchika, bu. di. 26, Wednesday, Puśiyu.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by purchase in Śāttaṅgalam alias Śivacharaṇasēkharanallūr, a hamlet of Paṇḍiṇavaramādēvi, for a flower-garden, to the shrine of Āḷuḍaiya-Piḷḷaiyār chēri in the temple, by a resident of Abhayāṇimāṇikka-chēri in the same temple.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Records an order of Tirudiṇḍigaiyarāyaṇ of Purakkudi presenting lands (purchased) from the inhabitants of Nallūr alias Nāgaṇūrpēralam to the shrine of Pon-padalha-Aḍuvar in the temple of Tirupperuma-muḍaiyār.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.date: 35th year, Makara, šu. di. Navami, Tuesday, Kartti-gai.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by purchase for feeding the apūrvins who come to worship in the same temple.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by purchase, by the assembly of Parākramachōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Veṇṇāyūr-nāḍu, for the maintenance of a flower-garden in the maṭha called Para-māyōlikkōlari-muḍam.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Registers a copy of an order issued by Tirudiṇḍigaiyarāyaṇ presenting lands for offerings and worship, to the shrine of Paṇḍiṇadēva-Aḍuvar in the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the prākāra of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.date: 9th year, Tuḷa, ba. di. Chaturthi, Monday, Makha.
cells.remarks: Records sale of land to a certain Kaṇḍan Śōḷan Śāḷiyāṇiyār of Veṇṇāyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Paṇḍiṇavaramādēvi, which is a district of Paṇḍi-maṇḍalam, by two residents of Rājāditya-chaturvēdimangalam in Veṇṇāyūr-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.date: 9th year, Tuḷa, ba. di. Chaturthi, Monday, Makha. [date-calculation appendix, No. 537: 18th year, Siṁha, 10, ba di., prathamā, Sunday, Śadayam = A.D. 1267, August 7 ; ·40.]
cells.remarks: Relates to the same transaction as is contained in No. 536, above.

cells.location: Āchchapuram
cells.place: On the wall of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.date: 14th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 538: 5th year, Kanyā, śu. di., prathamā, Monday, Chitra = A.D. 1254, September 14; ·50. On this day nak. Chitra which commenced at ·08 of the day was current throughout the remaining day.]
cells.remarks: Commences with the words svasti śrī. Records an order of Kulōttuṅgaśōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam reducing the alias of vāram and kudamai to be paid on lands by the cultivator and fixing the duties and privileges to be enjoyed by certain classes of persons.

cells.place: On the east wall of the prākāra of Śivāloktyā-gar †
cells.remarks: Unfinished and built in.

cells.place: On a slab near the dhvajastambha of Śivāloktyā-gar temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1605, Kali 4784, Dundubbi, Sittirai 8, Thurs-day, sū. di. Sap-tami, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Śivolokattyar by private individuals.

cells.place: On a slab near the village of Pulichchakkāḍu.
cells.remarks: Records that the Poligars and others decided that the village of Pulichchakkadu was not required to be held by the Mahajanas but must be enjoyed by the temple of Saṭṭainādapuram.

cells.location: Oḷaiyāmputtūr
cells.place: On the north and south walls of the Aruṇāmalaiyār temple
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Records that the repairs in the temple of Tiru-Aruniśuramudaiyār were executed by Nalla-evagapperumā], son of Kaliyugarāna IIattaraiyar Inakkunalla-Perumā].

cells.place: On a slab in the tank at the same village (as Aruṇāmalaiyār temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a parivāraṇa given by Vaittiyanāda- Aiyangār, the agent of Vijayaraghava-Nāyakkaraian to the temple of Oḷaiyāmputtūr.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: At the entrance into the Sundarēvara temple
cells.remarks: Fragment. Records a register a gift of land for conducting the service called Vīra-Vāṇḍi-Sandhi instituted in the temple of [Tiru] Jōkkiya-Mahādēvaramudaiyār

cells.place: On nine fragmentary stones the east wall of the first prākāra of the Naṭarāja templeat Chidāmbaram (Chidambaram taluk, South Arcot district); left of entrance.
cells.remarks: One of the fragments mentions the name of the king Tri- Bhuvanachakravartin Kulōttuṅga-Chōḷadēva, two others contain part of the historical introduction of Kulōttuṅga- Chōḷa I, and the rest provide for offerings to the temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Aruṇāmalaiyār †
cells.remarks: Stones missing in the middle. Registers a gift of land as jīvita to a number of persons who had to look after the garden called Sundarapāṇḍyan-tiruttoppu and the street called Sundarapāṇḍyan-keḍgu-tiruvīthi. Mentions the king's officers Tennavan-Brahmārāyar, Vikramapāṇḍya- Brahmārāyar, Vikrama-Pāṇḍya-Brahmārāyar, Jayatungapallavaraiyar, Vikkirama-Pāṇḍyar and Kurukulattaraiyar.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Aruṇāmalaiyār †
cells.remarks: Stones missing in the middle. Registers an order of Kalingarāyar granting lands for the maintenance of certain flower-gardens, some of which was called Aiyonaṅgākai-tirunandavaṇam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: Do. on the left and right sides
cells.remarks: Gift of land for supplying pomegranates and offerings to the gods and goddesses in the temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: Do. on the right side
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Vaṅgāttaraiyar. Gift of land for supplying plantain fruits.

cells.place: On six fragments built into the platform forming steps in front of the entrance.
cells.remarks: One of the fragments bears the regnal year 48. The others refer to gift of lands.

cells.place: On two other other fragments collected from the place of Aruṇāmalaiyār. †
cells.king: Vikrama-Chōladēva †
cells.date: 8th year of Parakēsari-varman Tribhuvanachakravartin Vikrama-Chōladēva (12th century) ... (A. D. 986-1013) †
cells.remarks: One of the fragments refers to the 8th year of Parakēsarivarman Tribhuva[nachakravartin Vik]rama-Choladēva (12th century) and mentions Nangūr in Nangūr-naḍu and another contains a portion of the historical introduction of Rajaraja I, (A. D. 985-1013).

cells.place: On a slab kept in the compound of the Union Club at Tanjore and presented by Mr. N. K. Ramaswami Ayyar.
cells.remarks: In Tamil characters. Mentions Kīḷikkadi in Kīḷiṅgili-nāḍu and seems to register a gift of gold.

cells.place: On fragments in the Nāgarāja temple in the Kamalamayam-tank, at Tiruvarūr, (Negapatam taluk, Tanjore district).
cells.remarks: Some of the fragments seem to register a gift of land. One of them mentions the name Agāravallaban who was probably the donor of the stone.

cells.place: On the north wall of the Sundarēśvarasvāmin temple at Sembēdu (Gingee taluk, South Arcot district).
cells.date: Śaka 1469, Plavaṅga, Rīshabha, śu. di. Punarvasu, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 1: Adigudi]
cells.remarks: Records gift of the village of Sīyāṇūr for offerings, lamps and daily worship to the temple of Vīru-Aḷagiya-Tambirāṇār at Vīramāḷamallūr, a hamlet of Pakkam in Pakkappu on the north side of the Peṇṇai (river), in Paḷakuṇṛa-kōṭṭam, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍa-śōḷa-maṇḍalam, by Sōrappa-Nāyaka and Vaiyappa-Nāyaka, the sons of Poḍḍu Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the wall of Sundarēśvarasvāmin †
cells.date: Śaka 1403 (mistake for Śaka 1443), Vṛisha, Kumbha, śu. di. [Dvī]tiyā, Mṛigaśīrshaḍy, Uttarāṣāḍha. [date-calculation appendix, No. 2: North Arcot]
cells.remarks: Records the lease of certain temple lands to Timmappa-Nāyaka, son of Obala-Nāyaka who had repaired breaches in the tank at Sīḍampāṭṭa and constructed shrines for Aḷagiya-Avaṇappilliyār, Vairava and Caṇḍēśvara.

cells.place: On the south wall of Sundarēśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1401 (mistake for 1441), Mōsha, śu. di. pañchami, Monday, Mṛigaśīrsha. [date-calculation appendix, No. 3: Ayyampalayam]
cells.remarks: Records a transaction similar to No. 2 above.

cells.place: On the wall of Sundarēśvarasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Registers gift of taxes by Avasaram Aṇṇamarāśiyar for the merit of the king, to the same temple.

cells.place: On the south and east walls of Sundarēśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1497, Yuva Rīshabha, ba. di. Newmoon, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 5: Desur]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of taxes for lamps to the same temple by Krishṇappa-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the Agastyēśvara temple at Avalūr (same district and taluk).
cells.remarks: Seems to register a gift of house-sites and money, for the merit of the king, by the agents of Tiruvengaḍa-Jīyar, to certain private individuals in order to form a madavilāgam and for doing service in the temple of Agastyēśvara at Avin-ūr.

cells.place: On a boulder near a tank at Singavaram (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Seems to register a gift of land for a garden to the temple at Singavaram.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vishnu temple at Daḍāpuram (Tiṇḍivanam taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Gives a list of vessels and ornaments made of gold, silver and pearls and presented to the temples of Kaṇḍavai-Viṇṇagar, Iruḷukimāṇikka-Īśvara and Kuṇḍavai-Jina-laya, by the queen-mother, the great lady Kuṇḍavai-pirāṭṭiyār, daughter of Uṇṇamulagaiyār, in the village of Rājarājapuram in Naḷḷūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Vāḷa-kuppa-kōṭṭam. Mentions the office Parakramēśa-Mūvēndavēḷar.

cells.place: On the west wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Stops with the mention of the king.

cells.place: On the south wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for lamps to the temple of Kundavai-Viṇṇagar-Ālvār by princess Pañchavan Mādēviyār-Pirāṭṭiyār. Mentions the sēnapati Mummudichōla Brahmamārāyar, who was in charge of the management of the temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu †
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by a maid-servant of the king.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for 10 lamps to the temple of Kundavai-Viṇṇagar-Ālvār by princess Kundavai-Pirāṭṭiyār.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the south and east walls of the mandapa in front of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the dancing girls attached to the temples of the Śrī-Iraikulamudaiyār-tēvar and Kundavai-Viṇṇagar-Ālvār should accompany the god in processions and sing and dance during the hunting festival. The inscription commences with the introduction Tirumagal pōla, etc., and is left unfinished.

cells.place: On the east wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of vessels by a dancing girl to the temple of Kundavai-Viṇṇagar-Ālvār for the bath of the god. Mentions Ārūran-Ambalattādiyār alias Sōla-kēralan-Mūvēndavēḷān, the headman of Mīrai.

cells.place: On the north wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Refers to the construction of the 3 temples at Rājarājapuram mentioned in No. 8 above, by princess Pāṇḍiyan Kundavai-Pirāṭṭiyār and records that on receipt of the royal writ the officer Aruran Aravanaiyān alias Parākrama-mājōḷa-Mūvēndavēḷān of Pāṇḍi-nāḍu alias Rāja-nārāyaṇa-vaḷanāḍu ordered the temple to be constructed and the ornaments made engraved on stone in the respective temples. The presents consisted of vessels and ornaments of various descriptions, made of gold, silver and pearl.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Muḷiyūr-śiva-rāyavin temple in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Refers to the gift mentioned in No. 18 above.

cells.place: On the south wall of Muḷiyūr-śiva-rāyavin temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for 10 lamps to the temple of Śrī-Iraikula-māṇikka-Javaramudaiyār by the same princess. Refers also to the construction of the temple by her.

cells.place: On the wall of Muḷiyūr-śiva-rāyavin †
