cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Records the gift of land by purchase, to the temple of Muḷaiyāḷam-uḍaiyār-Mahādēva, by a certain Paḷaikkaṇ Kaman Tiruvaga[ṭṭi]muḍaiyān, a native of Irāiyūr in Kuṇṛa-nāḍu, a sub-division of Uṛukkāṭṭu-kōṭṭam, for offerings to the image of Uḍaiyār-Piḷḷaiyār which he had set up in the temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Records gift by the individual mentioned in No. 65 to the assembly of Muḷiūr alias Rājēndra-chōḷa-chaturvēdi-maṅgalam for strengthening the bund of the big tank of the village wherever necessary.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Gift of land in Ēmāpuram alias Madhurāntakanallūr in Kaḍaiyūr-nāḍu, for a lamp to the temple of Muḷasthānamuḍaiya-Mahādēva, by a certain Mannaiyan Mātampapallavārayan, a resident of Tirukkōvalūr in Kurukkai-kūṟṟam, a subdivision of Irungōḷappāḍi-nāḍu, in the same nāḍu, in expiation of the sin of an accidental death of a person, Māṇikkam, in Viḷupparaiyan-nāḍu through the donor's nephew.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Modern. Gift of land by a certain Tirumalai-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On the north wall of the maṇḍapa of Āḍavalla-nāya. †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land for 8 kāśu by Yajña-Bhaṭṭa of Muṇiyūr, one of the members of the āḷuṅgaṇa of Muṇiyūr, to one Bōdhāyana-Bhaṭṭa, a brāhmaṇa, for a lamp, which was presented by a shepherd to the temple of Mūlasthānamuḍaiya Mahādēva.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the maṇḍapa of Āḍavalla-nāya. †
cells.remarks: Gift of 16 cows for another half lamp by the grandson of the donor mentioned in no. 69. Refers to Kulōttuṅga-Chōḷa by the name 'Soṅkappuṟam'.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the same maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Gift of taxes for repairing the “Ediraganayan-tiranaljigai” and other structures in the temple and for repair by Seṅgeni-Ammai-appan Shyan Pallavandān alias Rajanārayaṇ-Sambuvarayaṇ mentioned in No. 52 above.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.date: 15th year, Sinhha, ba. di. ekadaśi, Monday, Tiruvādirai.
cells.remarks: The introduction begins with the words gewībīgetas etc. Gift of 9 kaśu by Ariyān Āndān Kumalakara-Bhaṭṭan for a lamp to the shrine of Visvēsvaradēva built by him in the western prakāra (tiruchchurru) of the temple of Ajuđaiyar Ś.1-Mulasthānamuđaiyar.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Gift of land, māje tax-free, in Śirupāḍi alias Kuḷōttuṅga-śōḷanallūr by Siyan Pallavāṇḍān Ēḍiriliśōḷa Sambuvarāyan, under the orders issued by the king at the instance of Gaṅgaiyāran and others, to the temple of Aḍavaiyār. The donor is also called 'Aḷuḍaiyār-Śrī-Muḷasthānamuḍaiya-Nāyanār'.

cells.place: On the west wall of the maṇḍapa of Āḍavalla-nāya. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by a certain person for a lamp to the image of Viśvēśvaradēva set up in the temple of Mūlasthānamuḍaiyār, by Ariyan Kamalākara-Bhaṭṭa. See No. 72 above.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: The introduction begins with the words 'Gēyēśvari', etc. Records a royal gift of lands at Nagar alias Dinachintāmaṇinallūr, which was formed into a new village under the name Kuḷōttuṅgaśōḷanallūr. Mentions the Loyal Secretary Aḷaiyāḷa Mūvēndavēḷān.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: The introduction begins with the words 'Yēgēśvari', etc. Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Muḷasthānamuḍaiyār at Muṇiyūr alias Rājanārāyaṇa-caturvēdimangalam in Ōymā-nāḍu alias Vijayarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu which is a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍaśōḷamaṇḍalam, by a native of Rājarājapuram, Tirumuṇaippāḍi-nāḍu, a subdivision of Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Built in. Seems to record a gift of land for a lamp to the temple of Adavalla-Nayanar, by a native of Puttur in Pattana-nadu.

cells.place: At the top of the entrance into a vacant shrine in the west prakara of the temple of Āḍavalla-nāya. †
cells.remarks: Records that Ariyan Andan Kamakkaramban set up the image of Visvesvaradeva and repaired the temple.

cells.place: On the west wall of the main prakara (inside).
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records a gift of land to the temple of Adavalla-Nayanar by Ammaiyappan, the agent of Saluva Narasingaya-Udaiyar, for worship and festivals. Refers to a mandapa built by Ilamaraiya-Ayyan in the same temple.

cells.place: On the south wall of the prakara of Āḍavalla-nāya (inside). †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase for 10 lamps to the temple of Ādavalla-Nayanār at Muñūr alias Rajanarāyana-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, by a certain Madēvaṇ Kulōttungaśola-Mūvendaveja of Ambar in Ambar-nadu, a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-valanadu in Sola-manđalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Poriyanallur-udaiyar set up the image of Periya-Vinayakapillaiyar and gave land for offerings and lamps to it. States that she also built the sopana-madaiyam in front of the Dakshinamurti shrine.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya (outside) †
cells.date: Vyaya, Puratṭadi [2]4. [date-calculation appendix, No. 82: 11th year, Dhanus, ba. di., daśami, Thursday, Viśakhā = A.D. 1188, December 15; ba. 10 ended at 25 and nak. Viśakhā began at 25, ending next day at 18.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the bottom. Seems to record the appointment of a person by Tammarasa, the agent of Annamarasar, who was the avasaram of the king to look after the lamps in the same temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya (outside) †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Seems to register a gift of land for worship and offerings to the temple of Ādavalla-Nayanār.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya (outside) †
cells.date: Śaka 1389, [Vyaya], Mithuna, śu di. Monday, daśam1, Tiruvadirai.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by purchase, for a flower-garden, to the same temple by a native of Soladivakaranallur alias Tingađupakkam in Ugrukhattu-kōṭtam, a subdivision of Jayaṅgondachola-manđalam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya (outside) †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift to the temple of Adavallanayanar at Muniyur alias Rajanarayana-chaturvedimangalam in Oyma-nadu, a subdivision of Jayangondachola-mandalam, by Kanjai-Alappirandan Devamallaiyan alias Vapariya.

cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Built in and intercepted by pillars. Seems to provide for repairs to the temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Āḍavalla-nāya †
cells.remarks: Do. Seems to record the construction of a car and a gift of land to the same temple by Kaūjapa-Nayaka for the merit of Tirumalāi-Nayaka.

cells.place: On the east wall of the ruined Kamakshi Ammay shrine in the temple of Āḍavalla-nāya. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of money and land to the temple, by Aludai-yan Alagiyadeva alias Kadavatti of Nagappu, for the expenses of the car festival.

cells.place: On the west wall of Kamakshi Ammay shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land, midā tax-free, for the expenses to the shrine of Tirukkāmakkōṭṭamuḍaiya Periya-Nāchchiyār in the temple of Aḍavallār.

cells.place: On the wall of Kamakshi Ammay .. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land and house-site to a private individual. Mentions Kañjāna-Nāyaka.

cells.place: At the entrance into same temple; right side.
cells.remarks: Records that the entrance was (called after) Tirumaliñai-jōni-nāyakan Malavarāyar of Nalkarochchi in Pāṇḍimaṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the east and north walls of the deserted Vishnu temple in the same village (as Kamakshi Ammay shrine). †
cells.king: Dakshiṇa-Kapileśvara Kumāra Mahāpatra son of Ambiradēva.
cells.date: Śaka 1386, Tāraṇa, Mēsha, śu. di. tritīyā, Thursday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: A copy of No. 51, above.

cells.place: On the north wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.date: 10th year, Dhanus, śu. di. prathama, Monday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Records a tax-free gift of Śuṅgavaṇḍai, a hamlet of Muṇṇūru, with its name changed into Purushōttama-nallūr, by the people of Oymā-nāḍu, for worship and repairs to the temple of Purushōttamam alias Śittira-mēli-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān.

cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu .. †
cells.remarks: Built a boundary of land for worship and repairs to the same temple by Tiruvāṇattila-Bhaṭṭa-Somayāji of Kuṇḍūr.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu .. †
cells.remarks: Records that some construction or repairs (திருப்பணி) were executed by Perumpaḷḷai, the agent of Vijandappillai of Valluvappakkam.

cells.place: On the west and west walls of Vishnu temple. †
cells.date: Vyaya, Karttika 30. [date-calculation appendix, No. 96: 18th year, Dhanus, ēkādaśī, Wednesday, Mūla = A.D. 1163, December 25. The tithi was bahula-trayōdaśī (13) which ended at ·40 and the nak. Mūla ended at ·92 on that day.]
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a certain shed as a kōyil-maṭam to the temple of Ponnal Śittira-mēli-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān, by Tummaḷar, the agent of Ammamāṇḍar.

cells.place: On the west wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Worn out and incomplete. Mentions Vikrama-Pāṇḍya Mavali-vāṇarāyar.

cells.place: At the entrance into Vishnu temple; left side. †
cells.remarks: Records that the doorway (tirunilaikkal) was the gift of Aruļalapperumaļ of Vaṅgippuram.

cells.place: (On the wall) of a deserted shrine called Sambandapperumāḷ-kōyil, in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the building (of the shrine) was done by Kuṭṭana-Nāyaka, son of Timma-Nāyaka, one of the Kaṇṇadiya-Nāyakas of Marada-raḍar-paḍaivu.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Tirumalikhavara temple at Vēlūr (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a village as a devadāna to the temple of Tiruvakkiramuḍaiya-Nāyinar, by a certain Kamu-Nāyaka in the name of the king. Villavarayar figures as a signatory.

cells.place: On the east and north walls of Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Gift of a land by Kuramikkam Tittar-Pillai, for the merit of Viravananta-Nāyaka, for festivals in the temple of Tiruvakkiramuḍaiya-Nāyinar. Signed by Villavarayar.

cells.place: On the north wall of Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the shrine of Ilaya-Nāyinar, by Viruppaṇa-Nāyaka, son of Ellappa-Nāyaka, in the name of the king.

cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a gift by Śēṅgēṇi Ammaiyappan, for repairs to the temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Tirumalikhavara †
cells.remarks: Gift of a hamlet Mulliyappanagaram as a dēvadāna to the temple by the king. Signed by Kupparumal and Villavarāyar.

cells.place: On the north wall of Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones missing at the end. Gift of the village Kuppam as a dēvadāna to the temple by the king for the merit of Sāḷuvakkkaṇṭar. Signed by Eṭṭar-Piḷḷai and Villava

cells.place: On the north and west walls of Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of cows made at the instance of the residents of several districts, for a lamp, to the temple of Tiruvaguisvara-muḍaiya-Mahādēva at Valar alias Virudarājabhayaṅkara-nallūr in Ōyma-nāḍu, by a native of Kaḍuvampakkam for having shot his uncle with an arrow mistaking him for an animal.

cells.place: On the west wall of Tirumalikhavara temple †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seam to register a gift of lamp to the same temple by a certain Sirivān for a similar accidental death of an individual, while hunting.

cells.place: On the wall of Tirumalikhavara †
cells.remarks: Records that a titti, a native of Savundirya-dōḷapuram in Aḍai-nāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam built the nṛitta-maṇḍapa and Nayanar-tiru-viruppu, in the temple of Tiruvakkīraṇamuḍaiya-Nayi-nār, in the city; in order to please Kaḷahastīśvara, his ishtelary deity.

cells.place: On the west wall of the Subrah-maṇya shrine in Tirumalikhavara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a tax-free gift of the village of Parangōṇi in Valar-śīrmai, for worship and repairs to the temple of Tiruvakkīraṇamuḍaiya-Tanuṇār, by a certain Nagu-Reddyār. Records that Vijayaḍēva-Mahārāya was governing the country.

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of Subrah-maṇya shrine. †
cells.date: 18th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 110: Varaguṇa-Parāntaka, probably the Chēra king Kōkkaṇḍaṇ]
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Records a gift of 48 sheep made at the instance of the Bhaṭṭas, for a lamp to the temple of Tiru-Agniśvaramuḍaiya-Mahādēva at Veḷūr alias Viruda-rājabhayaṅkaranallūr in Ōyma-nāḍu alias Vijayarāja-ndra-vaḷanāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam by two residents of the village, for having killed a buffalo which had spoiled their crop.

cells.place: On three pillars built into the walls of Subrah-maṇya shrine. †
cells.remarks: The inscription is exposed only on one side of each pillar, the other sides being covered by the walls. Seems to register a gift of land for worship and offerings, to the temple of Tiru-Agniśvara at Veḷūr in Ma[ṇi]-nāḍu, a subdivision of Ōyma-nāḍu in Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On a wall on the south side of Subrah-maṇya shrine. On the east and south walls of the central shrine in the Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple in the same village (as Subrah-maṇya shrine). †
cells.remarks: Records that this maṇḍapa was built by Periya-Nagu-Redḍi, son of Periya-Erumai-Redḍi.

cells.place: On a wall on the south side of the same temple. On the east and south walls of the central shrine in the Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: The inscription has been mostly erased by a chisel. Seems to register a gift of taxes. Mentions Muññōgru-pagxu in Oyma-nađu alias Virudarajabhayankara-valanađu.

cells.place: On the west, south and east walls of the mandapa in front of Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a royal order made at the instance of Villavarayar granting the three villages Mambakkam, Kurugur and Navarpakkam clubbed together and re-named Kulottunga-nallur as a tax-free devadana, for meeting the expenses in the temple of Kulottunga-Aḷvār at Valur alias Virudarajabhayankaranallur, in Oymā-nāḍu alias Vi-jayanārāyaṇa-caturvedimangalam, of Jayangonda-chola-mandalam. At the time of making the grant the king was seated on his throne which was set up underneath a pearl canopy on the coronation hall of his palace at Vikramāśolapuram.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.date: 3rd year [date-calculation appendix, No. 115: Tirumaladēvī-Mahārāya. Śaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Tula, ba. ēkādaśī. Monday, Hastā. In-Tāraṇa, ba. ēkādaśī fell on Sunday (= A.D. 1524, October 23) ending at ·32 on which day Hastā commenced at ·67 and ended at ·60 on Monday following.]
cells.remarks: Relates to the same grant as the above. Mentions the officers Kulottungasola-Gāngēyarāyan and Villavarāyan.

cells.place: On the east wall of Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: Śobhakrit, Āvaṇi 15. [date-calculation appendix, No. 116: Śaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Dhanus, śu. paurṇami, Sunday. Paurṇami in Dhanus in Tāraṇa ended at ·95 on Saturday (= A.D. 1524, December 10) while Ārdrā commenced at ·50 on this day and ended at ·53 on Sunday.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Pariya-Nagu-Reddi, son of Ema-Reddi of Tirumudru-Omandur and the temple of Tira-virunda-Perumal.

cells.place: On the east north walls of Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: Šaka 18[2]5, Svabhānu, Tula, ba. di. dvadaśi, Friday, Uttiram. [date-calculation appendix, No. 117: Śaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Dhanus, śu. prathamā, Ārdrā, Sunday = A.D. 1524, December 11 Sunday; śu. prathamā must be mistake for ba. prathamā; ·96; 53.]
cells.remarks: Records that the devadana village of Navarpakkam, etc., formerly granted to the temple, had been ordered to be brought back under cultivation and worship and festivals conducted regularly in the temple of Kulottunga-Aḷvār-Vi-yagar-Aḷvār at Valur alias Virudarājabhayankaranallur.

cells.place: On the north wall of Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: Šaka 1893, Khars, Makara. [date-calculation appendix, No. 118: Śaka 1426, Raktākshi, Vrishicha, amāvāsyā, Wednesday, Visākhā. = A.D. 1504, November, 6, Wednesday (vide No. 98 above).]
cells.remarks: Appointment of a certain Irākadakkam of Kommadipūṇḍu as a tiruvilakkak-kuḍi to the temple of Tiruvirunda-Perumāḷ, by avasaram Aṇṇanāmasiyār, to secure conquests (tīrtha-vijaya) to the king.

cells.place: At the entrance into Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple; right side. †
cells.remarks: Records that the door-way (tirunilaikkal) and steps were made by Tiruvachchalan of Kīramūr.

cells.place: On the four faces of a slab set up near Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land by the assembly (ūr) of Vālur alias Rājēndra-Chola-chaturvedimangalam, to Achchaniyanbāy, the headman of Pagal, for the land granted to the temple of Rājēndrayan-Vinnagar-Aḷvār.

cells.place: On the slab of Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 9th [date-calculation appendix, No. 121: Śaka 1506, Tāraṇa, Vrishicha, śu. paurṇai, Saturday = A.D. 1584 November, 7 Saturday. On this day there was also a lunar eclipse.]
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to record a sale of land by the assembly of Vālur to a native of Kāmāṭṭakuḍi-chaturvedimangalam in Tirumunaippāḍi-nāḍu, a subdivision of Śōla-maṇḍalam, for being presented to the temple of Kulottunga-Aḷvār-Vinnagar-Aḷvār.

cells.place: On a stone set up in the Jaina temple street, in the same village (as Tiru-virunda-Perumāḷ temple). †
cells.date: Śaka 1453, Virochi-krit, Kumbha, su. di. trayodaśī, Mon-day, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a gift of money for worship, to the temple of Tiruvakki-aṇḍa-Tamiḻanār at Vālur.

cells.place: On another stone in the same street, Jaina temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a gift of land by the king to the same temple for the merit of Vīra-Vasanta-Nāyaka.

cells.place: At the entrance into the central shrine of the Jaina temple in the same village (as Jaina temple) ; left side. †
cells.remarks: In modern characters. Records the renovation of the temple by Jayasēna.

cells.place: On the back of the first central shrine in the ruined Śiva temple at Olagapuram (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Gift of sheep for lamps to the temple of Tirkkil-kesari-īśvaram at Olokamādēvipuram which was a city in [I]rāyur-nādu.

cells.place: On the south wall of Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Seems to register a gift of land by purchase by Nakkaṇ Vayiramēgaṇ for offerings and lamps to the shrine of Terkkil-vaśal, Śattan.

cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: Built in in the middle. Seems to record a sale of land by the nagarattār of Ilakamādēvipuram in Oyma-nādu to Gaṅgaṇ-Ambalavan Gaṇdaradi[tta]śōla-Vilupparaiyan of Kuyalalam in Gaṅgarasayira, for being presented to the temple for laying out a flower-garden. Mentions Kalikaṇṭaka-peruvarambu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: Gift of ewes for a lamp to the temple of Siraikāļatam-Arikulakēsari-lohcavamudaiya-Muhadēva at Olōga-mādēvipuram, by a merchant.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp to the temple of Śiraikālyatta-Paramēśvaran at Ulogamādēvipuram a taniýūr in Pangala-nādu. Amman. Gaņdarādīttanār, a parundaram of the king, who built it, made some provision.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words q [as?...]. Records a sale of land by the nagarattar of Olga-mādēvipuram in Perāyūr-nādu, a subdivision of Oyma-nādu for being presented to the temple of Arikulakēsari-īśvaramudaiyār in order to meet the expenses connected with the shrine of Rajēndrōla-Viłakhar built in it.

cells.place: At the top of the entrance into Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Puttulaṇ Niraiyan Kulattaṇ of Mavendaputūr in Tirumunaippadi, presented the sacred door.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of sheep for a lamp, to the temple [maintained] in the Tirumudiyl-vāsal, for worship, to the temple Arikulakesari-Iśvaramudaiya-Nayanar at Olagamādēvipuram in Oyma-nādu alias Vijayarājēndrala-valanadu.

cells.place: On the south and east walls of Śiva temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1348, Pa-rahava, Mesha, bu. di. chaturdaśi, Saturday, Rēvai.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship, offerings and lamps to the temple of Viłappiranādayan-Nayanar at Kufram-pundapuram alias Ulagamādēvipuram in Mūfīrru-purru a subdivision of Ulagamādēvipuram-valanādu, by Liñgama-yyar, son of the younger brother of Viłaiya-Nayaka.

cells.place: On the east and north walls of Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records a sale of land, as gift, and by the nagarattar of Ulogamādēvipuram to Pūriyaru-aiyan, the subdivision of Oyma-nādu, for feeding 25 Brahmaruis in a śālai attached to the temple.

cells.place: On the base of the bali-pīṭha in front of Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Solaman alias Vo[l]amban Ādavan alias Vidivādagau, set up the śri-pitha.

cells.place: On a stone set up near Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: Damage. Mentions Villavarāyar of Kiḍāran in Iraṅgolēp-pāḍi, the agent of Iḷara-Nāyaka and the temple of Aḷagiyaśōlapuram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Uḷagōṇadēvi-puram.

cells.place: On a side of the platform near a pond called Āykkulam in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: Gift of 4 cows for a lamp to the temple of Kōṇami-uṇḍar, by Arvalanḷan Viḍividaṅgan Śirumaṇḍabai a merchant of Uḷagōṇadēvipuram in Ōymā-nāḍu.

cells.place: On another side of the same platform.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land as a devadāna to the temple of Gōkaraṇamuḍaiya-Mahādēva, by the nagarattār of Uḷagōṇadēvipuram, a city in Ōymā-nāḍu alias Vijayarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the ruined Vishnu temple in the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records grants of lands for offerings and śrībali to the temple of Aḷagiya-Viṇṇagar-Aḷvar in Lōkamahādēvipuram in Pērāyūr-nāḍu, which had been hitherto in precarious years but had been no registered lands. Mentions a tank called Kaḷikaṇṭakappērēri and Gaṇḍarādittappērēri.

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words Svasti-śrī, etc. Records a sale of land by the nagarattār of Uḷa-gamadēvipuram, to a certain Saṭṭan for being presented to the temple of Aḷagiya-Viṇṇagar-Virrirundāḷvar, in order to meet its expenses. The sale-deed was drawn up by Samaṇḍi, of the Āchārya, a worshipper of Sundaraśōlap-perunderuvu.

cells.place: On the south wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Mentions a palace-woman belonging to temple of Aḷagiya-Viṇṇagar-Mummudiśōḷatterinda-tiru-mañjana-nattār-vēḷam.

cells.place: On the wall of Vishnu †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the shrine of Tiru-kailāśam-uḍaiya-Mahādēvar, by the Nagarattār of Uḷagōṇadēvipuram.

cells.place: On a slab set up near a well called Śaṇḍikhiṇaru in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Gift of śattukkappam, a hamlet of Uḷagamadēvipuram, in Mōṅgūrp-puram, for worship and repairs to the temple of Tiruvakki-Iśuvaramuḍaiya-Tambirānar at Vēḷūr, by Nagu-Reddi under the orders of Koṇḍamarasaiyyaṅ Timmaraśaiyar for the merit of Eran-Timmaraśar, the agent of the king.

cells.place: On three sides of a pillar lying in a field called Śaṭṭuppaṭṭa-koḷai, in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Built in. Seems to register a sale of land by the assembly, of Kōṇḍaṅgūru, Ambalavan Gaṇḍarādittan of Kura-jalam in 'Gaṅgaikoṇḍa-śōḷa-vaḷanāḍu' being presented to the temple of Tiruvīraṭṭāṉadēva for śrībali, etc.

cells.place: On the south, east and north walls of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end and incomplete. Mentions Kilinallūr alias Kāraḷantaka-chaturvēdimangalam a brahmādēya in Ōyma-nāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam.

cells.place: On the east wall of Vishnu temple †
cells.remarks: Provides for offerings at Ammāṉāya and Sākkāra-dēvar in the temple of Tiruvagnīśvaramuḍaiyār at Kilinallūr, a brahmādēya in Ōyma-nāḍu, by Parāśaran Tiyag-Saṭṭan, a member of the Alungaṇa of the village.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp to the same temple by a Brāhmaṇa lady.

cells.place: On the north wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. The inscription commences with the words Svasti-śrī and records a gift of sheep by the assembly of Kilinallūr alias Ulaguyyavandachōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Ōyma-nāḍu alias Vijayarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍalam, for offerings to the temple of Tiruvagnīśvaramuḍaiyār-Muḍaiyār-dēva of the village.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of the maṇḍapa in front of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words Svasti-śrī. Records a gift by the assembly of Kāraḷantaka-chaturvēdimangalam to the temple of Tiruvagnīśvaramuḍaiyār-Mahādēva, for the maintenance of a feeding house called Māravadigai.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Records another sale of land by the assembly, for the same purpose.

cells.place: On the east wall of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the assembly of Kilinallūr alias Ulaguyyavandachōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Ōyma-nāḍu alias Vijayarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, made over certain lands in return for the interest on money lent to them from the treasury of Piḍichadavara in the temple of Tiruvagnīśvaram in the same village.

cells.place: On a slab lying in the kitchen of Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that a certain chief Vijaya-rāya-Gāngēya, son of Viruppaya Gāngēya built a sīpōe and repaired three tanks of [Ki]linallūr alias Vaḷidavūr in Vaḷidavūr-nāḍu and endowed them.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine of the Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Records that the assembly of Kilinalūr in Oyma-nādu received 75 kaļaņju of gold from a native of Vaļudavūr in Vaļudavūr-nādu and agreed to feed daily 5 Brahmans.

cells.place: On the wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a kalam by a native of Perumbalamūru-dhir in Sōḷa-nāḍu for convening the assembly of Kili-nallūr, a brahmādēya in Ōyma-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp to the temple of Tigaittil-Viṣṇu-nugriha at Kilinallūr in Ōyma-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 300 sheep for lamps and land for offerings, to the temple of Tigaittil-Viṣṇugriha at Kilinallūr in Ōyma-nāḍu, by Vijaya-Nandivikramavarman who had built it.

cells.place: On the north wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words swasti sri, etc., and stops after mentioning the date of the king.

cells.place: On the wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a gift of land by purchase, by Sāttai Malaiyāl of Vādāppādi, for the annual repairs of a tank.

cells.place: On the wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land and of housesites to certain Vaishnavas, for conducting annual repairs to the temple of Virāminda-Paramai.

cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. The conquests of the king that are noted extend up to Kīlinguu.

cells.place: On the north wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Amappakkam, for worship and repairs, to the temple of Virgirunda-Peruma] at Kilinallōr alias Ulagovyavandaśola-chaturvedimangalam.

cells.place: On the west wall of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that this is the charity of Adittadēvan alias Kālīgarayapār.

cells.place: On the west side of the platform in front of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a vessel by a certain Vedanarayanan.

cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Records that the steps (sōpāna) were made by Dāvakuhu-Pērumāl alias Vāṃṭapādayan of Vijayanikoṇḍi.

cells.place: On the west wall of the prakara of Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple; inside. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for offerings to the temple, for the merit of the king and Timmappa-Nayaka.

cells.place: At the entrance into Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple; left side. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship to the temple of Virgirunda-Peruma] at Kiliyanōr, by Virappa-Nayaka, the agent of Namasśirāya-Nayaka, for the merit of the latter. Below this is an inscription which states that Tēgruvārgađaṇ of Ulandai gave the tiruchobip[na]pichoha: Fragments.

cells.place: On the margin of the platform in the Aiyanar temple in the same village (as Viṣṇu-Vithā-Perumāḷ temple). †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for worship to the temple of Virgirunda-Peruma] at Kiliyanōr, by Virappa-Nayaka, the agent of Namasśirāya-Nayaka, for the merit of the latter. Below this is an inscription which states that Tēgruvārgađaṇ of Ulandai gave the tiruchobip[na]pichoha: Fragments.

cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Apaṇāyudāvara temple at Chhampampǫt-VIII-Vakkam (Madhurantakam taluk).
cells.remarks: Gift of money for a lamp to the temple of Tiruvagattiśūrmudaiya-Nāyanār at Villipakkam alias Gaṅgaikonđaśola-nallōr in Oyma-nađu alias Vijuiyarajēndra-valaṇađu, a subdivision of Jayaṅgondachola-mandalam by a native of Kūvam alias Tyāgasamudranallōr in Manavir-kōṭtam.

cells.place: On the south wall of Agastyisvara temple. †
cells.date: Mithuna, ōn. di. prathamai, Wednesday Praņadi
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions Villi[pa]kkam alias Gaṅgaikonđaśola-nallōr.

cells.place: On the wall of Agastyisvara †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to provide for a festival to the temple at Vīlippākkam. The record is signed by Vīļīppākkan.

cells.place: On a pillar lying in front of the Zamindar's house, at Cauṣampet (same taluk and district).
cells.date: Śka 1424, Dur-mati, Siṃha, śu. di. dvayam, Monday, Srīvapa.
cells.remarks: The inscription reads from bottom upwards. Seems to record a gift of land by purchase for a maṇḍa (P) by Kevuraṇa-Nāyaka, son of Narasappa-Nāyaka to Kaṇādiya resident of Maṇādapadavidu in MaruŎagamanālaṇāru which was situated in Jayangoṇḍa-Tondamaṇāgalam.

cells.place: On the east wall of the Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple at Tribhuvanai (Pondicherry settlements).
cells.remarks: “This temple of Naduvil-Viranārāyaṇa-Vinnagar at Tribhuvanamahadēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Jayaṅgandachōla-maṇdalam, sh-ll be under the protection of the regiments Śri [Vādavūr]-lillaiyalipperumbaḍai and . . . . Pallayiravar of our lord Rajarajadēvar.” Begins with the historical introduction Śṇacchelwar, etc.

cells.place: On the east, north and west walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Registers a gift of land for the temple site, a hall, temple premises and flower-garden, to the god Arulakara-Iśvaramuḍaiyār set up in the 5th year of Vikrama-Chōladēva, by Arumbākkilān Madurāntakaṇ Popnaubalakkūttan alias Porkōyil Tōṇdaimānār residing in Maṇavil in Maṇavil-kōṭtam, a district of Jayaṅgandachōla-maṇdalam, for the prosperity of the king (Perumal) and the village. The gift was made at the command of the great assembly who were attending to the duties of the village of Tribhuvanamadēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya, from the month of Karkaṭaka. The flower garden of (the image of) Pārantakadēva set up in the temple of Rajarajīśvaramuḍaiyār is referred to incidentally. Begins with the historical introduction Śṇacchelwar, etc.

cells.place: On the same walls ..
cells.date: 30th year, Mīna Wednesday, Uttiram. [date-calculation appendix, No. 176: 30th year, Mīna, Wednesday, Uttiram. = Wednesday 2nd March A.D. 1048. In Mīna A.D. 1047-48, which was the 30th year of this reign, nakshatra Uttiram or Uttara-Phalguṇi began on Wednesday 2nd March A.D. 1048 at 13 ghaṭikas after mean sunrise and ended next day at 12 ghaṭikas after sunrise.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for providing a sumptuous offering called after Rajendra-Chōla, to the god Naduvil Śri-Viranārāyaṇa-Vinnagar-Ālyar, by Rajendrasōla-Mavali-Vanarājar under the auspices of the great assembly of Tribhuvanamadēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam which met in the manḍapa built by Sembiyaṇ Umbalanatṭtu-Mūvendaveĵar for the merit of Rajendra-Chōladēva. Tribhuvanamadēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam is herein stated to have been an independent village (taniyūr) in Vilupparaiya-nādu, a subdivision of Rajendrasōla-valaṇaḍu. Begins with the introduction Śṇacchelg, etc.

cells.place: On the north wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: 6th year, Siṁha, ba. di. Ekādaśī, Punarvasu, [Tuesday].
cells.remarks: Much worn out. Begins with the introduction Pugalmādu-vilanga, etc. Registers a gift of land by purchase for worship and offering to the god Kōḷavāra-Aḷvār who is enshrined in the temple of Śrīkōyil. The gold was deposited in the treasury of the temple.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ .. †
cells.date: 9th year, Rishabha, [su]. di. Saptami, Āśēsha, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Pugalmādu-vilanga, etc. Registers a gift of land by purchase, to the god Tiruvayindrapurattu-Aḷvār. Heacin Viḷupparai-nāḍu in Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam was situated, is stated to have been a subdivision of Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: On the north and west walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: 7th year, Mithuna, ba. di. chaturthi Thursday, Aviṭtam.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூமாது ஓங்கிய, etc. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple of Irunayindrapurat-[ta]lvan].

cells.place: On the west wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: 6th year Vrischika, ba. di. trayodasi, Sunday, Svati.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூமாது ஓங்கிய, etc. Registers the order of Pallavaraiyar of Vachchiyur, a commander of the forces (senapati) that nobody except the residentiary Vellalas of Vakkur should levy or pay any kind of dues within the village and that those who do so will be considered to have transgressed the law. This order was engraved while Parum puliyur-Nambi was inspecting the temple business.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 6th year, Mesha ba. di. trayodasi, Hasta, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Registers an order of the assembly altering the classification of the land at Pattur alias Jananathamallur which had been already granted for the merit of Udaiyappiyar Pirantakan Ulagamudaiyar. Refers to the kadai-hi of Villavaraiyar, . . . Mavandavarvelar, the adhikarin who is called 'unne' (amman) and senapati Rajendra- Vayittaranobhojar. Commences with the historical introduction பூமாது ஓங்கிய, etc.

cells.place: On the south wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the king constructed a temple for Harambal (Ganapati) on the banks of the tank at Tribhuvanamadevi. He repaired the embankment, the sluices and the irrigation channels of the tank.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூமாது ஓங்கிய, etc. Gift of land for offerings, worship etc., to the temple of Virasoladevisvaram-udaiya-Mahadevar, the assembly of Tribhuvanamadevi-chaturvedimangalam having been assembled in the temple of Viranarayana-Vinagar-Alvar.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 9th year, Kataka, ba. di. navami Rohini, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Commences with the introduction புகழுமாது விளங், etc. Gift of land free of taxes and two house-sites, for feeding twenty Brahmans with sumptuous meals. The land was called Tribhuvanamadevi alias this village. The great assembly met in the mandapa called Uttama-Chola-Uttamachappariyar-tiramandapam in front of the temple of Srikoyil Vinagar- Alvar.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.king: Rajakesarivarman alias Udaiyar Sri-Rajadra Choladeva (Kulottunga I).
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Commences with the introduction புகழுமாது விளங், etc. Mentions the adhikarin Uttama-Chola Vagavarayar and Kunjaramalla-chaturvedimangalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 9th year, Mitha-na, ba. di. tritiya, Thursday, Pūrat-tādi.
cells.remarks: Begin with the introduction, etc. Re-gisters an order of the great assembly altering the classification of the land which was given to the image of Virrirundālvar in the temple of Srikōyil alias Virana-nārāyanapuram-udaiyār for feeding twenty Brahmans.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction, etc. Gift of land to the Ādittan-Sūryadēvar temple, by Parambali-yūr Nilakanthan Nārāyanan, for feeding Brahmans and altering the classification. Mentions the adhikāri Ahavamalla-Kulantaka-Mūvendavēḷān.

cells.place: On the south and east walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction, etc. States that the village Vayakkūr was a dēvadāna of the temple of Naḍuvil-śiril-Śri-Virarnārāyana-Vinnagar-Ālvār, and some lands in that village were classified into six divisions generally. It was also stipulated that the tenants are not liable to pay any taxes except those due to the god of Naḍuvil-Śirkōyil and to the tank Kōkkilāḍippērēri.

cells.place: On the north side of the base of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction, etc. Land given for worship to the temple of Tiru-Tiruvangadudaiyār and the image of Umādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadaya in Virātāra-valanādu, a sub-division of Gangaikondaśōla-valanādu, was inadequate and that additional lands were given.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Stones displaced. Commences with the introduction, etc.

cells.place: On the north, west and south sides of the same base.
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the same base
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the west side of same base
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep for a lamp.

cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Stones displaced. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple of Virrirunda-Perumal.

cells.place: On the south side of the same base
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction, etc.

cells.place: On a slab built into the floor of the mandapa in front of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a gift of land by purchase, for supplying water and burning a lamp. The tank Kōkkilāḍippērēri figures among the boundaries of the land.

cells.place: On the south wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction, etc. Gift of land, free of taxes, for conducting a festival to the temple of Tirumangaimangaiyār-Paramaśivam.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: 27th year, Kaṭaka-ka, di. dvitiyā, Pushya, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Commences with the same introduction as in No. 197 above. Gift of land to [Pipa]ṛai Tirunārāyaṇa-bhaṭṭan alias Kavikuñjachandra-paṇḍitan of Maṇakulāśanachēri, by the great assembly of Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Rājēndra-Chōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, a sub-division of Gaṅgaikoṇḍa-chōḷa-vaḷanāḍu as a recompense for having composed Kulōttuṅga-Chōḷa-charitai, a kāvya glorifying the king (perumal). The assembly was required to listen to the kāvya as well.

cells.place: On the south, east and north walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones missing and displaced.

cells.place: On the east wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction பூமாதுவளர் etc. Seems to record a gift of land for feeding tapasvins and māhēśvaras.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.date: [28]th year, Mēsha, ba. di. trayōdaśi, Uttirāṭṭādi, Friday.
cells.remarks: Much worn out. Begins with the introduction பூமாதுவளர் etc. Proscribes certain rules regarding the cultivation of lands growing areca-palm.

cells.place: On the east and north walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Commences with the introduction பூமாதுவளர் etc. Gift of land by the assembly of Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam for feeding sampradāyins, during the festival of the temple of Tirumēṅgōyil-Aḷvār, on New-moon days and Vishus and while offerings are made to the Aḷvār of Mērkōyil in the Vēdantavēdamaḍam.

cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Stones missing. Begins with the same introduction. Refers to stones to register gift of land for feeding the śrīvaishṇavas, Śivabrāhmaṇas and Māhēśvaras in the Tirunāvukkarasar-maḍam.

cells.place: On the north wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragments. Begins with the same introduction. Refers to the temple of Toṇ-Tirunēṅgaḍaḷvār at Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that persons who are qualified to do the services of bhaṭṭavṛitti, kiḍai, appu, etc., and who fail to account for the temple lands and other things, and others should take up such services in the village only. Those who engage themselves in these services beyond this village will be considered to have transgressed the law, to have committed a fault against the great assembly and to have ruined the village. Commences with the introduction பூமாதுவளர் etc.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction ᣿ṣeṣṣṣ, etc.

cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Commences with the same introduction. Records that the lands belonging to the temple of Eṇṇāyira-Durgaiyār Oṭṭharuṇḍaiyār, situated in the eastern hamlet of this village with the temple flower-garden and tank, were registered as a village gift to the said goddess under class 12. This land was renamed Bhūpālasundara-vila-gam after demarcating the lands and fixing the boundaries.

cells.place: On the side of the west veranda in the prākāra of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction etc. Records a gift of land to the weavers for supplying certain cloths to the temple. It is said of these weavers that they were the offspring of a Brāhmaṇ with a Vaiśya (woman) and that as authorized by the Āgamas and the king they had the privilege of weaving and supplying cloths to the temple (Dēvar-kōyil-kainkaryam).

cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction etc. The tax-free lands already granted to the temple of Udaiyār Tirunāṇikkul-Mahādēva in Mērka-nāḍu, a sub-division of Virudarājabhayaṅkara-vaḷanāḍu were found insufficient to meet the daily expenses, incense, etc.; and the great assembly made an additional grant of tax-free land in the village of Tirunāṇikkul-nallūr, a hamlet of Iḍaiyāṅguḍi.

cells.place: On the west side of the ruined maṇḍapa opposite Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Commences with the introduction etc. Gift of land as goldsmith's service-man, to a goldsmith named Araṅguṇ. Komāran alias Rājadhirāja-perumaḷaḍaiyār who was required to do the work of a goldsmith for himself and for others within the village and its hamlets.

cells.place: On a stone lying by the side of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.location: TIRUVALLAM, Gudiyattam taluk, North Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the sides of a pillar lying near Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.date: 13th year, Siṃha, ba. di. Monday, ēkādaśi, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: The big men of the assembly decided that the tax-untarayam should be levied on those who cultivated the lands.

cells.place: On fragments lying round the same temple.

cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to record a gift of land to the temple of Gaṅgaivara-nāthar.

cells.place: On a slab lying in Ubhaya-Nāchhiyār shrine †
cells.remarks: Records that the bank of the tank at Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimaṅgalam had breached and that Bhūtaṅgan-gaḷamuḍaiyāṇ Ūrriyūran Bhūpālasundaran alias Sōḷa-kōṇār had it repaired. The stone revetment was constructed by the village assembly and the Araiya-Tirumalaipaḍi-Uḍaiyāṇ alias Malaiyappaiyaṇ, a sub-hamlet of the former. The revetment was called Kuḷōttuṅgāḍu.

cells.place: On the stone slab
cells.remarks: Refers to the same transaction and registers a gift of land by Solakanār for repairing the bank and constructing the stone revetment. The paddy accruing for the repair of the tank was being mixed up with the general dues from the village and the above noted paddy were now given land in Neṫṭāppākkām alias Nityasundaranallūr, a hamlet of Tribhuvanamādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam to the temple of Pallikonda-Perumāl at Tiruvāpadi in Pungūr-nādu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Rajagōpālasvāmin temple at Tirunāppadi (Wandi-vārram, North Arcot district)
cells.remarks: Gift of certain taxes for burning lamps to the temple of Pallikonḍa-Peruma! at Tiruvaypadi in Ponṇār-paṇra.

cells.place: On the north wall of Bhaṇḍāravāṇam temple. †
cells.remarks: Lost in the middle. Gift of land for worship, repairs and festivals to the same temple.

cells.place: On the east, west and south walls of Bhaṇḍāravāṇam temple. †

cells.place: On the west and south walls of Bhaṇḍāravāṇam temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the various festivals in the temple of Palii-konda-Perumal were to be conducted by collecting the dues from the persons who had undertaken to conduct these festivals.

These latter were punished for their misconduct and the four shares were equally distributed for conducting worship, etc., in the shrines of the Ālvār and Nammālvār.

cells.location: Tirumallādi

cells.remarks: Gift of land for supplying sandul-paste and scented powder for bath to the same temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of white chauri by Sundara-Pāṇḍyakōvalarāyan.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Śiva †
cells.remarks: Fixes the taxes to be levied from the ryots residing in the village on the lands cultivated by them.

cells.place: On a pillar by the side of the manḍapa of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: This is the sacred manḍapa of Kuḍiyaraśar Narasingadēvar.

cells.place: On the north wall of the Ganapati shrine in Śiva temple. †
cells.date: Vilambi, Kumbha, ba. di. Friday, Mūla.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village of Kuvākkōji as a hamlet of the village of Sōmanathapura-chaturvēdimaņgalam.

cells.place: On the west wall of Ganapati shrine. †
cells.date: Vilambi, Kumbha, ba. di. navami, Friday, Mūla.
cells.remarks: Records that Vīvēvandara of Periyamadam at Tiruvauṇāmalai made a gift of the village of Erpakkam to the mahājanas of Vaiyāpur alias Sōmanāthapura-chaturvvēdimangalam, an agrahāra in Singalāntapuram, in exchange for Kavakkoli which belonged to him as the mahājanas secured an order of the king assigning the latter an hamlet of Sōmanāthapuram.

cells.place: On the south wall of Ganapati shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land free of taxes to a certain Brahman for conducting the worship in the temples of Vaippūr-Kuvākkōji, the hamlet of Sōmanathapura-chaturvēdimaņgalam. Refers to Timappaṇar brother-in-law (of the king).

cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of Ganapati shrine. †
cells.remarks: Refers to Timmannar (fees) to a certain Brahman for conduct- (Gift of land for offering to the temple of Tirunandappāwi- Uḍaiyār at Avūr in Vāṇagappāḍi on the northern bank of the Pannār at the request of Nallolān Viṇai Attimāllaṇ alias Araiyanarāyanapavēḷār, while Rājārāja Vāṇakovaraiyar was residing at Perambarpalliyūr (i.e., Chidambaram). The letters appear to belong to a later date.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Amman shrine in Ganapati shrine. †
cells.date: Šaka 1871, Pramodūta, Makara, šu. di. dvadaśi, Monday, Svati.
cells.remarks: Gift of land for taxes to Vāṇakovaraiyar by the temple of Tiruvagattīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Avūr.

cells.place: On the west wall of Amman shrine. †
cells.date: Šaka 1405, Sobha-krit. . . . šu. di. saptami, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Middle stone completely peeled off. Seems to record gift of taxes to Vāṇakovaraiyar as araśukāval-vari.

cells.location: Pulahalī (hamlet of Bettamugalām), Krishnagiri taluk, Dharmapuri district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the east wall of Amman shrine †
cells.date: Śaka 1393, Vikṛiti, Āippaḍi 13, brayō-daśī, Monday, Āśvati.
cells.remarks: Built in. Mentions Ammaiyappan agent of the king and the temple of Tiruvāgīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār and Añjanēru-Porumāḷ at Avūr and refers to Oḍḍiyan disturbance.

cells.place: On a boulder in the central shrine of the ruined Viṣṇu temple in the same village (as Amman shrine) †
cells.remarks: Seems to record a gift of dry land to the temple of Karu-māṇikkattāḷvār at Avūr.

cells.place: On a rock in a field at Pujārpatti, hamlet of Ilavampāṭṭi (Omalur taluk, Salem district).
cells.date: Kaliyuga 4756, Śaka 1577, Man-matha, Āni, 10, Paurṇami, Friday, Mala.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Ilavampāṭṭi which was renamed Kailāsanāthapuram for conducting festivals in the temple of Śrīkailāsanātha and Ammai Śivakāmi at Taramangalam, by Immuḍi-kkuḷattū-Muḍaliyār, a member of the community of Vaṇṇaganmuḍi-Muḍaliyārs of the place.

cells.place: On a slab near a Māriyamman temple in the same hamlet (as Viṣṇu temple) †
cells.remarks: Gift of thirty kalanju of gold to the temple of Pulalūr-dēva by a private individual.

cells.place: On the reverse of the slab of Māriyamman †
cells.remarks: Gift of five kalanju of gold to the same god by a private individual.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple at Taramangalam (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: First section of the inscription is very much damaged. Records that certain portions of the temple were reconstructed and that certain images were set up and consecrated by Immuḍi-Muḍaliyār of the Vaṇṇaga-muḍi-Muḍaliyār community.

cells.place: On the north wall of the prakāra of Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.date: Kaliyuga 4780, Siddharthi, Sittirai 10, Monday, saptami, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Records that Kampayya, the son of Sannayya of Mysore, and the agent of the king set up and consecrated the images of Subrahmanya and the Aruvattanūvar in the temple.

cells.place: On a slab on the road-side, 10 miles from Dharmapuri on the Dharmapuri-Krishnagiri road (same district).
cells.remarks: Records that the hamlet of Ponnāri was given by Rājan-naya, a local chief of Irugulūr-nāḍu in Eḍirilichōḷa-maṇḍalam for the temple of Ponnakkūṭṭar.

cells.place: On the top of a hillock called Kuchakal near Pulahalli, a hamlet of Bettamugalam (Hosur taluk and same district).
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.place: On a hero-stone in Bairam-galam (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Mentions that Ammaiyāḷ, son of ... toruvalan, was killed by a tiger in a hunt.

cells.place: On a boulder in a field near a heap of rocks called Nallagutta in the same village (as Kailāsanātha temple). †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.place: On a pillar in the maṇḍapa at the northern entrance into the Mal-lēśvara temple at Bezwada (Bezwada taluk, Kistna district).
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 cows for a perpetual lamp to the god Mallisvara-Mahadēva (of) Bejavada by Malli-Dēsaṭi, son of Proli-Dēsaṭi, of the fourth caste a descendant of Ghadikōta Gunda, lord of Tumbūrn-nāndu and a devotee of the god Joti-Siddhavatēsvara. The boyi that was to supply the daily ghee was granted 1 putti of land.

cells.place: On the pillar of Mal-lēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that a certain setti of the Parvataḷa family made provision for a perpetual lamp in the temple of the same god.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the pillar of Mal-lēśvara †
cells.language: Telugu (verse). †
cells.remarks: Gift of 55 sheep for a perpetual lamp to the same god by Kanṭamma who was the paternal aunt of Nagarjuna, the treasurer (dhanādhyaksha) of Boddana-Nārayaṇa and who set up an image of the goddess Gauri for the god.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the pillar of Mal-lēśvara †
cells.language: Telugu (verse) and Telugu. †
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of 25 cows for a perpetual lamp to the same deity by the Vaiśya Puruva Aṇṇiseṭṭi of Gaṇṭūru who was 'a lord of Pennugoṇḍa' and belonged to the Peṇḍikūla-gōtra.

cells.place: On a pillar near the same entrance.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to an edict set up under the orders of the king by Rāyasam Kondamarusu with reference to the Kondapalli and Kondavidu provinces (rājya).

cells.place: On a mutilated pedestal stone in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions a chief named Bada.

cells.place: On the east face of the Nandi-pillar set up in front of the Mūlasthānēśvara temple at Nādinḍla (Narasaraopet taluk, Guntur district).
cells.remarks: Records the king's provision for a perpetual lamp in the temple of god Śiva at Nādinḍla. The king was the lord of 'Giripraṭṭohi' (i.e., Koṇḍavīḍu-kumāra) which comprised 73 villages.

cells.place: In the place of Mūlasthānēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of sheep by Kauṇḍa [ma]. The wife of Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Vara śrīmārāja to the same temple. See the above number.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|x||18" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. X, No. 18</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.place: On the left door-jamb of the northern entrance into the mukha-maṇḍapa of Mūlasthānēśvara temple. †
cells.language: Telugu (verse and prose) †
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 biruda-gadyas for a perpetual lamp in the same temple by Sūraṇa, wife of Budḍambayi. The five pūjāris of the temple received the money and provided the necessary ghee for the lamp.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|x||17" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. X, No. 17</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.place: On the right door-jamb of Mūlasthānēśvara temple. †
cells.language: Telugu (verse and prose). †
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of 55 sheep made for a perpetual lamp in the temple of the same god by the village-head [Ba]-deya, Nāgari, who was the son of Vellanki-dēva-Nāyaka-Nāyaka-Vāmi-Nāyaka, a Brāhmaṇa of the Mahāghaṭika family and the Bhāradvāja-gōtra. In the damaged verse portion is mentioned Goṅka-Bhūpati.

cells.place: On the south-east pillar in the yaṇa-maṇḍapa of the Trikoṭīśvara temple at Koṭappa-koṇḍa (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the gift of a lamp to the god Trikōtīsvara-Mahādēva of Kavūru by Dandanāyaka Mumma [ha]-Nāyaka of the Chaturtthakula.

cells.place: On the north-west pillar in the place of Trikoṭīśvara. †
cells.remarks: Gift of a perpetual lamp to the same deity by Datyanna-Pregada Sōmana the mudiveli of Mahāmaṇḍalika Bod-daṇa-Nāraya.

cells.place: On a slab set up near a well at Nambūru (Guntur taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Registers the terms of the settlement of the land under the donative-tank (dharma-cheruvu) dug by Kommarāja at Nambūru.

cells.place: To the left of the entrance into the maḍapa before the central shrine in the Śrīkakuḷēśvara temple at Śrīkakuḷam (Divi taluk, Kistna district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a gift of land made for a lamp to the god Śrīvallabha, Śrīkakuḷam by a certain Mālik-Nāyaka.

cells.place: On a pillar in the maṇḍapa in front of the west gōpura of the Bhīmēśvara temple at Drākshārāma (Rāmachandrapuram taluk, Gōdāvari district).
cells.date: 10th year, Makara, di. 6, kri, (i.e., Krehṇa) 7, Thursday, Ākabhaya, Phālguna, ba. 7, Thursday.
cells.remarks: States that the king, while ruling from the throne at Kaṭaka (i.e., Cuttack) having conquered the Gauḍa (country) giving promise of favour to the Gauḍa king, and having performed the paṭṭābhi-shēka and other ceremonies at the temple, (he) granted the village on this marriage in the twenty-seven sthala attached to Rājamahēndravaram.

cells.place: On the upper tier in the east wall of the Bhīmēśvara temple at Bhīmavaram (Cōsanāda taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Incomplete.

cells.place: On the same tier
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records gift of a perpetual lamp to the god Chaḷukya Bhīmēśvara. Mentions Ujāyar śrī-Hājēndra.

cells.place: On a mutilated image lying near the Buddhist ruins in Sālīhuṇḍam (Chicacole taluk, Ganjam district).
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to refer to some kōharyōpādhyāya.

cells.place: On the prabhās of four Buddhist images set up in the same village (as Bhīmēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: All these give the usual Buddhist formula beginning 'Yēdharmmā hētūprabhavā', etc.
Gives a genealogy for five generations from Nandivarman. Records the gift of the village of Vipurambedu free of all taxes to a number of Brahmane.
Gift of the village of Kangara free of all taxes to Brahmans of various gotras. The king calls himself a devotee of Buddha. The grant was issued from Vijay-Kandura-pura.

Registers the gift of 2½ hala of land which was purchased from the residents of the agrahārika village of Hondēvaka in Krōshtūka-vartani as an agrahāra to Jayaśarman of Vatsa-gōtra, a resident of Uramalla (i.e., the modern Urlam). The king is called Rajasingha and Ranābhita.

cells.date: Śaka 1654, Paridhavi, Paṅguni, 8, Tuesday, tritiya, Revati.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land in the village of Gandaradittan for conducting various services, for lamps and flower gardens, to the temple of Tirumalavadi-Nayanar by Sukadovayyan.

cells.date: Śaka 1257, Yuva, Kārttika, 6u. di., 12, Thursday, Manvadi.
cells.remarks: Mutilated at the end. Registers gift of certain lands in the villages of Chinakarti, Bhimavaram, Pulikonda, Mallavaram and Kummarapuri, to Chittamuri Timmana Bhatta. The village of Rametirtham in the Ammanabroli-sima in the Srisaila-Bhumi was also given to the same individual as agrahara.

cells.date: Saka 1296, Nabhaya, Bhadrapada, Purnima, Wednesday, Lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Reddi kings up to Anna-Vema. Records the grant of the village of Pacchani-Tandiparru by the king to the scholar Peddi who was 'the crest jewel among astronomers'.

cells.location: Kāñchipuram (Little), Chingleput taluk, Chingleput district — Tamil Nadu
cells.remarks: Registers the gift, by the king, of the village Rudravaram to a number of Brahmans. The last verse of the inscription says that Śrīnātha, the Vidyādhikāri of king Vēma composed the inscription which ends with the sign-manual of the king 'Śrī Vīranārāyaṇasya'.

The last of a set of plates. The boundaries of the granted village are given in Telugu. Then follows a verse in Sanskrit which says that the king gave to his preceptor Śaṅkara the village called Pinapāḍu and that Śrīnātha-Bhaṭṭāraka composed the inscription.

Damaged. Registers the grant, by the king, of the village Mrōpaṟṟu in Chanū[ṟpa]lli-vishaya to a Brahman called Maṇḍaśarman of the Vatsa-gōtra who was a resident of (the village) Vanapaṟṟu and was well-versed in the Vēdas and the Vēdāṅgas. The donee is stated to have been attached to (bhakta) Maṅgi Yuvarāja.

Records the grant, on the occasion of a Saṅkrānti, of 20 khaṇḍikas of paddy-growing land in the village Jalamūru lying in the Plōlnāṇḍu-vishaya, to a Brahman named Kēśavaśarman of the Ātrēya-gōtra and Hiraṇyakēśi-sūtra. A house-site and a flower-garden were also given to him on this occasion.
Registers the grant of the village Vilemba[li] in Guddāḍi-vishaya to the Brahman Agniśarman of the Vatsa-gōtra by the king for the prosperity of his race.
The plates are much worn away. They record the grant of the village Muronukaḷiki to two pious Brahmans.
Records the grant of the village Kalvavāmulu in the Triliṅga-vishaya and Khaṇḍavāṭa-sthala by the king to the Brahman Peddi-Yajvan of the Harita-gōtra, who was a great astronomer.

cells.date: Śaka 1333, Khara, Mārgaśira, śu. di., trayōdaśī, Dhanus.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Nandamūru in the same vishaya to the same Brahman.

cells.place: On the east side of the 'rock,' Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ temple, Little Conjeeveram, Conjeeveram taluk, Chingleput district.
cells.date: 8th year, Dhanus, śu. di., daśamī, Sunday, Rēvatī.
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle for a perpetual lamp by a native of Malai-maṇḍalam to the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ who was pleased to take his stand in Tiruvattiyūr. Mentions the liquid measure Ariyannavallān-nāḻi.

cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of one-eighth perpetual lamp by Gollappūṇḍi Dēvi-Nāyakkan residing in Śirumanai in Pākka-nāḍu to the same temple. The trustees of the temple took charge of the lamp.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: The first two lines are unfinished. Gift of 33 cattle for a perpetual lamp and a lamp-stand by Piṭṭima Dēvikkāmaiyan, one of the servants of Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichchōḻan Manumasiddharasan Tirukkāḷattidēvan alias Gaṇḍagōpālan to the temple of the Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 135 goats and sheep for 1½ perpetual lamps by Rāma Rāman of Muraṇōttamaṅgalam in Vaḷḷuva-nāḍu, a district of Malai-maṇḍalam to the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: A Sanskrit verse in praise of Tātāchārya, who celebrated 100 marriages every day.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Registers the names of the individuals and the number of lamps which each had to burn in the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ at Tiruvattiyūr in the city of Conjeeveram in Eyiṟ-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gift of 48 sheep for half a lamp to the temple of Āḻvār at Attiyūr in Eyil-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam by Māchaladēvi, daughter of Bhūtteya-Nāyaka of Dōrasamudra.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.date: 15th year Rishabha, ba. di., tritīyā, Friday, Mūla.
cells.remarks: Assignment of certain taxes in Sōmaṅgalam for offerings and repairs in the same temple by Kaḍakkan alias Nīlagaṅgaraiyan.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.date: 7th year, Rishabha, śu. di., dvitīyā, Wednesday, Ārdrā.
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 buffaloes for a perpetual lamp to the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ by Āḻva[n]kō[n], son of Pāṇḍavadūtan Vaḷavadaraiyakōn of Pāttūr. Mentions the liquid measure Arumoḻinaṅgai-nāḻi.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.date: 29th year, Kanya. su. di., pañchami, Thursday, Anurādhā.
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle for a perpetual lamp to the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷ by Kommanappaṅgāru of Mōṭṭuppaḷḷi.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Gift of 44 cows for a perpetual lamp to the same temple by Chandra-śeṭṭi of Maṇḍa[ga]ttali in Nellūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a Vimāna by Tātāchārya at Phaṇipatigiri (i.e.), Tirupati.

cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of 32 cows and one bull for a perpetual lamp to the same temple by Paramēśvaramudaiyān Śilamba-oindān Ambalakkūttan Sēdiyarāyar of Paramēśvara-nallūr, in the Śōḻakulavalli-chaturvēdimangalam

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of 15 Nallūr-naḻai coins for maintaining a perpetual lamp in the same temple by Sevvakkai, sister-in-law of Annaladēvan of Nallūr.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the village of Karaṇai for worship at the service called Gaṇḍagōpāḷan-sandhi, repairs, etc., in the temple of Aruḷāḷa-Perumāḷtiruvattiyūr in Kāñchīpuram-nāḍu in Eyil-kōṭṭam, by the minister Gaṇḍagōpāḷan-mūvēndavēḷān alias Gaṇḍagōpāḷan. The gift was made in the 18th year of Rājarājadēva.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: 21st year, Tula, šu. di., ochaturdaśi, Sunday, Rēvati.
cells.remarks: Gift of cows and bulls for 2 lamps to the same temple by Nulappiyarūlaṇ Narayananambi Damōdaraṇ, one of the Kelvi-Mudalis of Gandagopaladēva.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of cows and a lampstand for a perpetual lamp to the same temple by Mahārajaṇ Kajadēvaṇ, a feudeatory of the king. The chief bears many birudas.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of 10 Bujabalan-maḍai for burning a lamp in the same temple by a native of Puḻai in Poyyāḻi-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle for a lamp by a native of Oraḷachchēri in Veḷḷappa-nāḍu, a district of Maḷai-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.king: Rājarājadēva alias Gaṇḍagōpāḷan †
cells.remarks: Gift of land in Kāvirippakkam alias Vikrama-Chōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Paduvūr-kōṭṭam for festivals, worship at the service called Gaṇḍagōpāḷan-sandhi and repairs, in the temple by Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichōḷan Maṇumādēva in the 16th year of Rājarājadēva alias Gaṇḍagōpāḷan in the Sanskrit verse in characters of Tatayadēśa.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Sanskrit verse in praise of Tātayadēśika.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by Tikki-Nāyakkhar, brother of Padiyāri-Rāyappa-Nāyakkhan the Mahāpradhāna of Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichōḷan who is called pūlliyār of Nallūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: 1[9]th year, Kanyā, šu. di., Thursday, pañchami, Viśakha.
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 sheep and a ram for a lamp to the same temple by Arūnagiri-Perumaļ, one of the sons of Pañchanadivāna Nilagaṅgaraiyar who is call-d pilļaiyar (son).

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: 22nd year, Mina, ba. di., triti[ya], Śriday, Svnti.
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle and a lampstand for a perpetual lamp to the same temple by Vallaiya-Dandanayaka, son of Dodapilļai-Dandanayaka of Aranaipuram, one of the ministers of Hoysaļa Vira-Sōmēśvaradēvarnas.

cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: Śaka 1154, 16th year, Makara, su. di., prathama, Friday, Śravana.
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle and one lampstand for a lamp to the same temple by Kāmi Nāyakan, one of the mudalis of Madu-rāntaka Poṭṭapi chōḷa Tirukkalatti-dēva Gaṇḍagōpāla The latter is called piḷḷaiyār (son).

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: 23rd year, Makara, su. di., shashṭhi, Saturday, īēvati.
cells.remarks: Gift of 33 cattle for a lamp to the same temple by Vellapapagāda Kan[pi]rakōdu Gandan Iraman alias Purushamanikka-seṭhi.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the same side
cells.date: 20th year, Mina, ba. di., trittya, Friday, Svati.
cells.remarks: Gift of 11 cows for providing milk at the midnight service by Polalvi-Dandanayakan, one of the ministers of Hoysala Vira-Sōmēśvaradevurasa.

cells.place: Chōla
cells.remarks: Gift of 1,750 Nellūr-padi-mādu coins for purchase of land for offerings by a merchant of Karaiyappalli in Malai-mandalam.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of village of Udayākkāmam in Anta-ura-viśaya by Sōmādēvi Mahādēvi for daily worship and offerings to the god. It also mentions Sēndamangalam-uḍaiyār who seems to have belonged to the Vāṇa family or one of his birudas. He is stated to have camped at Abhinavavāraṇavāsi (perhaps Conjeeve-ram).

cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 128 cows and 4 bulls by Kalingesvara-Aniyanga Bhimadeva Rahutta for four perpetual lamps in the temple.

cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of Gaṇdagopala and records the gift of a number of villages for conducting the festivals in the months of Ādi and Puratṭadi, the service called by Gaṇdagopalan-sandi and repairs by Madhurantaka Pottappicholojai; Manumaśiddarasai; Tirukkalattidevan alias Gaṇdagopalan.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.date: Śaka 1480, Kalayukti, Karkaṭaka, ba. di., saptami, Thursday, Revati.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by Ajagiyamapavala Jiyar mentioned in No. 443 above for offerings. Mentions the shrine of Toṇdaradippodi-Ālyar and Pratapadevarajendrupuram alias Etirajapuram.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.date: Śaka 1482, Randri, Tula, śu. • Āi., saptami, Friday, Sravama.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land for offerings by the same individual. Mentions the Aḷagiyasingar and Tiruppā-gaḷvar.

cells.place: On the west and north walls of the rock of Arulala-Perumal. †
cells.date: Śaka 1452, Vikriti, Karkaṭaka, śu. di., navami, Viśakha, Monday.
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for offering cakes during festival days by Kaṭakēśvara-Lakshmaṇa[mman], a disciple of Śata-kōpa-jīyar. It is stated at Urukkāṭṭu-kōṭṭam in which Kāñchīpuram was situated is said to have belonged to Chandragiri-rājya.

cells.place: On the north wall of the rock of Arulala-Perumal. †
cells.date: 1[1]th year, Karkaṭaka, śu. di., pañchami, Monday, Uttara-Phalguni.
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by a Nāyaka of the Malai-maṇdalam.

cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp and a lamp-stand to the same temple by Eraṇiyakka Muṇaiyalan of Kāriy-yalli in Maḷi-maṇḍa-lam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 32 cows and one bull for a lamp to the same temple by a native of Aiñjūrmullaippadi in Seṅgunpra-nadu, a subdivision of Kalattūr-kōṭtam, a district of Jayangonda-60ja-maṇdalam.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 15 Bhujabala-Aṇṇamangalam-māḍai (coin) for a lamp by Pōśāḷi Reḍḍi of Śavukanśeruvaru in Muṇḍa-nāḍu, a subdivision of Nellūr-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the north wall of the rock of Arulala-Perumal. †
cells.king: Rājarājadēva †
cells.remarks: Gift of the villages of Avuḍaiyār-kōṭṭam alias Aravarttapuram-chaturvēdimangalam and Akkarai-kōṭṭam in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu-kōṭṭam for conducting the service called Gaṇḍagōpālan-sandhi and for festivals in the temple by Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichōḻan Manumasiddharaiyar alias Gaṇḍagōpāla in the 18th year of Rājarājadēva. It is also stated at the end that in the 14 + 1st year of Perumāḷ Sundara-Pāṇḍyadēva, the village Akkarai-kōṭṭam was exclusively assigned for the benefit of the service.

cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †

cells.remarks: Gift of 132 sheep for a lamp to the same temple by Siḍḍappa-Nāyaka Būruppa-Nāyaka of Viṇṇamallai in Paṭṭai-nāḍu of Vīmarasar Tyāgasamudra of Tyāgasamudrapaṭṭaṇa, one of the ūḍaiyārs of Gaṇḍagōpāladēva.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 96 sheep for a lamp by Paḍḍanārsar, son of Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichōḻan Nallanāḍāḻvān to the same temple.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 71 sheep, 31 goats and one ram for a lamp by a native of Segalur in the Nellore district.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of 32 cows, 1 bull and a lamp-stand for burning a lamp in the same temple by a native of Urukkāḍu in Urukkāṭṭu-kōṭṭam.

cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Paiyiyūr alias Rājakēsari-chaturvēdimangalam in Amūr-kōṭṭam for conducting the service called Gaṇḍagōpālan-sandhi, for festivals and repairs by Madurāntaka Poṭṭappichōḻan Manumasiddharaiyar Tiruk-kaḷattidēvan alias Gaṇḍagōpāla in the 17th year of Rājarājadēva.

cells.location: Tirumallādi
cells.place: On the wall of Arulala-Perumal †
cells.remarks: Verse in praise of Rājarājadēva.

cells.location: Tirumallādi

cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Kuṇḍiyūr, uttaramdam in Kaḷiyūr-kōṭṭam. The object of the grant and the donor are the same as in No. 362 above. Quotes the 16th year of Rājarājadēva.

cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Kuṇḍiyūr, uttaramdam in Kaḷiyūr-kōṭṭam. The object of the grant and the donor are the same as in No. 362 above. Quotes the 16th year of Rājarājadēva.

cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Vayalai[ka]?vūr in Eyil-kōṭṭam. Do. Quotes the 15th year of Rajarajadēva.
